groups.title: Troupe play and sagas
groups.intro: Troupe-style play, saga setup, styles, speed and house rules.

entries.title: Saga Background: History
entries.summary: The troupe decides how closely the saga follows real history, how much mundane interaction there is, and whether magi can change history after the canonical start date.
quotes: The troupe must simply decide whether the magi can change history.

entries.title: Saga Background: The Order of Hermes
entries.summary: The troupe decides how organized and intrusive the Order is in practice, from strict registration and enforcement to loose social Tribunals, which changes how much politics the saga contains.
quotes: How organized is the Order in practice?

entries.title: Rules Questions (House Rules)
entries.summary: Advice on when the Laboratory and Long-Term Event rules matter and on adopting house rules, with examples such as using only simple dice, adding trade rules, giving mundane believers a Magic Resistance, or dropping statistics altogether.
quotes: you can simply ignore stress dice, and always use a simple die
You might decide to give all Christians, Jews, and Muslims a Magic Resistance equal to five times the level of the local Dominion aura.

entries.title: Saga Background: The Church
entries.summary: Choices for portraying the Church in a saga: basically good or basically evil, and whether it treats magic as sinful or as a God-given gift.
quotes: The fundamental choice is between a Church which is basically good with a few bad members, is basically evil, with a few good members.

entries.title: Saga Background: The Fate of Magic
entries.summary: Options for whether magic is declining, rising or steady in a saga, including linking decline to the advance of the Dominion or to all supernatural realms together.
quotes: In your saga, magic could be declining, rising, or steady.

entries.title: Resources (Vis and Books Guidelines)
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on how much vis and how many books to give the player characters, with Low, Moderate and High vis supply levels per magus per year and advice on handing out vis finds before vis sources.
quotes: Up to 5 pawns/magus/year.
Around 10 pawns/magus/year.
Around 20 pawns/magus/year.

entries.title: Saga Speed
entries.summary: Introduces saga speed, the number of game seasons that pass per session, as a key choice that sets the style of a saga and can be changed later.
quotes: the number of seasons of game time that pass for every game session is an extremely important factor in determining the style of a saga

entries.title: Slow Saga
entries.summary: A saga with two or more sessions per season: characters barely improve and lifespans hardly matter, laboratory rules see little use, and Virtues and Flaws affecting starting scores matter more than those affecting study or lifespan.
quotes: In a slow saga there are, on average, two or more game sessions per season.

entries.title: Medium Saga
entries.summary: A saga with one to four seasons per session: a good compromise and starting rate in which characters improve, companions and grogs may eventually die of old age, and study-related Flaws weigh about as much as starting-score ones.
quotes: A medium saga has, on average, one to four seasons per game session.

entries.title: Fast Saga
entries.summary: A saga where more than a year passes per session: magi grow powerful quickly and may die of old age within it, companions are played only a few times, and Virtues and Flaws affecting only starting scores lose importance.
quotes: In a fast saga, more than one year passes per game session, on average.

entries.title: Pulsed Saga
entries.summary: A saga alternating bursts of intense play over a short span with long gaps of years, giving companions and grogs play time while magi advance during the downtime, at the cost of needing an in-game reason for the quiet periods.
quotes: A dozen game sessions might cover a single season, but then twelve game years might pass before the next session.

entries.title: Troupe-Style Roleplaying
entries.summary: Explains why troupe-style play, in which players have several characters and the storyguide role can be shared, suits Ars Magica better than conventional single-character play given how different magi, companions and grogs are.
quotes: it is almost always better to use some version of troupe-style play rather than conventional play

entries.title: Alternative Characters (Troupe Style)
entries.summary: Each player has two or more characters, at least one a magus and one a companion, but plays only one per session, so the characters need good reasons not to adventure together.
quotes: In this version of troupe-style play each player has two or more characters, but only plays one of them in a given session.

entries.title: Pooled Characters (Troupe Style)
entries.summary: A shared pool of grogs and bit-part characters that any player can run, each looked after between sessions by a single player; keeps magi few, lets grogs die safely, and handles player absences because advancement does not depend on being played.
quotes: in addition to a player's magi and companions, there is also a 'pool' of grogs and bit-parts, who can be played by anyone.

entries.title: Guest Storyguiding
entries.summary: A player occasionally runs a session while the regular storyguide plays pooled grogs; best used for isolated stories such as a distant island or a regio, agreeing in advance on rewards and risks.
quotes: The next level of troupe-style playing involves a player occasionally running a session.

entries.title: Alpha and Beta Storyguides
entries.summary: Several people storyguide regularly: an alpha storyguide with veto power over the saga's overall shape and beta storyguides each responsible for a location or aspect, who must agree on reward level and tone.
quotes: One storyguide, the alpha storyguide, is responsible for the overall shape of the saga, and has final veto power on story additions

entries.title: Pure Troupe Style
entries.summary: Everyone storyguides in roughly equal amounts with no alpha storyguide, requiring an agreed method, such as a rules storyguide, for resolving rules disputes.
quotes: In the purest form of troupe style, everyone runs games in roughly equal amounts, and there is no alpha storyguide.

entries.title: Researching a Setting
entries.summary: Describes levels of historical research a storyguide can put into a saga, from a pure fantasy world and no-research through low, medium, high and extreme research, with practical steps for each.
quotes: There are a number of options for this, and none is better or worse than the others.

entries.title: Saga Styles
entries.summary: Seven compatible styles of saga to choose or combine: high fantasy, mundane interactions, Hermetic life, action-adventure, investigation, politics and creation.
quotes: all valid, and many compatible with each other

entries.title: Saga Priorities
entries.summary: Puts player enjoyment first: talk through content that upsets players, let players adapt characters to the stories they like, and treat game balance only as a tool for sharing the spotlight when changing rules.
quotes: The highest priority for any saga is to ensure that all the players are having fun.
As long as the changes help everyone to have fun, they are good.

entries.title: Horror stories for grogs
entries.summary: Advice for running horror, which leans on Personality Traits such as Brave and can represent madness as temporarily imposed high Personality Traits that govern reactions to certain stimuli.
quotes: Horror stories make extensive use of Personality Traits (particularly the Brave Trait)

entries.title: Antagonists for grog stories
entries.summary: Guidance on choosing antagonists for grog-only stories, noting that grogs lack Magic Resistance so even weak supernatural powers threaten them, how a Brave roll can decide whether a band stands against a fear power, and how to keep a trained group from defeating the antagonist too early.
quotes: Grogs have no Magic Resistance at all

entries.title: Rewards for grog stories
entries.summary: Grogs earn experience like other characters but seldom gain vis or items, so the storyguide can reward success with experience in a Reputation among the covenfolk, favors, mentoring, an agency, or personalized equipment.
quotes: Grogs earn experience points at the same rate as any other character

entries.title: All-Grog Sagas
entries.summary: Introduces sagas in which players run only grogs while magi are storyguide characters, and suggests running a grog saga in parallel with a standard saga, possibly with an alternative storyguide.
quotes: One saga deals with the actions of the magi, the other the consequences that those actions have on the turb

entries.title: A Noble Saga
entries.summary: Describes a saga built on a noble household where the lord and a few select staff are companions and everyone else, including his sons of age, are grogs because they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.
quotes: Even the baron's sons who have reached their majority could be considered grog characters, since they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.

entries.title: A Redcap Saga
entries.summary: Explains that the Redcap Virtue is normally unavailable to grogs because it is a Major Social Status Virtue, and offers two fixes: make it a free Virtue for all characters or have the player characters work for redcaps instead.
quotes: allow the Redcap Virtue as a free Virtue

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages ch.3

entries.title: Variable Outcomes
entries.summary: Storyguide guidance to give every story at least success, neutral and failure outcomes, to avoid disastrous consequences for failure, and to prefer setbacks like lost possessions or lost study time over character or covenant destruction.
quotes: You should have at least three possible outcomes for any story: one corresponding to success, another to a neutral performance, and one to failure.

entries.title: Story Types (Reactive, Proactive, Soap Opera)
entries.summary: Divides stories into reactive, proactive and soap opera types and explains how each works as the magi grow more powerful, since powerful magi short-circuit reactive and investigative plots.
quotes: this discussion divides stories into three types: reactive, where something happens and the player characters respond

groups.title: Mythic Europe
groups.intro: Mythic Europe in the core rules and making it historical.

entries.title: Un-Fun History (Adjusting the Setting)
entries.summary: Guidance for troupes who dislike parts of medieval society: they may gloss over or remove unpalatable features, play the oppressed, or lean on the Order of Hermes as a tolerant home base.
quotes: The Order of Hermes is deliberately designed to be anachronistic and fundamentally tolerant

entries.title: Mythic Options: The Nobility
entries.summary: Optional ways to put more magic into the nobility, such as faerie lords, supernatural noble lines, magical rulers or enchanted items of succession, to be used as much or as little as the troupe wants.
quotes: If you want to keep medieval society fairly mundane, you shouldn't use any of them.

entries.title: Mythic Options: Towns and Trade
entries.summary: Optional ways to make towns more magical, such as faerie towns, supernatural traders, or a town that is a living being aligned to a realm.
quotes: A town might be alive as a whole, and aligned to any realm.

groups.title: Converting from Fourth Edition
groups.intro: Bringing Fourth Edition characters into Fifth.

entries.title: Converting Characters from Fourth Edition The Mysteries
entries.summary: Notes for converting Fourth Edition Mysteries characters: Abilities, Virtues and Flaws, Mastery, Mystae magics and the new Revised Edition schools.
quotes: Mastery Virtues are replaced by Mastery special abilities; see ArM5, page 87.
adding one Mastery Level for each Ability added

entries.title: Fourth Edition Conversion: What Changed
entries.summary: A summary of the main rule changes from Fourth to Fifth Edition in character generation, covenants, magic, long-term events and combat, useful when updating old material or house rules.
quotes: Spell level is now subtracted from the casting total before determining Penetration.
Abilities now cost five times their (level + 1) to raise by one level.
First, Virtues and Flaws no longer have point values; they are split into Major and Minor.

entries.title: Fourth Edition Character Conversion
entries.summary: Rule-of-thumb steps for converting a Fourth Edition character: adjust age, keep Characteristics, convert Virtues and Flaws, rescale Ability experience, replace uncastable spells and turn Twilight Points into a Warping Score.
quotes: add 20% to a Fourth Edition character's age
Abilities: Leave at the old value, and multiply remaining XP by five.
Divide the number of Twilight Points by three, and use this as the Warping Score.

groups.title: The Rhine Tribunal
groups.intro: Rules particular to the Rhine Tribunal (Guardians of the Forests).

entries.title: Retired Magi and Proxy Voting Sigils
entries.summary: Describes how the Rhine Tribunal treats magi lost to Twilight as retired rather than dead, and how their voting sigils may be held by proxy by magisters and archmagi, with the number strictly limited by rank.
quotes: a magus whom no other has witnessed for a period of two Tribunals or more shall be deemed to be retired
a magister may hold only one such sigil, an archmagus at most two

entries.title: Founding a Covenant in the Rhine Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains the Rhine Tribunal's rule that a new covenant needs the approval of every existing covenant before it is recognized, the consequences of lacking recognition, the bargaining and gift-giving that follow, and the sidebar ruling that requires a sponsor from each covenant.
quotes: prospective covenants have been required to obtain the explicit permission of all the Tribunal's other covenants, in order to obtain recognition
If a covenant is not successful in getting approval from the Tribunal, they may try again in seven years time.

entries.title: The Guardians of the Forests Ruling
entries.summary: The Rhine Tribunal's Peripheral Code ruling that obliges magi to protect forests, vis sources and auras from the encroachment of mundane settlement and the Dominion, its later clause limiting action that would anger mundanes, and how inconsistently it is enforced.
quotes: We must take care to only act in such a fashion so as not to incur the wrath of the mundanes
We must become Guardians of the Forests, for none will halt this decline if we do not.

entries.title: Rhine Tribunal Ranks
entries.summary: Introduces the four ranks by which the Rhine Tribunal classes its magi: apprentice, journeyman, master and archmage.
quotes: The Rhine Tribunal has four recognized ranks by which it classes its members.

entries.title: Laws of Hospitality and the Peregrinatores
entries.summary: The Peripheral Code ruling that lets any magus request hospitality from a Rhine covenant for a fixed span of years in return for vis or service, setting out the duties of guest and host and how many magi travel as peregrinatores.
quotes: guarantee him at least three, but no more than seven years at the covenant
a fee of three pawns of vis per year paid to the host

entries.title: Rhine Apprenticeship and Durenmar Training
entries.summary: Describes the legal status of a Rhine apprentice and the Peripheral Code requirement that every apprentice trained in the Tribunal spend time at Durenmar, including the optional induction into a political gild.
quotes: must spend a minimum of one season learning at Durenmar, to complement their normal studies

entries.title: Rhine Journeyman Rank
entries.summary: Explains how a magus becomes a journeyman (tyro) at Durenmar after the Gauntlet, receiving a voting sigil and the option to declare for a gild, and the choices of founding a covenant, joining one, or wandering as a peregrinator.
quotes: The magus is now legally a journeyman, and he may declare membership of a gild, if he wishes.

related.text: Laws of Hospitality and the Peregrinatores

entries.title: Earning the Rank of Master
entries.summary: How a Rhine magus becomes a magister: three masters of different covenants, Houses and gilds must each give a token of approval, and the candidate needs a reputation for magical prowess (or loyal service for Redcaps). Masters may take apprentices, hold one retired magus's sigil, and outrank lower ranks in disputes that could be settled by certamen.
quotes: The rank can only be conferred at the discretion of three magi who are masters themselves.
Once three of these tokens are collected, the new master may immediately style himself magister
One must achieve the status of master before being allowed to take an apprentice.
a higher-ranked magus automatically has priority

entries.title: Rhine Tribunal Gatherings
entries.summary: States when and where the Rhine Tribunal meets and how the gathering and the gild meetings before it are timed.
quotes: Meetings of the Rhine Tribunal are held every seven years and by tradition always take place at Durenmar.

entries.title: Voting in the Rhine Tribunal
entries.summary: Describes how voting sigils work at the Rhine Tribunal, with masters and archmagi receiving proxy sigils of retired magi at a ceremony, and the political effect this has on covenants and younger magi.
quotes: Upon achieving promotion to the rank of master, a magus is formally entrusted with the sigil of a retired (Twilight) Rhine magus, to wield by proxy.

related.text: Retired Magi and Proxy Voting Sigils

entries.title: The Gild System
entries.summary: Explains how the Rhine Tribunal's political gilds work: joining is open and public, members are expected to vote with the gild, gild members can call on each other for help and are protected from Wizard War by their fellows, and leaving or being expelled carries a social price.
quotes: Nevertheless, the Oath of Hermes forbids any mechanism to coerce a magus to vote in a particular way
All gilds forbid Wizard War among their members
Those that do not do so within seven years of their Gauntlet or their arrival in the Tribunal generally acquire a reputation as a loner.

entries.title: The Lineage of Irmele
entries.summary: Describes a wandering Bonisagus lineage in the Rhine whose members travel as peregrinatores, tend to weather magic, are strong in Arts and rich in vis, and often rely on spontaneous magic for lack of a laboratory.
quotes: Once they achieve the status of master, they will, unlike others, typically remain a peregrinator for a couple of decades

related.text: Laws of Hospitality and the Peregrinatores

entries.title: Earning the Rank of Archmage
entries.requires: Rank: Master (Rhine magus), 7th magnitude spell, great deed, successful archmage challenge
entries.summary: Sets out the requirements for archmagehood, including the challenge each archmage sets, the limits on challenging and granting the title, and the Rhine privileges of archmagi (extra proxy sigils and automatic victory in disputes against lower ranks).
quotes: they are permitted to hold the voting sigils of two retired magi
no archmage may grant the title to more than seven magi
a magus must have invented a spell of at least 7th magnitude

entries.title: The Mercere Portals
entries.requires: Mercere Portal access (Durenmar or other linked covenant)
entries.summary: Explains that Mercere Portals are permanent paired gateways with the effect of the ritual Hermes Portal, how Durenmar's are used and what visitors pay, and advises the storyguide how freely to allow long-range instant travel.
quotes: Each single Portal may only connect to one other, its matching pair.
all others are obliged to pay a fee of two pawns of vis each

entries.title: The Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains that unlike other Tribunals, where the oldest magus presides, the Rhine Tribunal's Praeco is by tradition the Primus of House Bonisagus.
quotes: but instead is always the Primus of House Bonisagus, who wields Bonisagus's voting sigil by proxy

entries.title: The Oak Gild (Eichengilde)
entries.summary: The largest and oldest Rhine gild, devoted to tradition, respect for the Founders and elders, and shunning outside wisdom, and led by the Prima of Bonisagus.

entries.title: The Hawthorn Gild (Weissdorngilde)
entries.summary: The smallest and one of the oldest Rhine gilds, which seeks to protect wild places and creatures from mundanes and is dominated by Bjornaer Wilderists.

entries.title: The Ash Gild (Eschengilde)
entries.summary: An aggressive, magically powerful gild favoring dominion over the magi's lands and open dealing with mundanes, with a hidden focus on combating the Order of Odin.

entries.title: The Elder Gild (Holundergilde)
entries.summary: A gild, largely of Merinita magi, devoted to preserving the fae and promoting friendly contact between magi and faeries.

entries.title: The Linden Gild (Lindengilde)
entries.summary: A small, altruistic go-between gild founded after the Schism War to build trust and peaceful resolution between magi and covenants.

entries.title: The Apple Gild (Apfelgilde)
entries.summary: The newest and weakest Rhine gild, advocating peaceful relations with and acceptance in the mundane world.

entries.title: Gild Alliances and Tribunal Politics
entries.summary: Describes which Rhine gilds ally with or oppose each other and the main fault line between wilderness-minded and mundane-minded magi.

entries.title: Wood Properties: The Trees of Germany
entries.summary: Lists Shape and Material bonuses for the woods of the common German trees for enchanting items, and notes that enchanting an entire living tree multiplies the bonus.
quotes: If an entire living tree is enchanted, any such bonuses are tripled.

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonuses

entries.title: Fates of the Forest Spirits
entries.summary: Explains the four fates (survival, dissolution, replacement, alliance) of the genii loci that fragmented from the original Hercynian Forest spirit, and how each produces magical, mundane, faerie, divine or infernal forests.

entries.title: Forest Types by Realm
entries.summary: Short descriptions of how a forest looks and behaves when it lies in the Magic, Faerie, Divine or Infernal realm, as guidance for the storyguide.

entries.title: Forest Spirit General Powers
entries.summary: Rules for a forest's Might score and the three powers every forest spirit has: Presence, Manifestation (controlling animals or growing plants) and Produce Vis.
quotes: but all forests have a Might of at least 30
For a cost of 5 points of Might, a single Size 0 creature (or an equivalent mass of smaller creatures) can be controlled.
a yearly harvest of vis, of a number of pawns up to the Might score

entries.title: Forest Spirit Specific Powers
entries.summary: A catalogue of optional powers a forest spirit can buy with Might (weather control, granting Virtues and Flaws, victory, guidance, healing, possession, oath-enforcement, regiones, shrouding and stasis), with costs, initiative and Forms, and a note that spirits have only Might, Personality Traits and powers.
quotes: 5 points for Minor Flaw, 10 points for Major Flaw, Init 0, Vim
A supernatural power requires 1 Might point per magnitude to produce, in addition to the Might cost (if any) to the possessed.
10 points per level, Init 0

entries.title: The Passage of the Seasons (Might Pools by Month)
entries.summary: A month-by-month record of the Might Pools and faerie auras of the four seasonal courts as they struggle through the year, for the storyguide to track.
quotes: King Holly (Might Pool 35) slays King Oak (Might Pool 15)

entries.title: The Courts of the Seasons
entries.summary: Describes four linked faerie forests ruled by seasonal lords, with Might, traits and powers, and the rule by which each ruler's Might Pool and aura rise and fall through the year.
quotes: Throughout the year they retain a Might Score of 30, used for Magic Resistance and Penetration
Every month following the height of their power, they lose 5 Might points to their opposing court

entries.title: Divine Auras of German Churches
entries.summary: Gives the strengths of Divine auras for the great cathedrals, other cathedrals and ordinary cities in Germany and notes where Divine auras are generally strongest and weakest.
quotes: The cathedral of Mainz, as the seat of a Holy See, has a Divine aura of 7
most cities have a Divine aura of 3

entries.title: The Rhinefalls: Aura, Regio and Vis
entries.summary: Describes the Rhinefalls island's Magic aura, the rolls needed to land on and climb the rock, the way to harvest Aquam vis by sacrificing goods to the river spirit, and the regio that rises with the rock.
quotes: Profession: Boating roll against an Ease Factor of 9
Athletics roll against an Ease Factor of 12
Each is worth one pawn of Aquam vis.

entries.title: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls (regio)
entries.requires: Storyguide-placed site in the Black Forest (never found)
entries.summary: A forest-spirit regio whose levels are the seven waterfalls; a visitor may only ascend each level by completing a different Quest, gaining a new level of understanding of the Forest at each step. Gives the spirit's Might, traits and powers as a stat block.
quotes: Magic Might: 50
Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker), Guide, Oath-Swearing, Regio, Shroud

related.text: Realms and Forest Paths in the Rhine Tribunal

entries.title: Durenmar guest laboratories and vis fees
entries.summary: Describes the fee in vis a covenant may charge a visiting magus of suitable rank for a season in its guest laboratories, with a cheaper rate for the small standard labs; a model for pricing guest lab use.
quotes: albeit with a charge of at least five pawns of vis
for the lesser fee of two pawns of vis per season each

entries.title: Studying in the Great Library (Durenmar)
entries.requires: Visit to Durenmar (members and House Bonisagus exempt)
entries.summary: Visiting magi earn seasons of study credit at the Great Library by contributing tomes, new spells or a season of copying, or by paying vis; rules cover priority when two magi want the same tome, certamen to settle disputes, and limits on removing or copying books.
quotes: For each new contribution to the Great Library, a magus is permitted to study freely there for two seasons.
a magus may instead gain a single season of credit by volunteering for a season of copying

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bonisagus)

entries.title: Searching the Great Library: lab notes, spells, tractatus and summae
entries.summary: Floor-by-floor procedures for finding a desired item in the Great Library: Intelligence + Magic Theory to locate lab notes, a stress die against an Ease Factor to find a Lab Text, and simple-die rolls (with Durenmar Lore and rank bonuses) to find tractatus and summae and to set their Quality.
quotes: The success should be determined by an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against an appropriate Ease Factor.
The Ease Factor for standard spells is 3, or 6 for a specific version of a general-level standard spell up to level 40.
To determine the Quality of a studied tractatus, roll a simple die and add 2.
To determine whether a summa of a specified Art is available to a magus, roll a simple die and add 10.

entries.title: Durenmar covenfolk: Warping from the strong Magic aura
entries.requires: Covenfolk of Durenmar (covenant in a strong Magic aura)
entries.summary: Durenmar's servants and grogs are shaped by life in a strong Magic aura: each has Warping-derived Minor Flaws, and the very old gain a Supernatural Ability Virtue. A model for generating covenfolk of any covenant that lives in a strong aura.
quotes: All covenfolk have at least one Minor Flaw due to Warping, and those over 30 years old have two.

entries.title: The Fane of the Founders
entries.summary: A hidden glade with a Magic aura in which twelve magi renew the Oath of the Founders every seven years; the stone is treated as an artifact with Magic Might and a limited set of forest powers, and it yields vis to those who perform the rite.
quotes: Thus, the Fane may be treated as if it has a Magic Might of 40
Produce Vis, Shroud, Oath-Swearing, Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker; temporarily)

related.text: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls

entries.title: The Source of the Danube (Faerie regio)
entries.requires: Storyguide-placed site in the eastern Black Forest
entries.summary: An enchanted spring and bottomless pool with a Faerie aura that rises within the water and in the deeper levels of a regio, ending in a gateway to Arcadia; large amounts of Aquam vis can be harvested at the cost of angering the river spirit.
quotes: There is a Faerie aura of 3 in the region of the pool, which rises to 5 if one is within the water itself.

entries.title: The Rottweiler (playable dog grog)
entries.requires: Storyguide approval; a magus who keeps Rottweilers
entries.summary: Optional rules for playing a faerie-blooded hunting dog as a grog: it uses Cunning in place of Intelligence, receives a fixed package of Virtues and Flaws, and has its age and aging rolls scaled to dog years. Some have faerie blood that slows aging or grants Second Sight.
quotes: the hound may be created as a normal character, except that it has Cunning instead of Intelligence
Their bite has the same combat statistics as a dagger.
Calculate their age (and experience) as for a human, and use this age for making aging rolls

entries.title: The Magestones of Verditius (portable Magic aura)
entries.requires: Possession of a magestone (Durenmar and Oculus Septentrionalis hold them)
entries.summary: Rare Creo Vim artifacts that each project a small Magic aura, allowing a covenant with no natural aura to give its magi lab work in a Magic aura for a limited number of seasons a year; Hermetic theory cannot replicate them.
quotes: Each stone manifests a Magic aura of 3, large enough to cover a large room or laboratory.
so that they are able to work in a Magic aura in their labs for up to two seasons every year

entries.title: The Holy Vehm (secret courts of northern Germany)
entries.summary: Describes how the secret Vehmic courts try capital crimes: who may be a member and who is exempt, the officials, how a summons works, and how many witnesses are needed for proof or acquittal. Useful for running a Vehm trial or hunt against suspected hedge wizards.
quotes: his accuser can present to the court seven witnesses to his own character as a man to be trusted
he requires twenty-one witnesses in favor of innocence to assure his acquittal

related.text: Order of Hermes and mundane law

entries.title: The Brocken: Faerie aura that doubles on Walpurgis Night
entries.requires: Visit to the Brocken in the Harz
entries.summary: A potent supernatural mountain where the Faerie aura varies by altitude and doubles on Walpurgis Night; also a source of a vis plant, a vision-granting spring and a place to find potential apprentices.
quotes: The lower slopes of the Brocken have a Faerie aura of 2, with 4 at the summit. These values are doubled on Walpurgis Night.

entries.title: Fengheld's Chapter Houses (covenant chapter rules)
entries.requires: A covenant that has founded chapter houses
entries.summary: Explains how a covenant can be spread over several sites as chapter houses: all chapters remain part of the main covenant, share its charter and Tribunal rulings, and may add a local charter for their own residents. The sidebar also suggests how a player covenant can become one of the chapters.
quotes: All magi must accept the charter of Fengheld, and any strictures or rulings from the Tribunal that apply to Fengheld also apply to the chapter houses (and vice versa).
a chapter usually has a local charter that applies only to those magi who live in the chapter house

entries.title: The Feengrotten (shifting caves yielding Imaginem vis)
entries.summary: A faerie-touched cave network with a weak Magic aura whose passages shift; only those who are genuinely lost for days emerge covered in Imaginem vis dust, while anyone trying to exploit the property gets plain dust.
quotes: The Feengrotten has a Magic aura of 1.
the dust is Imaginem vis, the quantity dependent on how many days that they were lost

entries.title: Crintera's four-level heartbeast regio
entries.requires: Visiting Crintera (the House Bjornaer domus magna on Rugen)
entries.summary: Crintera lies in a four-level regio whose auras rise by level; as each boundary is crossed every visitor must resist a Corpus effect that brings out a heartbeast, first changing Personality Traits and then causing minor physical changes. Parma Magica and a Bjornaer Heartbeast roll can resist or shrug off the changes.
quotes: There are four levels to the magical regio, with auras of 1, 3, 5, and 8.
every character must resist a Corpus effect with a Penetration Total equal to the Ease Factor needed to see the next level
Of course, magi of House Bjornaer can shrug off these changes with a Heartbeast roll, should they want to.

entries.title: The Gathering of Twelve Years (House Bjornaer)
entries.summary: The House Bjornaer assembly held at Crintera every twelve years, when most initiations into the House's Mysteries take place. Includes advice for running the Gathering in a saga, including giving non-Bjornaer players a Bjornaer character for the event.
quotes: most initiations into the Mysteries of House Bjornaer are conducted during the gathering
The next gathering, due in 1227, is likely to be politically explosive

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bjornaer)

entries.title: Council of Elders and the Seats of Crintera (Bjornaer governance)
entries.summary: How the Council of Elders of Crintera is organized: six seats with fixed duties, how vacant seats are filled at the Gathering, the Primus's Seat of the Wolf, the reserved Senior Elder seat and its casting vote.
quotes: When an Elder dies or passes into Final Twilight, he will not be replaced until the next Gathering of Twelve Years.
The Senior Elder has the casting vote in any decision of the council

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (House Bjornaer)

entries.title: Crintera covenfolk: the six animal clans
entries.requires: Covenant of House Bjornaer (Crintera) or a similar heartbeast-themed turb
entries.summary: Organizes the grogs and covenfolk of Crintera into six animal clans mirroring the Elders' seats, each with a role, preferred weapons and a clan leader; shows how to build a themed turb whose warriors share a heartbeast style.
quotes: The grogs and covenfolk are divided into six clans, named just as the six seats of the Elders.

entries.title: Pomeranian werewolves (skinchanger families)
entries.requires: Born into a Pomeranian werewolf family (storyguide approval)
entries.summary: Explains how shapeshifting is inherited in Pomeranian werewolf families, which Virtue or Flaw a child receives, how animals react to them, and offers a list of suitable additional Virtues and Flaws for playing a werewolf companion.
quotes: A child born into a werewolf family will acquire the Skinchanger Virtue.
Those unlucky enough to be born into human families will usually acquire the Lycanthrope Flaw, and be unable to control their change.

entries.title: Slave trade and prices
entries.summary: Describes the Prague slave market, who controls it, and gives a rule of thumb for what a slave costs relative to a horse, with higher prices for skilled, strong or young slaves.
quotes: An unremarkable slave may be purchased for as little as a few schillings
the younger, healthier, and stronger the slave is, the more he or she may be sold for

entries.title: Irencillia: Shifting Appearance and Patchy Faerie Aura
entries.summary: Faerie glamour makes the covenant look and feel different to each visitor, with sancta and communal areas settling into a firm consensus reality. Its Faerie aura varies from place to place, with the strongest patches (some inside regiones) holding the magi's sancta.
quotes: The Faerie aura of Irencillia is highly patchy.
All areas within the boundary wall have an aura of at least 1

entries.title: Caricatures of Irencillia
entries.requires: Residence at Irencillia (House Merinita domus magna)
entries.summary: Every long-term magus resident at Irencillia gains a faerie double, a caricature raised from the servant-folk, whose Faerie Might can grow with the magus's status and which may become an Arcane Connection to its human. Residents are treated as having the Faerie Friend Flaw for the duration of their stay.
quotes: In game terms, every long-term resident of Irencillia gains the Faerie Friend Flaw for the duration of his or her visit.

entries.title: Mount Radhost Ritual and Corpus Vis
entries.summary: The summit temple holds a strong Magic aura, and the yearly solstice festival to Radegast, fuelled by human sacrifice, lets the Roznov magi harvest large amounts of vis, including Corpus vis from the blood.
quotes: It has a Magic aura of 6.
The blood of the sacrifices is harvested for Corpus vis.

entries.title: Radegast
entries.summary: Describes the pagan Slavic god Radegast and the Virtues and Flaw his favored followers tend to display, useful when building his devotees as characters.
quotes: Those he favors often display the Inspirational and Great Presence Virtues, as well as the Overconfident Flaw.

related.text: Between the Devil and the Deep Blue Sea (Chapter 11)

entries.title: Establishing Your Covenant: Four Starting Options
entries.summary: Sets out four ways a group of Rhine magi can begin a saga: founding a new covenant, establishing a chapter house, settling at an existing covenant, or travelling between covenants as peregrinatores. Each option carries different approval requirements, resources and independence.
quotes: Any covenant with sufficient resources might support chapters

related.text: Chapter 3: The Rhine Tribunal, On the Founding of Covenants

entries.title: Chapter Houses
entries.summary: A chapter house lets a covenant with enough resources support additional sites. Chapters need no Tribunal approval and receive resources from the motherhouse, but are bound by the parent covenant's charter.
quotes: Chapters are not new covenants, therefore they do not require the approval of Tribunal; also, the motherhouse will provide resources for its foundation.

entries.title: Peregrinatores: Travelling Between Covenants
entries.summary: The Rhine Tribunal's tradition of hospitality lets wandering magi guest at other covenants without a permanent home of their own.
quotes: traditions of hospitality for wandering magi

related.text: Chapter 3: The Rhine Tribunal, Upon Being a Rhine Magus

entries.title: Radegast and Gymir: Disguised Infernal Auras
entries.summary: Describes two rival demon princes, how heavily the Order may be infiltrated, and Radegast's ability to disguise Infernal power so that his sites register as Magic or Faerie auras.
quotes: he is able to disguise his infernal power as magic or faerie power

entries.title: Saga Magi: Characters and Starting Resources
entries.summary: Guidance for building the player magi for the Curse of the Rhine Gorge saga: backgrounds, optional Gild Trained for Rhine-apprenticed magi, and a spread of starting resources such as shield grogs and money, with Fengheld magi favored.
quotes: the Minor Virtue (Gild) Trained
which allows them to start with a personal shield grog and a reasonable sum of money

related.text: Chapter 3: Tribunal History and Customs, Upon Being a Rhine Magus

entries.title: Saga Start: A Gentle Introduction
entries.summary: An easier saga start in which an existing friendly covenant supplies labs, books, grogs, vis or money while the young magi explore before settling.

entries.title: Saga Start: In at the Deep End
entries.summary: A harder saga start in which the magi leave Durenmar lightly equipped with scant resources and must found the covenant from the ground up.

entries.title: Saga Grogs and Shield Grogs
entries.summary: Explains that grogs are less central than magi, need not be taken at the very start, and may be recruited or donated as a founding gift; a shield grog should be played by someone other than the magus's player.
quotes: A grog who is assigned to be the shield grog of a particular magus should be played by someone other than the player of that magus.

entries.title: Seeking Tribunal Approval for a New Covenant
entries.summary: Rhine law requires a prospective covenant to be sponsored by one magus from every other covenant, which usually means trading promises, favors and debts; the sponsorship of a single magus is enough from each covenant.
quotes: a prospective covenant must be sponsored by one magus from every other covenant in the Tribunal

related.text: Chapter 3: Tribunal History and Customs, On the Founding of Covenants

entries.title: Companions for the Saga
entries.summary: Suggests companion character types that magi may befriend as the covenant settles in, and advises making a player's companion dissimilar to their magus.
quotes: these two characters should ideally be dissimilar

entries.title: The Receiving of Gifts
entries.summary: Each sponsor gives the new covenant a gift whose value reflects that covenant's greatness and attitude, such as books, magic items, valuables or grogs, delivered immediately or in later seasons.

entries.title: Imperial Toll Levels
entries.summary: A table of the emperor's set toll per vessel type, the daily income a toll station can expect from passing traffic, and the need for armed enforcement against rivals and toll-runners.
quotes: Small rowboat (5 persons or less) — 1d
Large ship (two or more masts) — 12d
providing a daily income of 10 schillings or more

entries.title: By Land or by River? (Merchant Route Choice)
entries.summary: Explains how merchants weigh shipwreck risk against overland banditry and tolls when choosing between river transport and portage, including the common portage bypass of the Bingen Hole.

entries.title: Mouse Swarm Attacks (Mäuseturm)
entries.summary: A swarm of demonic mice automatically damages victims each round according to the protection they wear, with no attack roll, and is driven off when over half the mice are killed. Includes how area spells and Brawl attacks affect a swarm and why the swarm regenerates in an Infernal aura.
quotes: No attack roll is required for the mice

entries.title: Loreley: Treacherous River Stretch
entries.summary: The narrowest stretch of the Rhine Gorge is dangerous to boats even without the siren, with a Boating roll needed by crews who have not learned the positions of the rocks, and the cliff has a Faerie aura.
quotes: Ease Factor 9 for those who have not learned the positions of the rocks

entries.title: The Rhine Faerie Courts: Seasonal Dominion
entries.summary: Describes the rival Seelie and Unseelie faerie courts on either side of the Rhine, when and where each can be found, how they alternate dominion through the year, and how they can become contested vis sources. Offers the Courts of the Seasons as an alternative.
quotes: Dark Summer holds dominion over Bright Winter from Walpurgis Night until All Hallows Eve, and vice versa.

related.text: Chapter 4: The Forest (Courts of the Seasons)

groups.title: The Normandy Tribunal
groups.intro: Rules particular to the Normandy Tribunal (The Lion and the Lily).

entries.title: The Blood of Merovech
entries.requires: Merovingian descent (Supernatural Virtue such as Greater Immunity: Drowning; Royal Touch)
entries.summary: Sidebar on the Merovingian bloodline: which Supernatural Virtues descendants of Merovech commonly carry, the red-cross birthmark, and theories on the origin of the king's Royal Touch.
quotes: most of the descendants of Merovech have a Supernatural Virtue
Greater Immunity: Drowning

related.text: Chapter 10: Normandy Sagas, The Tradition of Kings

entries.title: The Holy Oil of Consecration (Anointed King Benefits)
entries.requires: Anointed King of France (coronation with the holy oil of Reims)
entries.summary: Describes the game effects of anointing a Frankish or French king with the holy oil kept at Reims (Magic Resistance, Soak bonus and a commanding aura), the 3-point relic status of the ampoule, and the speculation about its other powers.
quotes: giving the king a Magic Resistance of 10, a Soak bonus of 2, and a Commanding Aura to Voice range with an effect equivalent to Aura of Rightful Authority with Penetration 0

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.42-43

entries.title: The Carolingian Blood
entries.summary: Sidebar noting that characters of Carolingian descent may be politically important and often carry a particular Virtue.
quotes: Those of Carolingian blood often have the Virtue Mythic Presence.

entries.title: The Capetian Blood
entries.summary: Sidebar on the pious Capetian bloodline, some of whose members manifest a faith-related Virtue.
quotes: Some members of the bloodline manifest this as the Virtue True Faith

entries.title: The Angevin Blood
entries.summary: Sidebar on the legend of Melusine and the uncertain, unpredictable supernatural heritage of the Angevin line, left for the troupe to define.
quotes: This tainted blood runs in the Angevin veins till this day, and may manifest in unpredictable ways.

entries.title: The Hermetic Landscape (Tribunal-Owned Vis and the Tourney)
entries.summary: Overview of how vis outside covenant grounds belongs to the whole Normandy Tribunal and is leased out through a seven-yearly Tourney that also awards books and other resources.
quotes: all vis that does not originate from within the grounds of a covenant was declared to be the property of the Tribunal as a whole rather than of any specific individual covenant

entries.title: The Perthean Compact
entries.summary: Introduces the Peripheral Code rulings that make all Normandy vis sources the property of covenants and sort them into seisins, legacies, tropaea and luctationes.
quotes: The Perthean Compact revolves around the ruling that all vis sources, whether they are exclusive access in perpetuity or a fixed term lease, belong to covenants, not to individuals. It categorizes vis sources into four types: seisins, legacies, tropaea, and luctationes.

entries.title: Seisins (and Cursor Travel Distance)
entries.summary: A vis source within a day's return march of a covenant's council chamber is automatically that covenant's seisin with exclusive harvest rights; includes the test of proving the distance with a cursor and a rule of thumb for miles covered per day.
quotes: A seisin recognized by the Tribunal grants its owners exclusive right of harvest.

if a man can get from the covenant's council chamber to a vis source and back again, on his own two feet and unaided by magic, between sunrise and sunset on a day which is within a month of an equinox, then the vis source is a seisin of that covenant
10 + (2 x Athletics) cross country

entries.title: Legacies (distant vis sources)
entries.summary: A newly found vis source too far to be a seisin can be a legacy lease held by its discoverer for seven years, renewable only by Tribunal vote; poaching from a legacy is a High Crime.
quotes: the terms of the lease last only seven years
the offender is automatically found guilty of the High Crime of depriving a magus of his magical power

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.59

entries.title: Tricks and Cheats (Seisin Manipulation)
entries.summary: Sidebar on how covenants bend seisin rules: remote council chambers, unchallenged assumed distances, and altering terrain to make or unmake a seisin.
quotes: a claim that remains uncontested stays a seisin until challenged.

entries.title: Tropaea
entries.summary: Easily harvested vis sources that are neither seisins nor legacies belong to the Tribunal and are leased for seven years to Tourney winners; founding a covenant near one needs Tribunal approval.
quotes: Tropaea are to be distributed among the members of the Tribunal on seven-year leases by being won in the Tourney.

entries.title: Luctationes
entries.summary: Tribunal-owned vis sources that need skill or risk to harvest are open contests for any magus each year, confer no lasting rights, and cost no Build Points unless a covenant has exclusive access.
quotes: If a covenant does have exclusive access to a luctatio for some reason, then it is costed as a vis source with the Contested Resource Hook.

entries.title: Interim Leases and Plundering
entries.summary: Procedure for claiming a newly found vis source through a Quaesitor's interim lease, and the Low Crime of plundering for harvesting without one.
quotes: A covenant which harvests a hitherto unknown vis source but chooses not to secure an interim lease is guilty of plundering, a Low Crime under the Peripheral Code of the Normandy Tribunal.

entries.title: The Perthean Compact and New Covenants
entries.summary: Optional guidance for limiting Build Points spent on vis when creating a Normandy covenant, and for founding a covenant with legacies or tropaea instead of seisins.
quotes: but 3 to 5 Build Points per magus to be spent on vis is reasonable.

entries.title: Minor Resources Hook: Vis Lease
entries.summary: A covenant Hook for a vis source that is only leased (legacy or tropaeum), forcing the covenant to campaign or compete at Tribunal to keep it; may be taken multiple times.
quotes: One of the covenant's vis sources is a legacy or a tropaeum rather than a seisin.

entries.title: The Library of the Normandy Tribunal
entries.summary: Magi who donate an original book to the Tribunal library win a guaranteed Tourney prize of a leased book of similar quality, with certamen to settle clashes over the same book.
quotes: Contributing an original book to the Tribunal's library grants a magus an automatic prize at the next Tourney, the lease of a book of similar quality to the one offered.
a character may chose a book that is worth up to as many Covenant Build Points as the one he contributed

entries.title: The Perthean Compact and Personal Vis Sources
entries.requires: Normandy Tribunal; Hermetic Virtue granting a personal vis source
entries.summary: Explains how a magus's own bodily vis is exempt from the Perthean Compact and how a character with an external personal vis source can justify it in a Normandy saga.
quotes: any vis that is generated by the person of a magus (in his hair, blood, and so forth) is the sole possession of that magus, and not subject to the Perthean Compact

entries.title: The Library of the Tribunal (Book Leases)
entries.summary: Rules for books won as Tourney prizes: seven-year exclusive lease, the leaseholder's duty to keep and return the book to Confluensis, and the Cow and Calf Oath on copies.
quotes: Winning a book in the tournament grants exclusive access to that tome for a total of seven years
Books are leased under a Cow and Calf Oath

related.text: Covenants p.95 Cow and Calf Oath

entries.title: Mundane Resources and Covenant Raiding
entries.summary: Explains why raiding another covenant's mundane resources is not a Hermetic crime in Normandy and gives storyguide advice on the consequences of raids, including the Poverty Hook and tracking yearly expenditures.
quotes: Raids should be primarily a source of stories, but may result in the gain or loss of supplies.

entries.title: Rulings on Mundane Resources and Raiding
entries.summary: Lists what counts as a magus's magical power (protected) and what does not (raidable), and the conduct rules for a raid: no damage to buildings, no Code breaches, and certamen against accompanying magi.
quotes: food, consumables, building supplies, arms and armor, and luxury goods are not part of a magus's magical power
The raiding maga must challenge any accompanying magi to certamen; should she lose then she must abandon her raid.

entries.title: Cross-Border Disputes
entries.summary: Foreign magi raiding into Normandy fall under the Normandy Peripheral Code, and the Tribunal's only recourse is to judge them harshly if they break the Code.
quotes: when in Normandy they are under the jurisdiction of the Normandy Peripheral Code

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.56

entries.title: Urban Covenants and the Town Sene
entries.summary: Background and precedent (Fudarus versus Atramentum, 1200) for how Tribunal law handles covenants interacting with autonomous towns.

entries.title: The Town Senex
entries.summary: The covenant nearest a town, judged by whose church bells sound loudest, is the senex and has superior rights in that town over other covenants' agents.
quotes: The Tribunal of 1200 determined that the agents of the covenant closest to a town, referred to as the senex, have superior rights to those of the agents of other covenants operating in that town.
The senex is judged to be the covenant in which the town's church bells sound the loudest, as determined by a Quaesitor.

entries.title: Urban Covenants (Town Charters and Fealty)
entries.summary: A covenant may be sited in a town and hold a mundane town charter and pay collective tax, but magi cannot use charter privileges, vote or hold office because that would amount to swearing fealty.
quotes: However, the magi themselves cannot take advantage of any privileges under the charter, as to do so would be effectively the same as swearing an oath of fealty.

entries.title: A Covenant Charter
entries.summary: Why a covenant benefits from a grant of charter: it formally limits what mundane lords can demand of the covenant.

entries.title: Implications of the Senex and Urban Covenant Rulings
entries.summary: Notes that the senex ruling can decide ownership of unclaimed urban vis sources, that senex rights depend on how far bells carry, and that seeking mundane charters is encouraged.

entries.title: Mundane Interference (Masks)
entries.summary: Normandy treats meddling with mundanes as an offense only once mundane reprisals harm Hermetic victims, so covenants act through masks; masks give no protection against depriving other magi of their power.
quotes: Masks provide no protection from charges of depriving other magi of their power, so they cannot legally be used against the senex of a town.

entries.title: Mundane Interference (Tribunal Ruling)
entries.summary: No specific rulings exist on agencies and masks, but the Tribunal rarely convicts when damage to a Hermetic magus cannot be clearly demonstrated.
quotes: the Tribunal rarely convicts in situations where damage to a Hermetic magus cannot be unequivocally demonstrated.

entries.title: Further Excerpts from the Normandy Peripheral Code
entries.summary: Dated precedents of the Normandy Tribunal covering court wizardry, borders, raids, deprivation of magical power, covert healing and mundane interference.
quotes: Quaesitor Lothaire ruled that raiding magi are forbidden from damaging the physical structure of a covenant

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Ex Miscellanea

entries.title: Founding a New Covenant (Normandy Requirements)
entries.summary: The legal requirements for a new Normandy covenant: exclusive vis supply of a set minimum, a recognized council chamber at a safe distance from other covenants, and no use of chapter houses to dodge the Compact; vis from the local aura counts only as stock.
quotes: The only legal requirement is that the nascent covenant has exclusive access to one or more sources of vis that collectively supply a minimum of one pawn of vis per year for every magus in the new covenant (or at least four pawns per year, if there are fewer than four magi).
Vis extracted from the local aura does not count as a vis supply but as vis stocks

entries.title: Typical Duties of Service
entries.summary: Sample duties a vassal covenant may owe its liege: proxy sigils, directed votes, vis tithes, book copying and legacy harvesting.

entries.title: Typical Duties of Protection (and Oath Boons and Hooks)
entries.summary: Sample duties of protection a liege owes its vassals, and how oath terms translate into covenant Boons and Hooks such as Powerful Ally and Beholden.
quotes: Terms that are favorable to the vassal may give them the Powerful Ally Boon, but most oaths leave the vassal with Hooks such as Beholden.

entries.title: Breaking Free (Escaping an Oath of Fealty)
entries.summary: How a vassal covenant can end its oath, by defaulting on duties and being convicted or by prosecuting its liege, with a table of suitable Boons and Hooks for liege and vassal.
quotes: To gain independence from a liege, a vassal covenant must either wait for its liege to default on the oath of fealty, or deliberately break it themselves, since either party can cancel the oath following a successful prosecution.

entries.title: Liege & Vassal Covenants
entries.summary: Describes the usual way new Normandy covenants form, as vassals of a covenant holding a legacy, and the five great lines of liege covenants.
quotes: The vassal covenant is established within a day's march of the legacy, and ownership of the vis source passes from the liege covenant to the vassal, which may then register it as a seisin at the next Tribunal meeting.

entries.title: Oaths of Fealty
entries.summary: How covenant-to-covenant oaths of fealty work: duty of support from the vassal, duty of protection from the liege, legal enforceability, and how an oath can be dissolved.
quotes: Oaths of fealty between vassal and liege covenants are part of Normandy's Peripheral Code and legally enforceable, although covenants are still forbidden to take oaths of fealty to a mundane lord.

entries.title: Eremites and Coenobites
entries.summary: Solitary magi (eremites) and communities that fail the vis requirement (coenobia) cannot hold seisins and must rely on Tourney tropaea and luctationes, competing as individuals.
quotes: An eremite is forbidden by the Peripheral Code from owning a seisin, and he must rely upon tropaeum leases won at the Tourney or attending luctatio for his vis supply.

entries.title: Tribunal Meetings (Hosting)
entries.summary: A covenant chosen by lot to host the Tribunal must provide a tournament site, an excellent Aegis of the Hearth and lavish hospitality, and risks financial ruin and Quaesitorial scrutiny.
quotes: The covenant is expected to provide a secluded area for the tournament, an excellent Aegis of the Hearth, and lavish hospitality.

entries.title: The Hermetic Tourney
entries.summary: Overview of the seven-yearly Tourney: who may enter, team size limits, the entry stake for outside teams, and the six traditional events.
quotes: Each team that does not represent one accepted Normandy covenant must stake five pawns of vis per magi to enter
Teams are limited to a maximum of five members, excluding grogs and companions.

entries.title: Winning the Tourney (Scoring)
entries.summary: Points scoring for each Tourney event, tie-breaking by seniority, the named finishing ranks, and the Hermetic Reputation granted for achieving them.
quotes: A team receives a starting tally equal to the number of members of their covenant
The team winning the hastiludium receives 20 points, the defeated finalist 10 points, and the other semifinalists five points each.
Any covenant achieving one of the named ranks in the Tourney has an appropriate Hermetic Reputation of level 2 for the next seven years.

entries.title: Tourney Events (General Rules)
entries.summary: Sidebar introducing the events: an even number of registered teams, and the hosting covenant's own event to be declared by the previous summer solstice.
quotes: Tradition and the rules demand there must always be an even number of teams in the tournament.

entries.title: The Hastiludium
entries.summary: Tourney event where teams of three magi on improvised magical mounts use spells to force opponents off and push their mount past the other team's line.
quotes: Each magus may cast a single spell before the contest begins in order to prepare, and may then cast magic freely during the contest.
Parma Magica may not be extended over the mounts, but both sides may freely cast magic on either mount.

entries.title: The Certamen Tournament
entries.summary: Knockout certamen event in which the older magus chooses the Technique and the younger the Form, with a team champion picked each round.
quotes: The older magus chooses the Technique, the younger the Form.

entries.title: The Joust
entries.summary: Mounted knockout event between single champions, best of three, where magic may affect only one's own person, mount or weapons; the Tourney's most dangerous event.
quotes: The winner is the magus who prevails in a best of three match

entries.title: The Melee
entries.summary: Non-magical team contest for grogs and companions to capture opposing Creo Imaginem circle castles using blunt weapons; seriously injuring an opponent forfeits the contest.
quotes: Three grog or companion champions for each team attempt to charge across the field
damage is fatigue unless botched

entries.title: The Dimicatio
entries.summary: House Flambeau's duel in which champions cast forceless spells at each other and defend with fast-cast defenses; penetrating the opponent's Parma is foul play.
quotes: Each magus uses a fast-cast defense (ArM5, page 83) to try to block the opposing spell. The first magus whose spell reaches his opponent's Parma is the winner.

entries.title: The Hosting Covenant's Choice
entries.summary: The sixth Tourney event is chosen by the host covenant and must be a true test of magical ability.
quotes: It must be a true test of magical ability, but beyond that may take any form.

entries.title: Tourney Prizes
entries.summary: How prize pawns are spent in rank order on tropaea, books, items and entrance-fee vis, with conversion rates between prize pawns and Build Points.
quotes: Calculate this as 1 prize pawn per 5 Build Points of the book.
One prize pawn may be traded for an immediate once-only selection of 5 pawns of Form vis, or three pawns of Technique vis.

entries.title: Tourney Ranks & Prizes (Table)
entries.summary: Table of prize pawns awarded for each finishing rank, with advice on adjusting it for richer or poorer sagas.
quotes: The prizes listed in this table assume at least 200 pawns worth of prizes are available in total, and 24 teams entering.

entries.title: St. Broch's Fountain Blessing (Lamballe and St. Brieuc)
entries.summary: A once-a-week devotional ritual at St. Broch's fountain after Sunday Mass that grants a temporary one-step shift to a Personality Trait, up to the usual cap, lasting until sunset.
quotes: a character may dip his right hand into the fountain and devoutly make the sign of the cross to gain a Blessing that gives a temporary change to a Personality Trait by one step
The blessing lasts until sunset.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.51

entries.title: Siting a Covenant in Brittany
entries.summary: Guidance on placing a player covenant in sparsely populated Brittany: many unclaimed vis sources and sites, but the covenant must still fit into or evade the feudal and Church structure.
quotes: Brittany is the least-civilized, most sparsely populated part of the Tribunal, with many unclaimed vis resources.

entries.title: Brocéliande (Faerie Forest, Auras and Vis Sources)
entries.summary: The Faerie forest of Brocéliande with its aura levels, the Fountain of Youth, the Stone of Merlin, Lake Comper's Faerie regio and the vis available from its lake, bridge and Barenton fountain.
quotes: Most of the forest has a Faerie aura of level 2 and there are places where it is considerably higher.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p.38 Path of Aging

entries.title: Carnac (Magic by Day, Infernal by Night)
entries.summary: The great stone avenues of Carnac, one of the strongest Magic auras known, which turns Infernal at night and is haunted by the Nains, with notes on research there and its many regiones.
quotes: By day, a Magic aura of strength 5 covers the heath
As the shadows lengthen the Magic aura fades away, and at night an Infernal aura replaces the magic.

entries.title: Mont St. Michael (Tidal Divine Regio)
entries.summary: The abbey is a Divine regio at high tide that nobody can enter or leave, with only an ordinary Divine aura at low tide; also covers its history as a former druidic site whose Magic aura was destroyed.
quotes: the monastery has a Divine aura of only 4

entries.title: Angers: Béhuard Island Dominion over Magic
entries.summary: Describes a former pagan shrine on an island in the Loire whose weak Magic aura has been overwhelmed by a Dominion aura from local prayer, and notes one nearby valley free of any Dominion aura. A worked example of Dominion displacing Magic in a populated Christian region.
quotes: their attentions have raised a Dominion aura to swamp the level-2 Magic aura of the old pagan shrine

entries.title: Tavant: Residual Magic Aura Under a Church
entries.summary: A church built over the ruins of the old covenant of Sinapis keeps a residual Magic aura that is normally overridden by the Dominion aura.
quotes: The residual Magic aura can only reassert itself when the Dominion aura is at its weakest.

entries.title: Tours: Magic and Faerie Auras Around the City
entries.summary: Lists several nearby sites with stated aura levels: a Roman tower with a Magic aura that grows stronger toward its top, a cave valley suited to a covenant site with an Aquam vis source, and a dolmen whose Faerie aura strengthens when the fae are present.
quotes: The structure normally has a Faerie aura of level 3, but this rises to 5 when the fae are present

entries.title: Gennes: Nymph Regio
entries.summary: A small Magic regio beside a Roman amphitheatre where nymphs may give Aquam vis to visitors who please them, and where male visitors may find it hard to leave.
quotes: There is a small Magic regio close beside this, where several nymphs live in a Gallo-Roman shrine.

entries.title: Noirmoutier: Island Magic Aura with Higher Beach
entries.summary: A coastal island with a modest Magic aura and a sacred beach where the aura is stronger, described as a possible covenant site with notable resources.
quotes: The isle has a Magic aura of level 3.

entries.title: Poitiers: Dominion Auras of Holy Sites
entries.summary: Gives Dominion aura levels for specific holy sites, including one that has faded over time through changed usage.
quotes: the Dominion aura there has faded to level 4
it has a Dominion aura of 5

entries.title: Vézère Valley: Magic Aura, Aligned Caves and Regio
entries.summary: Describes an extensive Magic aura under a river valley whose cave paintings and formations give higher, Form-aligned aura levels, plus a two-level regio reached through linked caves.
quotes: Places with the most vivid depictions have a Magic aura of 5 or 6, aligned with Animal

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.25

entries.title: Clermont: Moon-Gated Regio
entries.summary: A regio grove with a Terram vis spring beneath a city, entered through a spring-fed clump of trees and passable only at a particular phase of the moon.
quotes: The way in and out is only accessible when the moon is full.

entries.title: Auvergne Mountains: Puy de Dôme Regio and Healing Springs
entries.summary: Covers a regio on the Puy de Dôme entered by following the Roman road, scattered low Magic auras that yield vis in particular ways, and hot springs and gases that give a bonus to recovery rolls when used for a limited time.
quotes: Treat half an hour spent immersed in the water or breathing in the gas as giving a +3 to the recovery roll

entries.title: Oleron: The Apple Mile Faerie Regio
entries.summary: Describes a covenant regio with a strong Faerie aura and perpetual summer, whose roads loop back on themselves and lead only to the mortal world and the Stone Couches.
quotes: Within the regio, which has a Faerie aura of 5, it is always summer.

entries.title: Oleron: The Queen's Champion and the Challenges
entries.summary: Explains how the consort of the Faerie Queen of the Apple Mile is chosen by a Midsummer challenge, what a defeated challenger owes in restitution (a compelled task resisted as a Mentem effect with a stated Penetration), and what happens to the queen, her daughter and the old consort.
quotes: This may be resisted as a ReMe effect with a Penetration of 75

entries.title: Oleron: Stone Couches and Sleepers
entries.summary: Rules-flavored explanation of how tumuli grow faerie duplicates of folk heroes over years, how a Sleeper's powers and Might follow the hero's folklore and Reputation, when Sleepers wake, and what happens if an ordinary human is buried in a Couch.
quotes: A tumulus will build a skeleton for its hero after three years, and grow his flesh over the next eighteen.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (Mystery of Becoming)

entries.title: Bee King (Strong Faerie Blood variety)
entries.requires: Virtue: Strong Faerie Blood (Bee King variety)
entries.summary: Describes the special powers of a Bee King: commanding bees, speaking with hives, immunity to biting insects, and treating attacking bee swarms as an automatic damage effect rather than a melee group, along with the fixed lifespan drawback.
quotes: An attacking bee swarm is treated as an environmental effect, rather than an opposing mêlée group.

entries.title: Atsingani: Council Chamber Fixed by Tribunal Custom
entries.summary: A mobile covenant with no native aura is nonetheless bound by Tribunal custom to keep a fixed council chamber, which Quaesitors may check, and which also supplies its only stable vis.
quotes: The Tribunal's customs forbid them from moving their council chamber

entries.title: Atsingani: Limits of a Mobile Covenant
entries.summary: Lists the drawbacks of a covenant without a permanent base: no stable income, no fortifications, only poor shared tent laboratories, and a single fixed vis source.
quotes: can only establish rather poor temporary laboratories (apart from the one belonging to Viviana) in tents, which they share

entries.title: Templar Treasury: Deposits, Receipts and Loans
entries.summary: Explains how the Knights Templar act as a bank: deposits against coded parchment receipts that are drawn down along a pilgrimage, transfers for merchants and nobles, and loans that avoid the usury ban by charging rents.
quotes: the restriction on usury (the charging of interest) is sidestepped by the charging of

entries.title: Eboris: Injured Sodalis and Enforcing the Code in Paris
entries.summary: Explains how a local magus can serve as a convenient injured party so that otherwise tolerated activities become breaches of the Code, and why even minor infractions near Parisian potentates are punished in this Tribunal.
quotes: An injured sodalis makes an undesired activity a breach of the Code.

entries.title: Fontainebleau: Fountain of Fair Waters Faerie Regio
entries.summary: A Faerie regio around a spring with a nymph, tolerant of humble visitors but cursing hunters who persist, with transformed boulders that can be harvested for vis.
quotes: It has a Faerie aura of 6.

entries.title: Lapis Crudus: Regio Gate and Social Status Swap
entries.summary: Describes the sealed Faerie regio containing the covenant and the mirror-hut gate through which people can cross only by exchanging places with someone of comparable Social Status, along with the regio's Faerie aura and vis sources.
quotes: The persons must have comparable (but not necessarily identical) Social Status Virtues or Flaws to effect the passage to or from the regio
Within the regio, the covenant sits in a Faerie aura of 7.

entries.title: Lapis Crudus: Warping from a Strong Faerie Aura
entries.summary: Notes that magi trapped for decades in a strong Faerie aura gather Warping from the aura itself, in addition to their Longevity Rituals, and risk Final Twilight.
quotes: Each magus has accrued one Warping Point a year for the last eighty years of entrapment from the aura alone

entries.title: Lapis Crudus: Warping of Covenfolk Born in the Regio
entries.summary: Gives typical Warping Scores for mundane covenfolk raised in a strong Faerie regio at puberty and in later life, with the consequence that they treat magic items as normal.
quotes: acquiring a Warping Score of 3 by the time the reach puberty, and a Score of 5 in their late forties

entries.title: Flemish Cloth Fairs: Trade Fair Cycle
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the yearly cycle and order of Flemish cloth trade fairs, how the counts keep them secure, and a pointer to the general trade fair rules.
quotes: The cycle of trade fairs in Flanders runs from February to November

entries.title: Bavacum: Seven Roads and Mercury's Shortcuts
entries.summary: A Magic aura site where one of seven Roman roads gives a shortened journey depending on the heavens, with a roll to predict which road is active and an annual day when all roads work and footprints yield vis.
quotes: An Intelligence + Artes Liberales roll against an Ease Factor of 12 may be made to accurately predict which road will be active at any given time.

entries.title: Florum: Hiding a Source of Wealth Under the Peripheral Code
entries.summary: Shows how a covenant disguises a magically produced income behind a factory and a fictional family so that its wealth remains lawful under the Tribunal's Peripheral Code.
quotes: therefore legal according to the Tribunal's Peripheral Code

entries.title: Spider's Palace: Splitting Covenants to Claim Resources
entries.summary: Illustrates how the Normandy way of apportioning magical resources pushes nearby sites to be declared separate covenants, with one resident magus keeping the legal claim.
quotes: A single magus usually lives here, to maintain the covenant's claim to the surrounding resources

entries.title: Faux de Verzy: Faerie Aura Grove
entries.summary: A feared grove of twisted beeches with a stated Faerie aura, where captives are said to return scarred.
quotes: This place, which has a Faerie aura of 4, is shunned by the nearby peasants.

entries.title: Nanteuil: Possible Divine Regio
entries.summary: A Templar priory in a remote vale that one magus recorded as a regio of possibly Divine origin, though others blame a Twilight episode.
quotes: found it to be a regio, possibly of Divine origin

entries.title: Blue Springs of the Somme: Faerie Pools
entries.summary: Enchanted pools with Faerie auras of varying strength whose sprites steal things or reward gifts and bless infants.
quotes: The pools have Faerie auras of differing strengths, up to 3.

entries.title: Caves of Naours: Pact with a Genius Loci
entries.summary: An underground village protected by a mutual-protection pact with a cave spirit, set within a weak Magic aura.
quotes: A Magic aura of 2 pervades throughout.

entries.title: Champagne Trade Fairs
entries.summary: Sidebar describing the cycle of Champagne trade fairs, what is traded, and how Redcaps set up temporary Mercer Houses there to trade vis, books and news, with a pointer to the trade fair rules.
quotes: There are six main trade fairs in the great Champagne cycle

entries.title: Clairvaux: Divine Aura of an Abbey
entries.summary: Gives the Divine aura of a major Cistercian abbey as an example of a strong Dominion site.
quotes: The entire abbey has a Divine aura of 6.

entries.title: Catalaunian Fields: Infernal Aura and Solstice Regio
entries.summary: A battlefield with a Malevolent Infernal aura that on one night of the year opens into an Infernal regio of fighting shades, where Perdo and Corpus vis can be harvested, some of it Infernally tainted.
quotes: A Malevolent Infernal aura of 3

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.15

entries.title: Mont Auxois: Magic and Divine Aura on One Hill
entries.summary: A haunted hilltop ruin that keeps a Magic aura and could suit a covenant, with a separate Divine aura around a martyr's healing fountain on one edge.
quotes: The place retains a Magic aura and might make a suitable site for a covenant
On the southwestern edge of the hilltop, a Divine aura prevails.

entries.title: Cave of Sabinus: Genius Loci and Luctatio
entries.summary: A cave with a demanding genius loci that permits Aquam vis to be harvested from its spring, treated by the Tribunal as a contested vis site (a luctatio).
quotes: the site is, however, considered a luctatio by the Tribunal

entries.title: Cluny: Optional Infernal Corruption Inside a Divine Aura
entries.summary: Offers an optional dark option for a saga in which Infernal auras hide within, or weaken, the strong Divine aura of a wealthy monastery.
quotes: as an optional, somewhat dark take for your saga

entries.title: Cunfin: Magic Regio Within a Divine Aura
entries.summary: A covenant sits in a Magic regio overlapping a monastery's strong Divine aura, a coexistence nobody can explain, with a single-level regio entered by anyone carrying a charm made from stones of the old fort.
quotes: The regio's single level can be accessed by anyone holding a charm made from the stones of the fort.

entries.title: Cunfin: Holy Influence Calming the Dominion, Mercere Portal
entries.summary: Describes how a magus with Holy Influence shapes the temper of the surrounding Dominion to reduce conflict with mundanes, that the magi's Gentle Gift eases dealings with locals, and that the covenant hosts a Mercere Portal.
quotes: Eloi uses his Holy Influence to give the Dominion surrounding the monastery a Calm temper

entries.title: Forming a New Tribunal (Lotharingian Tribunal)
entries.summary: Explains the Hermetic-law requirement for founding a Tribunal and how a push to carve a new Lotharingian Tribunal out of Normandy and the Rhine can drive a saga, including how vassal covenants and leased legacies are affected.
quotes: In Hermetic law, a Tribunal must consist of twelve or more magi from at least four different covenants.

entries.title: Romantic Saga Structure
entries.summary: Advice on shaping a saga on the chivalric romances, with magi on quests and faerie regiones where knightly behavior is the norm, and on choosing between a physical Grail and a symbolic one.
quotes: If the players wish to explore this path, the troupe should decide on the nature of the quest.

entries.title: Covenants Held Through a Companion Knight
entries.summary: Explains how Normandy covenants cope with feudal land-holding by making a companion the nominal landholder, or by attaching to a monastery, an heiress or widow's manor, or a mercantile front, and what each choice drags into the saga.
quotes: Some have come to embrace a companion as nominal holder of their lands, thereby hoping to evade the problems of land ownership in the feudal system.

entries.title: Duties and Privileges of the Knight
entries.summary: Covers a knight's yearly military service (which may be commuted by paying Ecuage), court attendance, legal duties under Frankish Tribal Law (represented by the Common Law Ability), trial by combat, tournaments and knight errantry.
quotes: Each knight owes military service to his liege forty days every year
the legal system is based on Frankish Tribal Law, and is best represented by the ability Common Law

entries.title: Magi and Mundane Lords: Legal Precedents
entries.summary: Summarizes Normandy Tribunal precedents on living in a mundane lord's castle or manor without being a court wizard, offering magical support as a consors, economic interference, and the legality of mundane raiding that spares labs and libraries.
quotes: The vital aspect is that even if one lives within the actual home of a mundane noble, no vassal relationship exists.
