As mundane resources are not protected under the infamous 1116 ruling, rebellion and mundane raiding is technically legal in the Tribunal, providing that the laboratories and libraries of the magi themselves are not damaged.

related.text: ArM5 p.15 Order of Hermes and nobility

entries.title: Castles as Covenant Sites
entries.summary: Possessing a castle ties a covenant into feudal vassal relationships, requires a landowning knight companion, and counts as a major hook that generates stories and problems.
quotes: Castles are so obvious and party to problems that they are defined as a major hook (Covenants, page 12)

entries.title: Growth of Towns and the Spreading Dominion
entries.summary: Describes how expanding cities convert surrounding wild land into farmland that falls under the Dominion, impairing magic and corroding vis-harvesting sites.
quotes: Each city transforms the land around itself for a distance of twenty miles, gradually converting wild spaces into farmland.
Farmland is usually covered by the Dominion, which impairs magical practice and corrodes vis-harvesting sites.

entries.title: Masks (Disposable Agents)
entries.summary: Defines masks as disposable mundane agents who act for a covenant so the magi can hide their involvement, and gives a simple Intrigue-roll alternative to the complex agent rules in Houses of Hermes: Societates.
quotes: Troupes preferring a simpler system should instead allow characters to use Intrigue rolls to demonstrate the effectiveness of the agents a character can control.

entries.title: Masks for Observing and Controlling Nobles
entries.summary: Categories of agents (administrators, family members, servants, mercenary leaders, visitors, procurers) a covenant can use to watch or sway a nobleman, with the rule that agents need proximity to the noble or his activities.
quotes: A covenant's agent requires proximity either to the noble's person, or to the noble's activities.

entries.title: Vassalage Between Covenants
entries.summary: Describes vassalage as the weak paying the strong for protection, and how rising mundane hostility and the spreading Dominion make good lieges more expensive and weak lieges liabilities.
quotes: Vassalage is a system in which the weak pay the strong for protection

entries.title: Salvirius: Quest-Granted Virtues
entries.requires: Storyguide option: patronage of Salvirius (Boar King's court)
entries.summary: A faerie-court advisor who can grant Virtues to characters by assigning a mystical quest that costs a sacrifice, in the form of taking a Flaw.
quotes: Salvirius can grant Virtues to other characters, through a process whereby he assigns to the character a mystical quest that requires a sacrifice (acquisition of a Flaw).

entries.title: The Children of Odin Mystery Cult
entries.requires: Initiation: Children of Odin Mystery Cult
entries.summary: Describes the small, secretive Children of Odin cult led by Queen Skuld, its power-based philosophy, and the typical membership, including the suggestion that members need a good Ignem score.
quotes: all members should have a relatively good Ignem Art score, which may favor Flambeau, so that they could survive the first Quest to the burning ships (see below)

entries.title: Children of Odin Mystery Scripts and Ordeals
entries.requires: Initiation: Children of Odin Mystery Cult
entries.summary: Lists the Hermetic Virtues granted by the cult's Initiation Scripts and the Flaws that may be taken as Ordeals, including the new Minor Hermetic Flaw Blood Haze.
quotes: The cult currently has Initiation Scripts that grant the following Virtues:
The maga is crazed by bloodshed, and if she is directly involved in a combat situation she has a –10 penalty to Formulaic magic and has a –3 penalty to her Concentration Ability Score.

related.text: ArM5 p.44 Life Boost, Life-Linked Spontaneous Magic

entries.title: The Ships of Flame (Odin Cult Quest Regiones)
entries.requires: Initiation: Children of Odin Mystery Cult
entries.summary: Three small Magical regiones on the Seine, each a burning longship that can only be entered on a particular day by drifting in a burning boat, and which serve as the cult's first Quest with a fire hazard on deck.
quotes: Each Viking longship burns fiercely and inflicts fire damage (+20 each round) on anyone standing upon the deck. This is a magical attack with a Penetration of 30, which may be resisted as normal.
Cult Initiates must (as their first Quest) find their way, unaided, onto the deck of one of the longships and recover an axe from a fallen Viking warrior

entries.title: Rune Magic for the Order of Odin
entries.requires: Storyguide option; Children of Odin Mystery Cult
entries.summary: Optional rule suggestion: if the cult is an authentic heir to the Order of Odin, add rune magic powers to its repertoire, or let a researcher integrate rune magic with Hermetic theory.
quotes: you might like to add to the cult's repertoire some of the rune magic powers described in Ancient Magic (page 133)

entries.title: Masks for Parisian Stories
entries.requires: Covenant of the Normandy Tribunal with agents in Paris
entries.summary: Lists which Normandy covenants have established influence in which sections of Parisian society and explains why proxy battles between masks are now illegal there because Eboris is senex of Paris.
quotes: These disruptions, usually provoked by Tytalus magi, are now illegal because Eboris is the senex of Paris.

entries.title: Masks Within the Church
entries.summary: Notes that churchmen make useful masks because the Church mediates the Divine, and that French churchmen are less tied up with House Jerbiton than churchmen in the east or Italy.

entries.title: Cracking of Old Wards
entries.summary: As the Dominion rises, old magical wards (such as those holding subdued creatures) weaken individually or in clusters, leaving weak auras that spring covenants may colonize.
quotes: Sites that have contained powerful, subdued magical creatures for centuries are likely to have weak auras and be prime sites for colonization by spring covenants.

entries.title: Tytalus Cabals
entries.summary: Explains Tytalus cabals: anonymous clandestine groups formed to pursue a specific tactical goal, whose members may each have different motives.
quotes: to do so they form clandestine organizations called cabals

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Tytalus

entries.title: Tytalus Primus Succession and the Two Primi
entries.summary: States how a Tytalus Primus claims the title and describes the current dispute between two Primi, the three ways it could end, and the approach of the Grand Tribunal as a crisis point.
quotes: The condition of Primus-hood for House Tytalus is that one magus must force the others to accept his right to lead.

entries.title: Young and In Charge: Player-Driven Covenant Saga
entries.summary: Optional setup for troupes who want their characters to decide their own activities in Confluensis: they take over roles of the NPC magi, serve Proctor for a few missions, and then Proctor is removed and replaced by a senior Quaesitor who delegates.
quotes: This can be accommodated with a few simple adjustments.

entries.title: Confluensis Magical Resources and Local Auras
entries.summary: Describes the covenant's strong Magic aura, the tidal vortices harvested for vis on spring tides, and the Orchard island whose aura has shifted from Faerie to Magic with a minor Faerie aura returning on the solstices.
quotes: The island's aura, once Faerie, has gradually been transformed to Magic, although a minor Faerie aura reappears on the solstices.

entries.title: The Tytalus Traitor
entries.summary: A voluntarily exiled Tytalus magus who counts as having lost every conflict and is an untouchable foe in House games. The Traitor's one duty is to restart stalled House conflicts, and they are often placed as Quaesitores or hoplites.
quotes: The Traitor has a single obligation to House Tytalus: to restart the House's conflicts if they stall.

entries.title: Sample Oath of Fealty Between Covenants
entries.summary: Presents a worked example of the terms of an oath of fealty between a liege covenant and its Mercere House vassal, covering mutual aid, voting, tithes, hospitality and non-competition, along with the Tribunal's Evangelium who reports Tourney results.
quotes: Dragon's Rest will pay a tithe of one pawn of vis per year per member to Confluensis.

entries.title: Chapter Houses and Cenobites in Normandy
entries.summary: Shows how the Normandy Peripheral Code treats an outside covenant's chapter house: it is not recognized, so a lone resident magus is a cenobite, and recognition may come only over time.
quotes: Chapter houses are not recognized under the Peripheral Code in the Normandy Tribunal, so the single magus who lives in the Cherbourg covenant is considered a cenobite.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p.82

groups.title: The Theban Tribunal
groups.intro: Rules particular to the Theban Tribunal (The Sundered Eagle).

entries.title: Constantine's Visions: wards of Constantinople
entries.summary: Describes the two ancient Divine wards (Invocation/Cursing effects) that once protected the walls of Constantinople, now disabled, and what would be needed to restore them.
quotes: The Might of Faerie and Infernal creatures within the walls was reduced by 10, with a penetration of 20.
Invaders attempting to storm the walls suffered three additional botch dice on all stress rolls.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.70 (Sol Invictus)

entries.title: The Hermetic Polity
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains the split between executive power held by the citizens and administrative power held by the Council of Magistrates, and how prosecution and judgment of Code breaches differ from other Tribunals.
quotes: The citizens of the polity have all the executive power, whereas the Council of Magistrates has all the administrative power.

entries.title: Origins of the Polity (archai, archon, logothete, polemarch)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Sidebar summarising the Athenian-style polity the Tribunal copies: magistrates chosen at random, serving for limited terms with no executive power, and the offices of archai, archon, logothete and polemarch.
quotes: a council of 16 magistrates who manage the Tribunal's resources, review the law, and investigate cases
Archai are selected at each Tribunal meeting, and serve for seven years at a time.

entries.title: Citizenship: politai and metoikoi
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Defines the two classes of magus in the Tribunal, citizens (politai) and resident foreigners (metoikoi), how civic duty is tracked with tokens, and who may hold office.
quotes: Only politai are entitled to become magistrates.
A foreign magus can become a polites through a citizenship decree of the Tribunal

entries.title: The Phylai (four tribes)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Citizens are divided into four phylai by the covenant where they keep their sanctum, each represented by an equal number of archai; lists the four phylai and their covenants.
quotes: all its politai are divided into four phylai

entries.title: The Council of Magistrates
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Describes the archai as a duty rather than an honor: who serves, how terms are limited, when the Council meets, and how service is compensated with tokens.
quotes: There are 16 archai, four drawn from each of the four phylai
No citizen can serve two consecutive terms as arche

entries.title: Theban Quaesitores
entries.requires: House Guernicus in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains how the Tribunal's polity, not House Guernicus, investigates Code breaches and revises the Peripheral Code, leaving Quaesitores as legal experts and witnesses.
quotes: the polity (in the form of a board of magistrates, see later) conducts investigations into potential breaches of the Code of Hermes, rather than the Quaesitores

entries.title: The Archon
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The archon is chosen by the archai from among themselves, chairs the Council, and holds the Praeco's duties; may serve more than once.
quotes: A magus can serve as archon more than once.

entries.title: The Polemarch
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The polemarch is elected for ability to execute Wizard's Marches and enforce sentences, can award tokens to helpers, and uses Tribunal enchanted devices that restrain a magus.
quotes: There is no limit to the number of times an individual can serve as polemarch

entries.title: The Logothete
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The permanent Chief Redcap who records Council business, keeps the token and shard records and assigns Redcaps; sets out when a new logothete is elected and how Redcaps are barred from votes and sortition.
quotes: The logothete is the Chief Redcap of the Theban Tribunal.

entries.title: The Boards of Magistrates
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains how the Judicial, Legislative and Conciliatory Boards are staffed, convened by citizen application, and what each handles, including interim Tribunals and certamen conventions.
quotes: nominally there are three members of each board, and seven members of the treasury council
The Peripheral Code states that a board must convene within six months of the request
the Judicial Board can also convene an interim Tribunal if they can gather together at least 12 magi from four different covenants

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates pp.90-93 (certamen, debate)

entries.title: The Treasury Council (apodektai)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The seven archai not on a board manage the Tribunal's vis, vis loans, collection of vis and Gifted children, and the tutoring of prospective apprentices.
quotes: This duty typically results in the discovery of about 15 apprentices in total every seven years.
The repayment of vis does not include interest, since usury is a sin.

entries.title: Tokens and Shards
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The Tribunal's social currency: tokens credit service to the polity, shards debit antisocial acts, tokens may neutralize shards for a season of service, and shards expose a citizen to ostracism.
quotes: The principle use of the tokens is neutralization.
Being found guilty of a High Crime (three per crime in addition to any other penalty);
Any citizen possessing one or more shards is liable to the vote of ostracism

entries.title: The Language of Magi (Classical Greek)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Theban magi cast in Classical Greek; gives the language scores needed to read and write Greek Hermetic books and the penalties non-Greek speakers suffer to recognise a spell's Form.
quotes: Non-Greek speakers suffer a –10 to attempts to determine the Form of a magical effect
they need an effective score in that language of 4

entries.title: Common Vis Sources
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Vis from shrines and certain mythic sites belongs to the polity, is gathered by volunteers for a token, and funds Longevity Rituals, items and the Ceremony of Propitiation.
quotes: In total, the Tribunal harvests approximately 50 pawns of vis from such sources each year.

entries.title: Provision of Longevity Rituals
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Each year the Tribunal sponsors one Longevity Ritual for the eligible citizen with the most tokens, who surrenders them; crafting it earns the maker tokens.
quotes: Every year, the Tribunal sponsors a Longevity Ritual for a single Theban magus.
The applicant with the most tokens is chosen; she must surrender all these tokens

entries.title: Provision of Healing
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Customary duty to provide magical healing to a fellow magus, with the healer bearing the vis cost, a customary vis gift in return and a token awarded to the healer.
quotes: by tradition, the gift is usually half the amount that was required for the healing

entries.title: Donation of Apprentices
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Finders of Gifted children must report them to the Treasury Council so the Apprentice Presentation can assign them rather than claiming them directly.
quotes: If a magus discovers a Gifted individual, he has a duty to notify the Treasury Council.

entries.title: The Covenant Patrons
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Every Theban covenant has a supernatural patron in a pact of mutual protection, represented by a Powerful Ally or Local Ally Boon, and the covenant expires if it lacks a patron.
quotes: expressed as either the Powerful Ally Boon or the Local Ally Boon
a covenant without a patron is deemed to have itself expired

entries.title: Other Tasks for the Common Good
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Sidebar listing the extra tasks the Tribunal may ask volunteers to perform, each earning a token on success.
quotes: Any magus who volunteers and successfully completes the job is awarded a token.

entries.title: Gifts of Vis
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Describes informal customs of gifting vis for hospitality and healing, the etiquette penalties for stinginess or hoarding, and the ban on trading tokens or shards for vis.
quotes: The exchange of tokens or shards, the true "currency" of the Tribunal, for vis is not permitted.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.85

entries.title: The Ceremony of Propitiation
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Procedure at Delos by which covenants offer vis or treasure to their patrons, which grants the patron experience offset by its Might, with vis offered counting like eaten vis.
quotes: Any patron who is propitiated in the rite gains 25 experience points
reducing the penalty due to the patron's Might by two points per pawn

entries.title: The Founding of Covenants
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Requirements for founding a Theban covenant: a declared purpose, a willing patron at the site and a charter reviewed by the Conciliatory Board, then a decree of founding at Tribunal.
quotes: a prospective covenant needs a patron at the proposed site of the new covenant

entries.title: The Tribunal Meeting
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Overview of the septennial meeting on Delos: its four phases in fixed order and the rotation of the principal phyle that organises it.
quotes: It is divided into four phases, each of which fulfills a different state function.

entries.title: Pre-Tribunal Procedure
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The organising phyle prepares the housing on Delos before the meeting.

entries.title: Selection of Archai Candidates
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Each phyle compiles its candidate list of eligible citizens; refusing consent when eligible costs a shard.
quotes: a magus who is eligible for selection but refuses consent is given one shard

entries.title: Interviews with Apprentices
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Before the Tribunal, masters without shards may question Gifted children and bid for them by gifting tokens; Bonisagus may claim any child.
quotes: Bonisagus magi may immediately claim any of the presented apprentices.

entries.title: The Hermetic Assembly
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: First phase of the Tribunal: voting by sigils on Conciliatory Board decrees, where all magi present vote and a majority carries a decree.
quotes: All decrees are passed by a majority vote of those magi present.

entries.title: Decrees of Citizenship
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: How a metoikos petitions the Assembly for citizenship, with required contribution, resident covenant and an arche sponsor.
quotes: have at least one arche as sponsor

entries.title: Decrees of Defamation
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: A citizen can accuse another of acting against the polity's unity; success gives the accused a shard, failure gives one to the accuser.
quotes: If the Assembly finds in favor of the decree, then the accused is credited with one shard.

entries.title: Decrees of Contrition
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: A shard-bearing magus may offer reparation and apology to have the shard removed; the offering's size is the magus's own choice and is kept if the plea fails.
quotes: The magnitude of the reparation is determined by the magus himself.

entries.title: The Apprentice Presentation
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Formal assignment of Gifted children to masters by tokens gathered in the interviews, complaints against masters, token rewards for training without abuse, and the effect on apprenticeship length.
quotes: magi are awarded tokens for training an apprentice without abuse, one for the first seven years and another at Gauntlet

entries.title: Ostrakismos (ostracism)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Closing business of the Assembly: citizens holding shards may be voted as candidates, the majority name on potsherds is ostracised and exiled from the Tribunal for a time.
quotes: He cannot return to Thebes for seven years

entries.title: The Nature of the Law
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The Theban Code contains only deliberate legislation, with no precedent from earlier rulings.
quotes: Each case is judged according to the Code and with no reference to previous rulings.

entries.title: The Law Council
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Second phase: review of the Peripheral Code, debate between the two archai, and the option of a pre-emptive review of a law one expects to be convicted under.
quotes: if the alternative is accepted, the change to the Peripheral Code is recorded

entries.title: The People's Court
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Third phase: trial of Hermetic crimes with archai as prosecution and defense principals, a vote on guilt only, and the polemarch's power to prevent flight.
quotes: The polemarch is empowered by the Peripheral Code to prevent the flight of a guilty party by any means

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.56-61

entries.title: Execution of Sentences
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Punishments are proposed in decreasing severity and voted on; shards accompany every conviction, tokens reward the prosecuting arche, and Marches never occur on Delos.
quotes: All punishments are accompanied by a penalty of three shards for a High Crime or one for a Low Crime.
A Wizard's March is never conducted on Delos

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.60

entries.title: Conduct of Archai
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Any citizen can accuse an arche or the polemarch of dereliction and propose a shard fine, decided by two votes.
quotes: a proposed fine of one to seven shards

entries.title: Sortition of Archai
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: How the new archai are drawn by lot from each phyle's candidate list and assigned to boards, and token payment for outgoing officers.
quotes: The logothete then selects four tokens from the jar at random

entries.title: Election of the Archon and Polemarch
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: The archai elect the archon by show of hands and then vote on nominated polemarch candidates; only a previous polemarch may refuse.
quotes: Only a magus who has already served as polemarch can refuse the role.

entries.title: Hermetic Correspondence
entries.summary: Theban magi write rhetorical letters hiding their purpose in tales of their patrons; composing and reading such a letter is resolved with Lore-based rolls against an Ease Factor.
quotes: A Com + relevant Lore roll should be made against an Ease Factor of 6 to encapsulate a relatively straightforward message
An Int + relevant Lore roll against the same Ease Factor should be made to discern the rhetorical purpose of the story.

entries.title: The Color Purple (Shape & Material bonuses)
entries.summary: True imperial purple (murex dye or porphyry) is reserved for emperors and carries enchanting Shape & Material bonuses for royalty, rulership and control of people.
quotes: True purple, either porphyry or the Byzantine dye, has the following Shape & Material bonuses: +10 royalty, +7 rulership and authority, +5 control people.

entries.title: The Dynatoi as Player Characters
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Suggests Virtues and Flaws that fit a character from the dispossessed Byzantine nobility.
quotes: Such a character is likely to have the Privileged Upbringing Virtue to represent his former status.

entries.title: Taxation (kommerkion)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Byzantine lands
entries.summary: Describes the Byzantine tax system, including the flat tax on goods sold within the empire.
quotes: All goods sold throughout the empire are taxed at the rate of 10%

entries.title: Coinage
entries.requires: Saga set in the Byzantine lands
entries.summary: Gives the Byzantine and Venetian coin denominations and their values in Mythic pounds and pence.
quotes: One bezant is thus worth 20 grossos.

entries.title: The Alaphroiskiotoi
entries.summary: Folklore holds that those born on a Saturday have a light shadow, usually represented by Second Sight, Dowsing or Magic Sensitivity, and special power over vrykolakes.
quotes: Most alaphroiskiotoi have the Second Sight Virtue, although others possess Dowsing or Magic Sensitivity instead

entries.title: Adelphopoiesis (ritual brotherhood)
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: A ceremony of brotherhood that makes each adelphos a Sympathetic Connection to the other, represented by the True Love/True Friend Virtue or Flaw.
quotes: An adelphos who has undergone this rite becomes a Sympathetic Connection to his adopted brother

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.120 (Cult of Orpheus)

entries.title: The Power of Oaths
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: An oath-breaker may be called out at the place of the oath so a river spirit enforces it, resolved with an Oath Invocation roll against an Ease Factor.
quotes: Oath Invocation Roll: Communication + Charm + simple die (+6 if Styx is invoked)
Ease Factor: 15 + simple die

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 (Invoking a Saint)

entries.title: Punishments for Oath-Breaking
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Oath-breakers are punished with imposed Flaws or maledictions; sidebar lists sample lesser and greater maledictions.
quotes: Major Flaws are imposed by powerful entities with a Might of 40 or greater, otherwise the punishment is usually a Minor Flaw.
When the character uses a tool or weapon, roll a simple die; on a 1 or 2 it breaks.

entries.title: The Bridge of Arta (Infernal aura and Greedy trait)
entries.summary: An Infernal-aura bridge that temporarily raises or grants the Greedy Personality Trait in anyone who crosses it.
quotes: It has a perfidious Infernal aura of 2
Any who cross the bridge have their Greedy Personality Trait increased by two, or gain it with a score of 2, until the following day.

entries.title: Mount Athos: Divine auras and the ban on females
entries.summary: Lists the graded Divine aura levels of the Holy Mountain and the ward that keeps females, human or animal, off the promontory.
quotes: The whole promontory has a Divine aura of 5, with the monasteries and cells often reaching 7, the altars 8, and certain holy spots on Mount Athos itself 9.
Nothing female, either animal or human, is able to set foot upon this holy land

entries.title: Mount Olympos: Immortals' Mushrooms and the Realm above the Clouds
entries.summary: Speckled mushrooms on Olympos' slopes can aid an Aging roll, and the mountain's Faerie regio leads to a high-aura realm guarded by the three Horae where magi may study or seek Mystery initiations.
quotes: a character may receive a –3 bonus to his Aging roll for that year
has a Faerie aura of 10

entries.title: The Temptations of Christ (Tower of the Devil ordeal)
entries.requires: Attempting an ascent of the Pyrgos Diavolou at Meteora, e.g. as a Mystery initiation ordeal
entries.summary: A forty-day ordeal on the Tower of the Devil in which the hermit faces three temptations mirroring Christ's, with fatal or Infernal consequences if he yields; suggested as an initiation ordeal.
quotes: Over the course of forty days and nights, the duration of Christ's time in the desert, he is tormented by the vultures.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, page 85 (Infernal Blessing)

entries.title: Studying with a Lamia (Palace of the Lamia)
entries.requires: Being taken in by a lamia (Gulf of Corinth)
entries.summary: A magus may be taken to a lamia's underwater palace and taught secrets; a dangerous route to learning, and many lamiae can initiate Mystery Virtues.
quotes: Many lamiae are capable of initiating Mystery Virtues, for example.

entries.title: The Cult of Eleusis (Eleusinian Mysteries)
entries.requires: Initiation: Eleusinian Mysteries (sponsor required; Greek, no blood guilt)
entries.summary: Describes how a character is sponsored into and initiated in the Eleusinian Mystery cult at Eleusis, with a Lesser Mystery held yearly and a Greater Mystery held less often, and what Virtues each may grant.
quotes: Initiation into the Lesser Mystery occurs once a year in March, and grants the Virtue Self-Confident
The Greater Mystery is initiated once every five years, at the end of August. It may grant the Death Prophecy Virtue

entries.title: The Blood of Medusa (healing blood, vis, Longevity Ritual bonus)
entries.requires: Access to the Blood of Medusa at Epidauros
entries.summary: A renewable vis source whose blood heals wounds and diseases when drunk in quantity, and gives a Lab Total bonus when a small dose is used in crafting a Longevity Ritual.
quotes: If copiously drunk, the imbiber's Incapacitating Wounds are immediately reduced to Heavy and all later Recovery rolls for all current wounds succeed automatically.
If a smaller dose of the blood (4 pawns) is used in the crafting of a Longevity Ritual, +12 is gained to the Lab Total.

entries.title: The Hall of Repose at Epidauros (Longevity Ritual laboratory)
entries.summary: Describes the Hall of Repose, a shared laboratory specialized for longevity and healing that is used whenever a Tribunal-funded Longevity Ritual is made.
quotes: It may be used whenever a Tribunal-funded Longevity Ritual is created; the recipient is required to sleep in the hall.

entries.title: Asklepios as patron: sleeping in the Hall of Repose
entries.requires: Sleeping in the Hall of Repose at Epidauros
entries.summary: Sleepers in the Hall of Repose may receive healing visions and bonuses to Wound Recovery rolls and to the Lab Total of a Longevity Ritual crafted for them there.
quotes: Sleepers here also gain +12 to their next Wound Recovery roll and a +6 bonus to the Lab Total if a Longevity Rituals is crafted for them here.

entries.title: The Terrae Cult at Hedyosmos (Cult of the Earth)
entries.requires: Initiation: Terrae Cult (threskeia geine), headed by House Guernicus
entries.summary: Describes the Theban chapter of the Terrae Cult, listing the Virtues its Initiation Scripts confer, typical Ordeal Flaws, and a Terram-aligned variant of the Summoning Virtue that is not Infernal.
quotes: The threskeia geine of Hedyosmos has Initiation Scripts for the following Virtues:
it can instead summon any creature with a Magic Might that is aligned to the Form of Terram
When summoning elementals, the character must use the scouring mechanic to create the elemental de novo.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, pages 36 & 68
Realms of Power: The Infernal, pages 114-115

entries.title: Lesbos: reversed gender roles and character creation
entries.summary: Natives of Lesbos live in a society where women hold higher status than men, so characters who have not adjusted to other regions' gender roles are advised to take the Social Handicap Flaw, and certain Virtues are very common.
quotes: should take the Social Handicap Flaw
The Enchanting Music and Free Expression Virtues are very common.

entries.title: Delos Today: Restless aura and the ban on births and deaths
entries.requires: Visiting Delos (site of the Theban Tribunal)
entries.summary: Explains the floating island's Magic aura levels, the Restless Personality Trait it imposes on everyone present, its wandering route, and the prohibitions on births, deaths, pregnant women and predatory animals during Tribunal.
quotes: imposing the Personality Trait of Restless +1 on anyone who sets foot on the island (where the aura is greater than 3, this trait rises to +2)
The whole island has a Magic aura of 3

related.text: Chapter 3: The Order of Hermes, The Ceremony of Propitiation

entries.title: The Tribunal Treasury on Delos
entries.summary: Describes the Tribunal's vis and artifact treasury, who holds its key, how it is guarded, and the spontaneous magical effects caused by the stored vis.
quotes: may only be opened with a large iron key that is entrusted to the archon

entries.title: Aegaea's underwater Faerie regio
entries.summary: Describes the underwater Faerie regio where mortals can breathe, work and move as if in air, and the Faerie aura of its top level.
quotes: Inside the regio, the top level has a Faerie aura of 8.
mortals can breathe unhindered, ink dries on parchment, and fires can even be lit

entries.title: Warping from living in Aegaea's Faerie aura
entries.summary: Notes that magi who stay long in the covenant's potent Faerie aura and eat or use faerie goods, unless of House Merinita, accumulate Warping rapidly.
quotes: is a rapid accumulation of Warping

entries.title: Dryops: a patron that pays Might for regiones
entries.summary: Explains how the covenant's spirit patron created the ships' regiones at a permanent cost to its own Might, and the debt this creates for the covenant.
quotes: Every time the spirit uses its Regio power, it permanently loses 15 points from its Might.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, pages 52 and 103

entries.title: The Enchanted Ships of Favonius (ship statistics and bonuses)
entries.summary: Gives the Quality, Size, damage levels and navigation and ship-handling bonuses of the covenant's four enchanted ships, and notes they are bought with the Magical Fortress Boon without spending Build Points on enchantments.
quotes: Because of the quality of workmanship, pilots receive a +2 to any navigation rolls, and captains receive a +2 bonus to any ship-handling rolls.
These ships are bought with the Magical Fortress Boon, and their enchantments do not cost covenant Build Points.

entries.title: Ingasia's Forge of Hephaistos laboratory bonuses
entries.summary: The covenant's central forge has been converted into a shared Hermetic laboratory specialized for Rego magic and for creating enchanted items, within a Magic aura.
quotes: specialized to provide a +8 bonus to Rego magic and a +5 bonus to creating enchanted items

entries.title: Limits on sales of enchanted items to mundanes (Stouritus)
entries.summary: Within a magus' description, explains the Order's only rule on selling enchanted items to mundanes and the number allowed per year in the Theban Tribunal, and that Items of Quality do not count against it.
quotes: The Order's only rule concerning the sale of enchanted items is that magi must use intermediaries when selling to mundanes
Items of Quality (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults, page 124) are not enchanted items per se

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults, page 124

entries.title: Constantinople's Auras (layered, fluctuating realm auras)
entries.summary: Explains how Divine, Infernal, Faerie and Magic auras overlap in Constantinople, why most Divine auras are Dominion auras tied to worshipers, how auras vary with the calendar and meet at borders, and that Magic auras are no longer maintained.
quotes: Most of the Divine auras are Dominion rather than empyreal auras, meaning that their strength and size are determined by the number of faithful worshipers.
In places where auras of different realms but equal strength meet, they form a border and rest against each other.

entries.title: The Column of Theodosius: prophetic visions and Premonitions
entries.requires: Visiting the Forum of Theodosius; Supernatural Ability: Premonitions to understand or study
entries.summary: Anyone gazing at the column for an hour gets a vision, which only a character with Premonitions can interpret with a roll, and those with Premonitions can also study the column as a limited-use Source Quality.
quotes: succeeding with an Intelligence + Premonitions vs. an Ease Factor set by the storyguide (12 is a good start)
The column may also be studied by those with Premonitions, acting as a Source Quality of 6.

entries.title: The Serpent Column: vis procedure, snake ward and regio
entries.summary: Gives the ritual of sacrifices through which the column yields vis, its ward against ordinary snakes, and how to enter the Faerie regio above it.
quotes: Four times a year, at the solstices and equinoxes, a ram must be sacrificed and its blood poured into the bronze chalice, where it is consumed by the column.
Snakes with a Might score are unfazed by the ward.

entries.title: The Egyptian Obelisk: divination roll and Ease Factor
entries.summary: A character may read the obelisk's engravings to divine the future with a roll against a fixed Ease Factor, handled as Hermetic Divination, and the Ease Factor falls if missing pieces are recovered.
quotes: A character may divine the future with an Intelligence + Magic Lore + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 15.
Finding the other two missing thirds of the obelisk reduces the Ease Factor by 3 for each found piece, so a complete obelisk lowers it to 9.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, pages 59-62 (Hermetic Divination)

entries.title: Haghia Sophia: auras and the healing Column of St. Gregory
entries.summary: Lists the Dominion and Infernal aura levels inside the Great Church and a surviving relic column that improves Recovery rolls and shortens wound healing.
quotes: providing a +6 bonus to Recovery Rolls and decreasing the healing time of a wound by one level
The nave has an Infernal aura of 7

entries.title: The Porphyry Chamber: born in the purple (status and succession)
entries.requires: Born in the Porphyry Chamber (Byzantine imperial family)
entries.summary: Explains the Byzantine custom giving children born in the purple chamber a better claim to the throne than older siblings, and the social consequences and restrictions that follow.
quotes: children born to a reigning emperor and empress outrank older siblings born before the succession to the throne.
Being porphyrogennetos gives a character a claim to the imperial throne, a good education, and the support of the people.

entries.title: Porphyrogenitos: supernatural Virtue table for characters born in the purple
entries.requires: Character born in the Porphyry Chamber, Constantinople
entries.summary: A character born in the Porphyry Chamber gains a free Minor Supernatural Virtue whose realm is determined by a die roll, with a small chance of a Major Virtue instead.
quotes: If a character is born in the chamber, the storyguide should roll a simple die and consult the following:

entries.title: St. Loukia's icon: study source and Magic aura at Xylinites
entries.requires: Covenant of Xylinites (icon of St. Loukia)
entries.summary: Within the covenant's history, describes an icon whose meditation can serve as a summa for a Supernatural Ability and which radiates a spherical Magic aura limited by the Dominion aura.
quotes: meditation on her icon can function as a Level 3, Quality 10 summa for learning the Supernatural Ability Animal Ken
A Magic aura of strength 3 emanates from it in a perfect sphere

entries.title: Vantage Point of Xerxes (bound druj site)
entries.requires: Location: Vantage Point of Xerxes, Hellespont
entries.summary: An artificial hill above the Hellespont that grants enhanced vision to anyone standing on it, at the price of exposure to the Obsession power of the Infernal druj bound beneath it.
quotes: The hill has an Infernal aura of 3.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, page 31 (Obsession)

entries.title: The Great Altar of Pergamos (free ritual spells)
entries.summary: A Faerie-aura altar that powers any Hermetic ritual spell cast from atop it without vis expenditure, at the cost of tainted botches and odd side effects.
quotes: it will supply the supernatural power to empower any ritual spell cast by a Hermetic magus
Botched spells are tainted, as if the caster used faerie-tainted vis

entries.title: The Prison of Klymene (altar bond strength)
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining that the altar is the lock on a bound titan, and that each ritual cast through it wears down the bond's strength until the titan is freed.
quotes: The imprisoning bonds have a strength of 50, which renews itself at the beginning of each year.
If the bond strength is reduced to zero in a single year, the great altar cracks in half and Klymene is released.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, page 109 (Kosmokrator Spirit)

entries.title: The Cave of the Seven Sleepers (dilated-time regio)
entries.requires: Location: Cave of the Seven Sleepers, near Ephesus
entries.summary: A Divine-aura pilgrimage cave that still hides a Magic regio with dilated time, tempting vis harvesters who cannot predict how much time will pass outside.
quotes: It has a Magic aura of 6 and has dilated time (Covenants, page 7).

entries.title: Anima damage levels and repair (glass submarine)
entries.summary: Stat block of an awakened iron simulacrum, with the special rule that it tracks Damage Levels like a commercial product rather than Wound Penalties, and can only be repaired by a character with Mechanica or Automata.
quotes: Roll the anima's Stamina (+1) plus a stress die against an Ease Factor equal to the excess damage.
If a character has one of these Abilities, she can repair a number of Damage Levels equal to her score in a season.

entries.title: Mythic Blood: Gigantes (Greek giants)
entries.summary: A Mythic Blood lineage for descendants of the Greek giants with snake tails, listing the typical Magical Focus, Personality Flaw and common Virtues and Flaws, plus two new Flaws (Rebellious and Horrifying Appearance - Snake Legs).
quotes: The Magical Focus that accompanies the Mythic Blood is usually connected with strength or the Form of Terram, and the Personality Flaw is Rebellious.

entries.title: The Sibyls (magic humans bound to their auras)
entries.summary: Overview of the sibyls as ancient immortal magic humans who each dwell in a powerful Magic aura or regio and risk losing their powers through Acclimation if they leave it.
quotes: Each sibyl rests in a powerful Magic aura or regio, and cannot leave without risking losing her prophetic powers

entries.title: The Sibyllides (children of sibyls)
entries.summary: Describes the children of sibyls as magic kin who always have prophecy- or sight-related powers and who must report back to their mother periodically.
quotes: They are obligated to return to their mother's home every decade to report to her what they have learned about the world

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, page 89 (magic kin)
Realms of Power: Magic, page 95 (Warders of Mystery)

entries.title: Character Guide: A Sibyl (magic character template)
entries.requires: Being type: Magic Human / Magic character
entries.summary: A minimal-statistics template for a sibyl built with the Magic Characters rules, with notes on the five points of Virtues and Flaws, Magic Might, and the Enigmatic Essential Trait that prevents her speaking clearly.
quotes: The sibyl's Enigmatic Personality Trait is an Essential Trait; magical effects to make her speak clearly mysteriously fail.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 7 (Divination & Augury)

entries.title: Heroic descent: Virtues and Flaws of Greek heroes
entries.requires: Virtue: Mythic Blood or Hero's Birthright Power
entries.summary: Lists famous Greek heroes and the Virtues and Flaws their descendants are likely to inherit, as guidance for building heroic bloodlines.
quotes: His descendants are highly likely to have a Greater Immunity to Metal and the Fury Flaw.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, page 105 (Hero's Birthright)

entries.title: The Children of Olympos (league and its Mysteries)
entries.summary: Describes the Hermetic league that channels Greek gods and the two Mysteries its leader invented for it, explaining how a channeled god can eventually overcome the recipient.
quotes: Lucian has invented two Mysteries for his followers: Elysian Ecstasy and Olympian Pact.

entries.title: Channeling a Greek god (Elysian Ecstasy and Olympian Pact)
entries.requires: Initiation: Elysian Ecstasy (Minor) or Olympian Pact (Major)
entries.summary: Rules for the roll to channel a Greek god, with a table of Ease Factors giving Personality Trait bonuses, Sympathy Trait points and (for Olympian Pact) access to the god's powers, plus the preparation hours, failure cost and duration.
quotes: Channeling a Greek God: (Characteristic) + Faerie Lore + stress die + aura
A character may spend additional hours in this frenetic state, with each additional hour adding +1 to his die roll.
A character gains Sympathy Traits, Personality Traits, and powers (for Olympian Pact) for a number of hours equal to the total rolled.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie, pages 102-105 (Sympathy Traits)
Realms of Power: Magic, page 88 (Spiritual Pact)

entries.title: Initiation of Elysian Ecstasy
entries.summary: The Initiation Script for Elysian Ecstasy, with its Ease Factor, Script Bonus and the twelve boons from beings representing the Olympians.
quotes: The initiate must visit 12 powerful beings, each one chosen to represent one of the 12 Olympians, and receive a boon from each.

entries.title: Sympathy Traits of the Olympians
entries.summary: Table of the positive and negative Sympathy Traits for each Olympian god, for characters taking the Faerie God variant of Faerie Blood.
quotes: Characters taking the Faerie God variant of Faerie Blood

entries.title: Stoicheia (place-guardian faeries)
entries.requires: Being type: Stoicheion (faerie spirit of place)
entries.summary: Overview of the Greek spirits of places and the kinds they take (koukouvaounes, basiliskoi, pergalioi, kalotyches), with the powers and wards typical of each.
quotes: Like portunes, the basiliskoi usually have a Focus Power for Domestic Work.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, page 106 (genii loci)

entries.title: Character Guide: Stoicheion (faerie guardian template)
entries.summary: A faerie character template with its Virtue and Flaw budget and powers, including the Guardian of the Bounds ward power with its Might cost and the Extended Glamour vis yield.
quotes: The power costs 1 Might point per 5 levels (or fraction) of the equivalent spell.
The area controlled by the faerie can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of Animal vis, which manifests as physical objects within the controlled region.

entries.title: Magic and the Church in Byzantine cities
entries.summary: Guidance on how Byzantine mobs and Church authorities react to visible magic, amulets and sorcery, and which Holy Magic traditions appear in the Tribunal.
quotes: The Gentle Gift is an invaluable attribute in the urban areas of the Theban Tribunal.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, pages 38, 70, 140-142

entries.title: Byzantine Saints: invoking a saint and common powers
entries.summary: Describes the Orthodox veneration of saints, the roll for invoking a saint's intercession, and a set of powers commonly used by Greek saints.
quotes: Communication + Charm + modifier + simple die vs. 15 + simple die
The petitioner does not need to eat or sleep for a number of days equal to the saint's Divine Might

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, pages 87-88

entries.title: Creating and venerating divine icons (eikons)
entries.summary: How a cleric paints an eikon with an Aesthetic Quality, how that quality becomes a bonus to saintly intercession, and the emergency veneration roll.
quotes: Aesthetic Quality: Dexterity + Craft (Painting) + bonuses
The bonus is equal to the Aesthetic Quality divided by 5 (round up).
Emergency Veneration Roll: Presence + Concentration vs Ease Factor 15

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, pages 41, 87

entries.title: Holy Tradition: Hesychasts
entries.summary: Gives the favored Abilities of ascetic and monastic hesychasts for the Holy Tradition rules, and notes their proneness to Divine Gloom.
quotes: Meditation, Purity, Transcendence, Understanding
Ceremony, Meditation, Transcendence, Understanding

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, page 63 (Divine Gloom)

entries.title: Society of Cyprian and Justina
entries.requires: Tradition: Holy Society of Cyprian and Justina
entries.summary: Gives the favored Abilities of this Holy Society of repentant magicians who serve the Divine.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Holy Magic, Invocation, Sense Holy/Unholy and Wonders

entries.title: The Relics of Constantinople (Faith Scores)
entries.summary: Sidebar on the great relics of Constantinople, giving each a Faith Score, powers and the guidance that relics should motivate characters rather than start in play.
quotes: A fragment of the True Cross that is as large as a man's leg has a Faith Score of 10, giving it 10 Faith Points and a Divine Might of 100.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, page 35 (Powerful Relic)

entries.title: Non-Divine icons and veneration versus worship
entries.summary: Explains false icons aligned with other Realms and how veneration differs from worship, and says to model such icons as supernatural creatures with Might and powers.
quotes: They are therefore best represented as supernatural creatures with a Might score and powers.

entries.title: Three Symbols of Divine Authority (imperial regalia)
entries.summary: The emperor's battle standard, crown and hagka icon, which together extend his Divine commanding aura, give Discipline and Morale bonuses to friendly soldiers and spread Magic Resistance.
quotes: This effectively grants a +3 bonus to any Discipline and Morale tests friendly soldiers have to make.
By itself it confers a Magic Resistance of 10 to the bearer.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, pages 42-43

entries.title: A Mother's Curse
entries.summary: A storyguide tool letting a mother curse her child with an effect like the Lesser Malediction Flaw until he completes a task or receives divine intervention.
quotes: he suffers a –3 penalty to all rolls involving that activity

entries.title: Greek Saints (saint categories and Divine Might)
entries.summary: Sidebar recalling the three categories of saint and their Divine Might, with lists of notable Greater, Area and Local saints of the Greek Church.
quotes: Greater saints have a Divine Might of 75, area saints a Divine Might of 50, and local saints a Divine Might of 25.

entries.title: Infernal Tradition: Stringla
entries.summary: Rules for the Byzantine stringla witch tradition: favored Abilities, common Virtues and Flaws, the Infernal Blessing rite and three extra powers granted by a maleficium cast by the coven leader.
quotes: Ceremony, Debauchery, Effusion, Phantasm
This maleficium is level 25 (base 4, +1 Touch, +4 Forsaken), granting the stringla a supernatural ability.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pages 85-86, 129 (Strigae)

entries.title: Infernal Tradition: The Paulicians
entries.summary: Describes the Paulician heretical sect secretly serving the Infernal and lists its favored Abilities.
quotes: Ceremony, Debauchery, Diablerie, Malediction

groups.title: The Transylvanian Tribunal
groups.intro: Rules particular to the Transylvanian Tribunal (Against the Dark).

entries.title: A Note on Oppida
entries.summary: Explains that in Transylvania a covenant is a legal membership class while an oppidum is the physical camp where magi of several covenants live together, and that oppida are independent rather than subordinate chapter houses.
quotes: The five covenants of this Tribunal are more like classes of citizenship than the covenants of the West.

entries.title: The Praeco
entries.summary: Describes how the Transylvanian Praeco is chosen and removed, and how that office relates to the Prima of Tremere, who actually sets policy.
quotes: Praecohood in Transylvania is not earned by age; it is assigned by a democratic vote.

entries.title: Oppida and Aediles
entries.summary: Gives the binding Tribunal rulings on oppida membership (minimum size, mandatory cives, mixed Houses) and explains the aedile, the odd-man-out member with a right of emergency audience.
quotes: No oppidum may have members exclusively from one House.
In oppida with even numbers of cives and non-cives, there are two aediles.

entries.title: Regulating Magical Settlement & Residency
entries.summary: Explains the written privilege each resident magus agrees with the Praeco, the five broad privilege styles, and the five legally persisting covenants that membership maps onto.
quotes: Each privilege permits membership of at least one of the five covenants.

entries.title: Public Financier
entries.summary: Explains the Praeco's role in collecting and distributing taxes for Tribunal-approved projects, and which privileged groups must give reasonable aid.
quotes: The Praeco collects and distribute taxes for a range of projects that the Tribunal has approved.

entries.title: Stipends
entries.summary: Describes how the Praeco collects and delivers the stipends paid to Redcaps and Quaesitores.
quotes: The Praeco also collects the stipends given to the Redcaps and Quaesitores, and distributes them.

entries.title: Promissory Notes
entries.summary: Explains the older system of promissory notes the Praeco issues against reserved vis income, which also circulate as a high-value currency.
quotes: Promissory notes are still issued, and some ancient notes are still traded, having never been redeemed, because they act as a high-value currency.

entries.title: Quaesitores in Transylvania
entries.summary: Describes the extra powers Transylvanian Quaesitores hold compared with other Tribunals and how Tremere block voting shapes their role.
quotes: Powers some Quaesitors have been seeking in other Tribunals, to levy taxes and demand aid against renounced wizards, have been granted them here.

entries.title: Annual Emergency Tribunals
entries.summary: Explains that Quaesitores here call emergency Tribunals every year, how Tremere proxies decide the vote, and why concessions are made that other Tribunals would not allow.
quotes: Quaesitores are permitted to call emergency Tribunals to deal with legal matters in all Tribunals, but only in Transylvania do they call them annually.

entries.title: Wizard's War in Transylvania
entries.summary: Covers local custom on Wizard's War: Wizards' Marches approved by emergency Tribunal are preferred, personal Wars are rare, and mediation then certamen are the usual ways to settle disputes.
quotes: Transylvanian magi retain their right, under the Code of Hermes, to capriciously declare War.
Those who cannot agree perform certamen.

entries.title: Certamen is a Direct Proxy For War
entries.summary: Describes the Transylvanian convention that a certamen challenge stands in for a Wizard's War, with the loser treated as spared by the victor's mercy and the victor allowed one blow to the face.
quotes: Certamen is used in this Tribunal as a direct proxy for Wizard's War.
a Transylvanian magus victorious in certamen is permitted to physically strike his opponent in the face once.

entries.title: Certamen for Love
entries.summary: Lists the declarations duelists must make before witnesses and the prohibitions that apply (no vis, no spells or items to affect the outcome, no striking as a victory mark) for friendly certamen duels fought for love.
quotes: Duelists for love must clearly state, before at least two witnesses whom the Tribunal could question:
Use vis during the duel.

entries.title: Diplomacy
entries.summary: Explains that many oppida may not make treaties with foreign covenants or Tribunals and that commercial deals must be entered in the Peripheral Code or approved by the Praeco and witnessed by a Quaesitor.
quotes: Many oppida are forbidden to enter treaties with foreign covenants or Tribunals.

entries.title: Recruitment
entries.summary: Restricts importing Gifted children and inviting settler magi: magi must instead ask the Praeco to invite or buy in a particular person.
quotes: Magi may not import Gifted children into the Tribunal, or invite magi as settlers.

entries.title: Vis & Magic Item Sales
entries.summary: Explains the ban on most magi selling vis or magic items (and many magical animals) to outsiders, the exceptions, and the Old Histria system of record with notarized letters and the Praeco's right to act as buyer.
quotes: Most Transylvanian magi are forbidden to sell vis or magic items to outsiders.

entries.title: Asclepius and the Privileges of the Coloniae
entries.summary: Lists what coloniae (young settler magi from other Tribunals) may expect and may not do under their privilege, including office, apprentices and visitors.
quotes: The coloniae, or settlers, are young magi from other Tribunals permitted to develop underutilized sections of the Tribunal, under tight agreements.

entries.title: Triumph of Asclepius
entries.summary: Describes the annually elected leadership of the Covenant of Asclepius and the yearly payment and minor duties that go with it.
quotes: This includes 16 pawns of vis, three pounds of pure gold, six requested books copied from a certain library, a fine dinner, and several other minor tokens of esteem.

entries.title: Coeris and the Privileges of the Cives
entries.requires: Privilege: cives (Covenant of Coeris), automatic for House Tremere
entries.summary: Lists what citizens (cives) of the Covenant of Coeris are permitted and required to do, including House Tremere's assistance, standing for any office, and selecting the aedile.
quotes: A cives, or citizen, is usually a Tremere magus living as a Tremere magus should.

entries.title: Domostron and the Privileges of the Socii
entries.summary: Lists what socii (allied non-Tremere magi such as Redcaps, Quaesitores and hoplites) may do and must do under their privilege, including office, support and aedile selection.
quotes: All Redcaps, Quaestiores, and dedicated hoplites are automatically socii, if they are not civitates.

entries.title: Diodorus and the Privileges of the Hospites
entries.summary: Lists what hospites (magi hired to practise particular skills for House Tremere) may expect and which actions need permission, such as new apprentices, familiars and talismans.
quotes: Hospites are usually required to seek permission before:
They have few rights, but are paid well for their services.

entries.title: Pannonia and the Privileges of the Foederati
entries.summary: Describes foederati, magi of foreign covenants admitted to the Tribunal under individually negotiated agreements, and the usual rights and permission requirements in those agreements.
quotes: Foederati have individually negotiated agreements, but usually they include the right to:

entries.title: Decorations
entries.summary: Describes the decorations worn by Transylvanian magi for service to the Tribunal, what earns each one, and that a decoration is never awarded twice and is replaced by a higher one.
quotes: Decorations are not repeated.
Parsley: This decoration is awarded for landing the mortal blow upon a magus expelled from the Order by the Tribunal.

entries.title: Legalities of Residency
entries.summary: Explains why a magus's privilege is rarely challenged as against the Code, that leaving the Tribunal is allowed, and the competing legal views on whether a broken privilege must be repaid.
quotes: A magus can leave the Tribunal at any time.

entries.title: Co-option
entries.summary: Describes how House Tremere gets others to want what it wants and lists the key political tools (Advocacy, Aiding Emulants, Always Keeping Deals, Defining Normal, Direct Acculturation, Information, Latin, Non-Hermetic Actors, Prosperity) a character can use to lead on issues.
quotes: House Tremere coopts when it can, acting either as leader on an issue, or supporting those magi who are working toward a co-interest.
Players trying to use their characters as leaders on issues should familiarize themselves with the key tools used by House Tremere.

entries.title: House Tremere Reputation (Soft Power)
entries.summary: Optional rule: the troupe may set a Reputation score for House Tremere for characters acting on its behalf, which rises as soft-power stories succeed and falls through foolish or unjustified acts.
quotes: The troupe may to select a Reputation score for House Tremere which a character acting on the House's behalf may use.

entries.title: Tremere Apprentices
entries.summary: Describes the House Tremere custom of exchanging apprentices between Transylvania and frontier Tribunals so that each spends time in the other setting.
quotes: An apprentice must spend at least some time in Transylvania, to understand the value of what the House is building.

entries.title: Rotations and Decennials
entries.summary: Explains the Tremere expectation of regular returns to Transylvania and the Decennial planning meeting at Coeris, with advice on how a troupe can handle a magus's rotation using a reskinned replacement character.
quotes: At minimum, every Tremere magus should spend at least a season every ten years in Transylvania, unless kept abroad by pressing duties.
The easiest way to do this is just to reskin the primary magus (create a new character who looks and sounds different, but has the same underlying numbers).

entries.title: Serfs and Free Men
entries.summary: Explains the legal status of serfs, bonded free men and the privileged few with golden freedom in Hungary, including what is owed when each is killed, who may attend court, and how castle folk, castle warriors and the half-free fit in.
quotes: Serfs are property and may be bought and sold.
A blood price of 110 steers is due at the death of a free man: 50 for the kin, 50 for the king, and 10 for the mediators.

entries.title: Nobility: A Clarification
entries.summary: Lists the competing Hungarian beliefs about what makes someone noble in 1220 and rules that a character may claim nobility on any of them, noting that magi can easily become noble without an Oath of Fealty.
quotes: A player character can claim to be noble if she has any of these attributes, but other nobles will not necessarily agree that they share status.
This does not require an Oath of Fealty, and so does not breach the Code.

entries.title: Hungarian Social Classes as Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Maps each Hungarian social class (serfs, castle folk, hospites, castle warriors, free horsemen, petty and greater nobles, counts, bishops) to the Virtues and Flaws used to build such a character, with the seasons, money and retainers a landed noble gets.
quotes: Serfs, udvornici, most free men, and castle folk use the Peasant Free Virtue.
A Landed Noble, lacking other Virtues or Flaws, spends two seasons a year on maintaining his lifestyle, with a spare 10 pounds a year for largesse.
Counts must take the Oath of Fealty Flaw.

entries.title: The Holy Crown of Hungary
entries.summary: Describes the Doctrine of the Holy Crown, the grounds on which a king or noble may be legitimately resisted, and its effect on magi: a moral duty to resist corrupt nobles, occasional miraculous aid, and guaranteed trial under the Code.
quotes: The Holy Crown is a living being, and it connects God to Man.
In addition, their right to be tried for crimes under the Code of Hermes is guaranteed by the Crown, a Divine being, not the king.

entries.title: Witches Don't Exist (So Magi Are Not Witches)
entries.summary: Explains that witchcraft is not a crime in Hungary, that magi are treated as an ethnic group living by their own custom and judges, how jurisdiction disputes are handled, and how hedge magicians are policed.
quotes: witches do not exist, therefore no trials for witchcraft may be held
Hedge magicians in desperate trouble with someone else who has the right to dispense justice can claim the right to be tried under the Ancient Custom.

entries.title: The Aggtelek Caves
entries.summary: Gives the auras, vis types and special lesser-enchantment vis of the Aggtelek caves near Laniena, including a ward-granting vis from the iron flowers of Ochtinska Cave.
quotes: Baradla, as the biggest and most spectacular, has the most powerful aura of 5.
Both Imaginem and Muto vis can be collected in Baradla Cave.

entries.title: Fectores Versus Hermetic Fectores
entries.summary: Explains how Laniena splits its Gifted recruits between non-Hermetic Fectores (made Gifted Companions of House Ex Miscellanea) and Hermetic Fectores, what the initiation scripts can and cannot do, and the legal justification for the programme.
quotes: Two of every three Gifted individuals sent to or discovered by the oppidum are trained as Fectores before being admitted into the Order as Gifted Companions within House Ex Miscellanea
Laniena is under strict instructions from House Tremere not to give Hermetic training to any dhampirs

entries.title: Fector Characters
entries.requires: Social Status Virtue: Fector (Tradition: Hunters' Arts)
entries.summary: Character-creation rules for a non-Hermetic Fector: the Gift plus the free Fector Social Status Virtue, all three Practice Arts and three Foe Arts, free Second Sight, a five-year apprenticeship with a set pool of experience, and permitted starting Abilities.
quotes: A Fector has all three Practice Arts of Scry, Ban, and Slay, and can choose three Foe Arts.
During this time, the Fector receives 120 experience points that can be spent on the Hunters' Arts or on Abilities.

entries.title: Hermetic Fectores
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea (societas of Murat of Terezin)
entries.summary: Character-creation rules for a Hermetic Fector, a magus Ex Miscellanea who has one Practice Art as a free Major non-Hermetic Virtue with a Foe Art, a free Minor Magical Focus in harming a creature, and the Weak Spontaneous Magic Flaw.
quotes: Their free Minor Hermetic Virtue is a Minor Magical Focus in harming a particular supernatural creature
Their Major Hermetic Flaw is Weak Spontaneous Magic; the methodical preparation typical of a hunter comes at the expense of flexibility.

entries.title: Leap of Homecoming and Regiones
entries.summary: Sidebar on how Rego Corpus teleportation effects interact with regio boundaries: usually they can cross, but some regiones cannot be entered or left this way and this cannot be reliably predicted.
quotes: some regiones cannot be entered or left via Rego Corpus effects

entries.title: Studying from Exhibits (realia)
entries.summary: Restates the realia study rules: a realia is a study source that can be used a number of times equal to its Source Quality, and Source Quality drops when several characters study from the same exhibit at once.
quotes: The number of times that a character may study from a particular realia is equal to its Source Quality.
up to four characters studying reduce the Source Quality by 2; up to eight characters reduce the Source Quality by 3

entries.title: Exhibit Source Quality
entries.summary: Sidebar giving guideline Source Quality bands for exhibits depending on how many items they hold.
quotes: Unparalleled: Source Quality 11+
Comprehensive: Source Quality 8-10
Cursory: Source Quality 5-7

entries.title: Competition for Exhibit Study Access
entries.summary: Access rules for Tablinum's open exhibits and a stress die roll to see how many other characters also want to study from the same exhibit in a season.
quotes: roll a stress die against an Ease Factor of 3

entries.title: Ivan Rilski's Cave
entries.summary: Gives the Divine aura of the cave, tree and rock associated with Saint Ivan Rilski, which is separate from the Dominion aura of the nearby monastery.
quotes: The cave, tree, and rock bear a Divine aura of 4, separate from the Dominion aura of 3 possessed by the monastery.

entries.title: The Seven Lakes
entries.summary: Describes the Faerie aura and per-lake regiones of the Seven Lakes and the vila hosts who grant faerie gifts (each equivalent to a Minor Virtue with a Faerie Charm) to guests who accept a deadly year-and-a-day stay.
quotes: The area has a Faerie aura of 3, and each lake has a Faerie regio of aura 6.
Each gift is equivalent to a Minor Virtue, and is accompanied by a Faerie Charm.

entries.title: Starosel Tomb Temple Aura
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura, vis types and guardian genius loci of the Starosel tomb temple as a potential oppidum site.
quotes: it has a strong Magic aura of 6
Both Terram and Herbam vis can be collected within a few yards from the tomb temple.

entries.title: The Madara Horseman
entries.summary: Describes the Faerie aura of the Madara plateau and how a faerie rite wakes the Horseman and his opposing Lion, with a guideline for their Faerie Might.
quotes: The whole plateau has a Faerie aura of 3, which rises to 5 in immediate proximity to the Horseman.
The Madara Horseman should have a Faerie Might of at least 20, although this could be more depending on the needs of the people and the success of the rite which awakens him.

entries.title: The Bogomils
entries.summary: Explains Bogomilism as a non-Christian Divine religion: its structure, the Dominion aura Bogomil gatherings generate and how it conflicts with the Orthodox aura, the Social Status Virtues of its leaders, and a template for Bogomil missionaries.
quotes: Bogomilism is a non-Christian Divine religion.
Bogomil dedets and starets have the Wise One Social Status Virtue; the former usually have the Temporal Influence Virtue as well.
but exchange Transcendence for either Intervention or Adjuration.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition p.11, p.39, p.94

entries.title: The Silivriak
entries.summary: Describes the Orpheus flower as an Imaginem vis source and a Plant of Virtue that can be Enriched by daily poetry, then used to anoint lyre strings that grant a fixed Enchanting Music score useful only on the bereaved.
quotes: by composing a poem every day for 90 days, and reciting those poems to the plant.
The lyre grants its player the Enchanting Music Ability with a score of 3, although it can only affect those who are bereaved of a loved one.

entries.title: Gela
entries.summary: Explains the sanctum at Gela where the resident magus receives an annual personal vis source in return for teaching music and performance.
quotes: In return for an annual grant of vis from the oppidum (amounting to a Personal Vis Source), the magus in residence is obliged to teach music and performance to those who ask.

entries.title: The Devil's Throat
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura of the Devil's Throat cave and the Corpus vis found on the shore of its underground lake.
quotes: There is a Magic aura of 4 here.
Corpus vis that is occasionally washed up on the shores of the underground lake in the form of fragments of ancient skeletons.

entries.title: Perperikon
entries.summary: Describes the Magic aura of the ruined oracular city of Perperikon and the seasonal fertility aura of the Rock Womb, including its use as a source of Insight into Fertility Magics.
quotes: Perperikon has a Magic aura of 3.
the Rock Womb becomes flooded with a powerful Magic aura aligned with fertility.

entries.title: Seuthopolis Caverns and Auras
entries.summary: Gives the aura of the Thracian caverns beneath Seuthopolis, which house the magi's laboratories and libraries, and the Divine exception in the crypt.
quotes: These have a Magic aura of 5, with a few exceptions, such as the Crypt of the Martyred Virgin, which is Divine.

entries.title: Shipka Pass Regio and Tribunal Site
entries.summary: Describes the regio chosen as the Transylvanian Tribunal meeting site, its custodian, the seven-year schedule of meetings, and how visitors and traders use the Promenades and Hall.
quotes: The Quaestiores selected the Shipka Pass regio as the Tribunal site.
Transylvanian Tribunals, held every seven years

entries.title: Lictors
entries.requires: Role: lictor / hoplite in the Transylvanian Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains lictors (hoplites serving long term), the aid they may demand from Transylvanian covenants, and their badge of office, whose forgery is a serious crime.
quotes: Lictors have a duty to protect Quaestiores and follow their instructions.
lictors have a right to expect reasonable aid from any cives, soci, foederatus, or colona.
Carrying a facsimile of a lictorial badge is a serious crime.

entries.title: Red and Black Libraries
entries.summary: Describes the Quaesitorial Red Library (sigils of Renounced magi and spells used for Hermetic crimes) and Black Library (books it is a crime to own), and the vault with a Divine aura that houses them.
quotes: The Red and Black Libraries are stored in a vault consecrated by the bones of a virgin martyr, with a Divine Aura of 3.
these spells can be cast with impunity on hedge magicians, members of the Order of Odin or the Order of Solomon, or Renounced magi.

entries.title: Cult of the False Kabeiros (Initiation Scripts)
entries.requires: Initiation: Cult of the False Kabeiros (Cabeiri)
entries.summary: Presents a faerie-led Cabeiri mystery cult: its degrees, the faerie mystagogue's contribution to the Initiation total, the shared Minor Ordeal Vow and holy-day bonus, and the Minor cult Virtues (Piercing Gaze, Invasive Eyes, Bright Eyes, Eyes of Theseus) with their initiation breakdowns.
quotes: The degrees of initiation in this cult are called Interrogator, Invader, Observer, and Liberator.
Each of the cult Virtues is Minor.
The Initiation Scripts assume that the mystagogue provides combined scores of 9 to the Initiation total
Invasive Eyes are not blocked by Magic Resistance, since it's an observational, rather than magical, process.

entries.title: Regiones at Tablinum (access via Arcane Connections)
entries.summary: Explains that Tablinum's many superimposed regiones cannot be entered by sensing or following a path, but only by targeting Fixed Arcane Connections held by the curator with effects such as Leap of Homecoming.
quotes: The Arcane Connections are used to target Leap of Homecoming and similar effects to allow travel to the different regiones.

entries.title: Art Exhibits (realia and local auras)
entries.summary: Each Art exhibit is a realia for its Art and lets characters with a Study Requirement or Study Bonus study freely up to a set Art Score; each sits in its own regio with a Magic aura.
quotes: up until they reach an Art Score of 15
The Art Exhibit regiones all have a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: Arcanum Exhibit (four separate realia)
entries.summary: A regio holding several independent realia (Finesse, Magic Theory, Parma Magica and Penetration) so studying one does not interfere with others studying another.
quotes: The Arcanum Exhibit has a Magic aura of 6.

entries.title: Hiring Scribes at the Scriptorium
entries.summary: Visiting magi can hire some of the permanent scribes to copy books, paying vis and materials; Tremere may requisition scribes free. Gives the scribes' Ability scores.
quotes: It costs 2 pawns of vis to hire a scribe for a season
up to two scribes can be hired by visiting magi to copy books

entries.title: Copying Lab Texts at the Spell Hall
entries.summary: Tremere copy spells freely from the archive; other magi must donate a Lab Text or vis. Texts cannot be removed and cannot be used to invent spells directly.
quotes: Generally, donating a Lab Text allows the character to copy a number of other texts equal to the magnitude of the donated spell.
Alternatively, a magus may donate a number of pawns of vis equal to the total magnitude of the Lab Texts he wants to copy.

entries.title: The Chronicle (encyclopedia and fact lookup)
entries.summary: Treats the Chronicle volumes as tractatus in Order of Hermes Lore and Code of Hermes and gives a roll to look up a fact, with a bonus for each block of years of records accessed.
quotes: Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore (or Code of Hermes) + stress die roll against an Ease Factor
every complete 50 years of The Chronicle to which he has access

entries.title: The Chapel (Divine aura and relics)
entries.summary: The Divine exhibit is a realia in Divine Lore, filled with holy relics, with a Divine aura that probably overrides any Magic aura underneath.
quotes: The Chapel has a Divine aura of 6.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition pp.43-46

entries.title: The Mirrored Hall (Faerie Lore realia)
entries.summary: A restricted exhibit of mirrors each imprisoning a faerie, serving as a realia in Faerie Lore.
quotes: The Mirrored Hall has a Magic aura of 6.

entries.title: The Dungeon (Infernal Lore realia and aura)
entries.summary: A restricted exhibit of infernal horrors that serves as a realia in Infernal Lore and has a modest Infernal aura.
quotes: The Dungeon has an Infernal aura of 3.

entries.title: The Empty Halls (empty regiones)
entries.summary: Describes the many vacant regio halls where characters can be imprisoned or marooned, and the typical Magic auras found there.
quotes: Most of the Empty Halls have Magic auras of 3 or 4.

entries.title: Mansiones
entries.summary: Explains what a mansio is: a Mercere-run rest stop spaced along the main roads between covenants, either secret or semi-public, and why it is not an oppidum.
quotes: These are placed one day apart on the major roads between covenants.
Mansiones are not oppida, because they lack a cives as a resident.

entries.title: Studenica Monastery (Divine aura and saint's oil)
entries.summary: A holy site with a very high Divine aura and a saint with substantial Divine Might whose daily flow of oil can bestow a saint's miracle on an anointed person.
quotes: The Studenica is the most holy site in Serbia and has a Divine aura of 8.
With a Divine Might of 50

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.88 Saints' miracles

entries.title: Old Histria (aura and vis sources)
entries.summary: Describes the strong Magic aura of the old covenant, its mercury pool, and the truffle harvest that provide vis sources and affect research.
quotes: The aura here is strong, a Magic aura of 7.
A pool of magical mercury provides bountiful Terram vis.

entries.title: Unusual Vis (Strange Vis from roof tar)
