entries.summary: Sidebar on an unusual Creo vis source formed once a year in the roof tar of particular houses in villages inside the Dominion, whose collection area grows with the Tribunal's borders.
quotes: becomes infused with a little Creo vis

entries.title: Pula (Faerie aura, Magic aura and amphorae vis)
entries.summary: A town with a Faerie-aura amphitheater whose aura rises on special nights, a temple with a Magic aura, and hard-to-collect vis amphorae.
quotes: retains a Faerie aura of 6, which rises to 8 on special nights
has a powerful Magic aura of 5

entries.title: Shrouded Bay on Cres (vis and auras)
entries.summary: Lists the vis sources of the island (a blood well and storm-washed Rego vis) and the Magic auras of the villa and the island at large.
quotes: The villa has a Magic aura of 6, but a Magic aura of 1 is found over much of the island.
There is a well of blood that provides a major Corpus vis source

entries.title: Mercere House in the Transylvanian Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains Mercere's special arrangement in this Tribunal: members do not vote unless Gifted, Redcaps are numerous and disputed, spouses may be styled Redcaps, and vampire-blooded children are recruited.
quotes: House Mercere's members in the Tribunal do not vote unless they are Gifted
Formally speaking there are only fifteen Redcaps in all of Transylvania.

entries.title: Playing Gifted Children (Scholomance saga option)
entries.summary: Optional saga premise that starts the player characters as pupils in the same Scholomance class, giving a shared backstory for why a group of magi settle together and who their companions might be.
quotes: Having them as members of the Scholomance's class gives an opportunity for characters of different backgrounds to meet and form friendships.

entries.title: Teutonic Knight Characters
entries.summary: Character-creation guidance for Teutonic Order members (priests, knights, graymantles): typical Poor Flaw and relic Virtue choices, favored Abilities, and new Minor Social Status Virtues that set which Abilities may be taken at creation.
quotes: Teutonic Knights very commonly carry relics (the Relic Virtue), often in the hilt of their swords.
so knowledge of Dominion Lore is highly prized

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.41

entries.title: A More Holy Order (optional Teutonic Order variant)
entries.summary: Optional variant that makes the Teutonic Order truly holy, giving its conquered lands a Dominion aura with a particular temper and an inner circle with a Holy Tradition of Divine wonder-workers.
quotes: the lands conquered by the knights carry a Dominion aura with a Brave temper
whose favored Methods and Powers are Invocation, Blessing, and Cursing

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.39

entries.title: New Blessing Guideline
entries.summary: A new Blessing guideline that extends the beneficial effects of a relic to a group of men, targeting the relic rather than the men.
quotes: Level 15: Extend the beneficial effects of a relic over a standard Group of men.

entries.title: The Scholomance Regio and Auras
entries.summary: Describes the Scholomance tower, which sits inside a regio that opens during violent storms and can wander, with a Magic aura in both the valley and the regio and enchantments that garble speech and smear text.
quotes: At such times the regio (which has a Magic aura of 5) lies open and anyone can walk in

entries.title: Scholomance Schooling (pupils and curriculum)
entries.summary: Explains who is admitted to the Scholomance, what pupils are taught, what they must produce, and which background Virtues attendance can justify for companions, Redcaps and apprentices.
quotes: It accepts ten pupils at a time, all at once, and they remain for a total of seven years.
Pupils are required to make copies of some of the texts that they study at the school, and to write at least one summa or three tractatus during their stay.
Attending the Scholomance is a good way to explain Virtues such as Educated, Arcane Lore, Privileged Upbringing or (for apprentices) Skilled Parens.

entries.title: Teaching Duties at the Scholomance
entries.summary: Sets the teaching obligations of the oppidum's magi, including the requirement that they extend their Parma Magica around pupils so The Gift does not affect them.
quotes: Magi are expected to spend one season a year teaching
Magi are required to extend their Parma around those they teach to negate the social effects of The Gift.

entries.title: The Zenodochium (use, vis and Tribunal law)
entries.summary: Describes what each safehouse hospital holds, what magi must replace after using it, and the Tribunal's legal treatment of stealing vis from or damaging a zenodochium.
quotes: Stealing vis from a zenodochium is a Low Crime.
Damaging or destroying a zenodochium is a High Crime
up to two rooks of Corpus vis that can be used by magi in need

entries.title: Casting Tablets
entries.summary: Sidebar summarizing how any magus casts a spell from a casting tablet: a fixed Casting Total with no variation or vis boost, with Fatigue losses and Warping increasing the more the Spell Level exceeds the total.
quotes: Generate a Casting Total as if the magus knew the formulaic spell or ritual, and remember to include Wound and Aura Penalties.
If the Spell Level is up to 10 levels greater than the Casting Total, the spell is still cast, but the magus loses two Fatigue levels.

entries.title: Locating a Zenodochium
entries.summary: Where zenodochia are found and how to roll to see whether a character knows of a nearby one, with different Ease Factors for residents and visitors and adjustments for Tremere and for rarity.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore roll
In either case, Tremere characters have a +3 bonus to the roll.
Increase the Ease Factors by 3 if zenodochia are rare in your saga.

entries.title: Minor Covenant Hook: Zenodochium
entries.summary: A covenant creation hook placing a zenodochium within a day's travel, with the covenant's duty to replace what it uses and the consequences of damage or visiting injured magi.
quotes: The covenant may freely make use of the zenodochium, but must replace any vis or other items that are used or removed.

entries.title: The Curantis
entries.summary: Describes the Tribunal officer elected to inspect and repair zenodochia, his legal powers, vis salary, term limits and his Notary.
quotes: The Curantis spends about a season each year traveling the zenodochia network.
A character may not serve two successive terms as Curantis.

entries.title: Zenodochium Items and Warping
entries.summary: Explains that the high-power constant-effect items in a zenodochium give Warping to every human who rests there, and how long recovery from each wound severity takes.
quotes: any human character who remains within a zenodochium for a season accumulates 6 Warping Points

entries.title: Kezdö Válasz Forts (relocation)
entries.summary: Describes the oppidum's forts, their staffing, the periodic relocation cycle, and the time and casting tablets used to establish or destroy a fort and move laboratories.
quotes: establishing the fort can take one to two seasons
Currently there are four active forts in the Tribunal, each home to two magi.

entries.title: Kezdö Válasz Obligations and Methods
entries.summary: Explains the members' pledge to drop everything and respond to threats, their signalling charms with enough Penetration to pass Parma Magica, their rapid-travel methods, and the annual meeting where vexillations are announced.
quotes: Kezdö Válasz has approximately 55 grogs in total.
each is constructed with enough Penetration to pass through the magus' Parma Magica

groups.title: The Lands of the Nile
groups.intro: Rules particular to Egypt, Nubia and Ethiopia (Lands of the Nile).

entries.title: Reading Hieroglyphs and Tomb Warnings
entries.summary: Explains the medieval belief that learned Copts can read hieroglyphs, and gives a stress roll with Ease Factors for grasping the gist of tomb warnings and curses as taught by the Seekers' Guild.
quotes: the gist of a text can be understood with an Intelligence + Profession: Seeker stress roll against an Ease Factor related to the age and complexity of the text (common curses are Ease Factor 6, typical texts are Ease Factor 9)

entries.title: Hazards of the Desert
entries.summary: Adjusts the Deprivation rules for desert travel (faster water checks, extra sun damage) and gives a stress roll to escape dry quicksand, with notes on brigands, storms and jinn.
quotes: The Deprivation check time for lack of water is reduced in the deserts to 4 hours, while the sunlight does +1 non-combat damage if skin is left exposed
A character who is caught in an area of dry quicksand may make a Strength or Quickness stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 in the first round

entries.title: The Future and Hex Rolls
entries.summary: Boasting about future plans without saying 'if God wills it' is believed to invite curses, giving envious characters a bonus on Hex rolls unless the protective phrase is used.
quotes: This is represented as a +6 bonus on Hex rolls, to destroy the circumstance discussed, by any character who envies the speaker.

entries.title: Reputations, Shame and the Haj
entries.summary: Describes how characters remove a shameful Local Reputation by building a rival Reputation and buying down the old one, and how the Haj pilgrimage is treated as a series of scenes granting Reputation experience.
quotes: Once the competing Reputation equals the undesired Reputation, new experience gained in the second Reputation can instead be used to buy down the first
The Haj is, from a game perspective, a series of scenes.

entries.title: Pretending to Be Male or Married (Dark Secrets)
entries.summary: Advice on when a female character's disguise as a man or as a married woman counts as a Dark Secret or Gender Nonconforming Flaw, and when it is only a convenience.
quotes: If it will ruin the character's life, it is a Dark Secret.

entries.title: The Dhimmi Flaw in Egypt
entries.summary: Explains the legal status of non-Muslims in Egypt and lists what a dhimmi character must not do, which is the extended rule behind the Minor General Flaw Dhimmi; European characters may use Outsider instead.
quotes: Their duties and proscriptions are reflected in the Dhimmi Flaw, which is a Minor General Flaw. Characters from Europe might use Outsider instead.

entries.title: Overrun (creature Quality)
entries.requires: Creature with the Overrun Quality (hippopotamus, elephant)
entries.summary: A charging creature that hits with Overrun knocks its opponent down on a failed Dexterity + Athletics stress roll, after which the opponent is prone and cannot parry. The rule appears in the hippopotamus stat block and is reused for the elephant.
quotes: the opponent must make a Dexterity + Athletics stress roll against an Ease Factor equal to (Damage Total (before soak) + hippopotamus's Size – opponent's Size)

entries.title: Roll Attack and Drowning (crocodile)
entries.requires: Creature with the Roll Attack Quality (crocodile)
entries.summary: A crocodile that has bitten a foe can roll next round to tear flesh or drag the victim underwater to drown, and a victim breaks free only by overcoming a Grapple. The block also gives stealth, ambush and Crushing Jaws notes.
quotes: doing +6 damage without an attack roll
This requires the character to overcome a successful Grapple attack with a Grapple Strength of 10.

entries.title: Crushing Jaws (creature Quality)
entries.requires: Creature with the Crushing Jaws Quality (hyena, crocodile)
entries.summary: A new animal Quality for creatures with tremendously powerful biting muscles; the jaws can be held shut with a successful Grapple.
quotes: This Quality adds +3 Damage to any bite attack.

entries.title: Constriction and Swallow Whole (giant serpents)
entries.requires: Creature with the Constriction or Swallow Whole Quality
entries.summary: Rules for a serpent that constricts a grappled victim (deprivation checks) and can swallow smaller prey whole, where stomach acid does damage each round unless the victim braces against immersion. Includes group-attack tactics against elephants.
quotes: The victim must make a Stamina check every five rounds, or suffer the normal effects of deprivation.
The powerful acids inflict +9 damage every round, complete immersion quadruples this to +36

entries.title: The Seekers' Guild and Profession: Seeker
entries.summary: Describes the licensed Egyptian guild of tomb-robbers, its membership cost, library and training benefits, and the Profession: Seeker Ability that represents its lore.
quotes: Membership is purchased with an annual fee and a slice of the recovered treasure. This is currently 20% of all valuables found.
This knowledge is covered by the Profession: Seeker Ability.

entries.title: Resolving Tomb Traps
entries.summary: An optional trap procedure in which each player frames a clever response and rolls only for it against a trap Ease Factor the storyguide adjusts per character, with actions resolved in Quickness order (endangered character first, trap last), Fast-Cast magic and Action Priority Rolls.
quotes: Each trap is assigned a base Ease Factor, indicating the complexity of its construction.
The actions are resolved in order of Quickness, but with the character actually in danger always being treated as fastest, and the trap always going last.

entries.title: How Egyptian Tombs Sustain Ghosts
entries.summary: Explains the Egyptian afterlife in the Magic Realm: a ka must return each year to feed from offerings in its tomb or risk becoming a mut, and each tomb has a chapel, serdab and sepulcher with different defenses.
quotes: A ghost that does not do this risks losing its memories and becoming a mut, or else fading away entirely.

entries.title: Serdab and Stele
entries.summary: The serdab is the ghost's home in a tomb; a ghost can manifest any item from its grave goods or tomb paintings, and the stele in the serdab is the doorway to Duat and the Field of Reeds.
quotes: An Egyptian ghost can manifest, as part of its ethereal form, any item found in its grave goods or depicted on its tomb walls, provided they have not been stolen or defaced.

entries.title: Ghosts Animating Statues
entries.summary: Egyptian ghosts prefer to be incarnate and animate statues that resemble their bodies, which is why servant statues (ushabtis) and defacing statues matter to tomb robbers.
quotes: Defacement prevents a ghost animating a statue from ambushing the thieves, and deanimates those already possessed

entries.title: Tomb Auras, the Stele Vestige and Mummies as Arcane Connections
entries.summary: Tombs commonly lie in Magic auras and their stele is a vestige whose level equals the aura; an intact mummy is an Arcane Connection that helps the ka's Vestige Travel Total. Temples tend toward weak Faerie auras.
quotes: The stele within the tomb's serdab is a vestige to the Magic Realm with a level equal to the Magic aura within the tomb.
granting a Familiarity Bonus to the Vestige Travel Total of 15

entries.title: Ghosts Carving Equipment
entries.summary: A ghost buried with carving tools can make representations of objects that become real for its purposes, with creation time depending on the age of the tomb, and can feed itself or summon faerie reinforcements.
quotes: so the ghost can create a new object by drawing it in a single round

entries.title: The Field of Reeds
entries.summary: Describes the Egyptian afterlife regio in the Magic Realm, an archipelago of paradise islands ruled by the Daimon Wesir, each with a stele linking to a tomb, and its Faerie copy ruled by Osiris.

entries.title: Tomb Curses: Condition and Excoriation
entries.summary: Egyptian tomb curses are written enchantments made of a condition that triggers them and one or more excoriations that deliver the penalty; the storyguide decides how literally the condition is read.
quotes: All curses have two parts: a condition and one or more excoriations.

entries.title: Egyptian Talismans (tomb magic)
entries.summary: Describes trigger-based Egyptian talismans, which lack Penetration against humans, can be temporarily deactivated by a particular spell, and can be investigated like item triggers or resolved as narrative traps with a base Ease Factor from the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The base Ease Factor for bypassing a magical trap is equal to (6 + the magnitude of its effect).

entries.title: Possess Statue (Minor Power)
entries.requires: Egyptian ghost with the Possess Statue power
entries.summary: A power letting a ghost animate a wooden, stone or metal statue, given with a Hermetic equivalent level for each material; the statue's physical attacks must penetrate opponents' Magic Resistance.
quotes: Note that the physical attacks of an animated statue have to Penetrate the Magic Resistance of any opponents struck.

entries.title: Egyptian Wards (tomb magic)
entries.summary: Egyptian wards hide tombs or repel intruders, usually with a defined way to deactivate them, may carry Penetration against spirits, and are overcome with the narrative trap rules at a base Ease Factor from the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The base Ease Factor for such actions is (9 + the magnitude of effect).

entries.title: Quick Ghost Conversion (ka)
entries.summary: A step-by-step kit for turning an ordinary character into an Egyptian ghost (ka): choose Magic Might, swap Virtues and Flaws, add Magic Spirit, note intangibility and vulnerability to Mentem, and add powers and vis.
quotes: Give the character a Magic Might score of between 5 and 25
Add vis, usually Mentem, equal to the Might score divided by 5.

entries.title: Quick Animated Statue Conversion
entries.summary: A kit for building an animated statue from a mortal character, including Soak by statue material, size adjustments to Strength and Quickness, damage penalties for stone or bronze weapons, and how to force a ghost out of a statue.
quotes: Wood grants +9 Soak.
Hard metal grants +21 Soak.
Characters lose 2 Strength and gain 1 Quickness per Size lost, or conversely gain 2 Strength and lose 1 Quickness per Size gained.

entries.title: Royal Pharaonic Ghosts
entries.summary: Guidelines for designing the ghosts of Egyptian royalty: bloodline Virtues from Faerie gods, odd powers drawn from a pharaoh's life, and Transformation after death thanks to long death rituals.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Transformation

entries.title: Blood of the Old Gods and Sympathy Traits
entries.requires: Virtue: Blood of the Old Gods (Minor or Major Supernatural)
entries.summary: A variety of Faerie Blood that grants a Sympathy Trait which can replace an Ability speciality on applicable rolls (always as a stress roll), is raised with experience, and is capped by the Warping Score.
quotes: A Sympathy Trait can replace the character's speciality on any applicable Ability roll, but doing so always makes the roll a stress roll.

entries.title: The Akh (Egyptian Daimon)
entries.summary: Explains how the ba, ka and khu fuse into an akh, a Daimon, and how to build one as a Magic Spirit with a Magic Might range, as a Winter creature summoned by name or relics.
quotes: Assume a Magic Might Score of 20 for noblemen who have the simplest coffin texts, up to 60 for the greatest pharaohs

entries.title: Designing Tombs and Mortuaries
entries.summary: Introduces a method for designing ancient tombs with Boons, Hooks and Build Points as if they were covenants, needed only if a tomb is an ongoing part of a saga.
quotes: This section presents a method for designing ancient tombs using Boons, Hooks, and Build Points as if it were a covenant.

entries.title: Basic Tomb Features: Tether, Aura and Build Points
entries.summary: Tombs generate preternatural tethers that create Magic auras, and the tomb's rank sets its base aura and Build Points; each tomb has a cap on Hook points to spend on Boons.
quotes: For every century that a grave site (which could be a series of pyramids, or a number of individual tombs) was in use, it generates a tether score of 1, up to a maximum of 5.
Each tomb can have up to 10 points of Hooks, which can be used to purchase Boons.

entries.title: Tomb Curses as Resources
entries.summary: How to build a tomb curse as a Hermetic-style enchantment: usual Range and Target, triggers, uses per day, Greater or Lesser Malediction for effects Hermetic magic cannot copy, false curses and their Build Point cost.
quotes: Maledictions can be of any appropriate Technique or Form, and have a base level of 10 for a Lesser Malediction, and level 30 for a Greater Malediction.
A curse costs two Build Points for every five levels of effects.

entries.title: Tomb Enchanted Items: Talismans and Wards
entries.summary: Sets the Build Point cost of tomb talismans and wards and notes that they are not true Hermetic enchantments, so they can be bypassed using the trap Ease Factors, with Magic Resistance beating low Penetration automatically.
quotes: These cost two Build Points for every five levels of effects.

entries.title: Tomb Specialists
entries.summary: Tomb inhabitants such as cult priests, walking cadavers and ghostly viziers are bought as specialists, teachers or guardians for Build Points.
quotes: Tomb guardians usually cost Build Points equal to their highest Martial Ability or Brawl, as applicable.

entries.title: Example Traps and Trap Damage
entries.summary: A catalogue of mechanical traps with Build Costs and Ease Factors, including rules of thumb for rockfall, projectile and pit damage, head wires and poisoned powders.
quotes: For smaller rockfalls, a rule of thumb is +1 damage per 10 pounds of rocks.
calculate Damage as (Stress die + Weapon Damage Modifier from page 177 of the core rules)

entries.title: Tomb Traps: Build Point Costs
entries.summary: Tables giving the Build Point cost of tomb traps by severity of harm and the modifier for how hard they are to avoid.
quotes: The ease of avoiding a trap modifies the Build Point cost.

entries.title: Tomb Hooks and Boons
entries.summary: Notes how covenant Boons and Hooks apply to tombs: Wealth means intact grave goods, and Nubian tombs should take the Seclusion Boon.
quotes: In Nubia, all tombs should purchase the Seclusion Boon due to the superstitious avoidance of all things to do with the dead.

entries.title: Means of Avoiding Traps
entries.summary: Traps take effect last in the combat round so characters can react, and slower traps such as flooding rooms give extended time to escape.
quotes: Traps, regardless of their type, impose their effects last in the combat round.

entries.title: Perception Checks and Trap Lighting
entries.summary: A Perception + Awareness roll lets a character notice a trap without triggering it, with Ease Factors modified by the quality of lighting.
quotes: Characters able to supply perfect lighting conditions (such as through a spell) decrease the Ease Factor by 3

entries.title: Evading Traps with Lords of Men Evasion
entries.requires: Optional Combat rules from Lords of Men
entries.summary: For troupes using the optional Lords of Men combat rules, a trap's Attack total is based on the trap setter's Intelligence and Profession and tested against the Evasion Combat Statistic.
quotes: assume the trap's Attack total is stress die + Intelligence of the trap setter + Profession of the trap setter

entries.title: Auras in Egypt
entries.summary: Gives typical Dominion aura strengths for holy sites, graves, workplaces and the call to prayer, how to set Faerie auras from the strongest faerie's Might, where Magic auras come from, and Infernal auras.
quotes: Faerie auras are equal to (Might of the most powerful faerie in the area /5)

generally places of worship have a Dominion aura of 4, the cemeteries and homes of the People of the Book have an aura of 3, the places of work of monotheists have an aura of 2, and land from which the call to prayer can be heard has an aura of 1

entries.title: Naphtha Pots and Lighting Bombs
entries.summary: Rules for Egyptian incendiary, explosive and poison grenades, including the damage each kind does and how troops react to them.
quotes: Most pots contain a thick gel that burns for several minutes, doing +10 damage each turn to whatever the fuel touches.
Characters may face the naphtha with a Brave Personality trait roll against an Ease Factor of 5.

entries.title: Making Naphtha With Magic
entries.summary: Spell guideline for creating naphtha with Creo Aquam, giving the Base level and Base Individual size, and noting that it ignites if made outside a container.
quotes: This gives Creo Aquam spells a Base level of 3, and the Base Individual target is a pool one foot across and six inches deep, regardless of the viscosity of the naphtha.

entries.title: Teacher of the House (Mystery Initiation Path)
entries.requires: Initiation into the House of the Sultan's school (mystagogue with Lore of the House)
entries.summary: Initiation scripts for the House's teaching Virtues, each with a mystagogue requirement, a ritual and a script bonus, including a debate with Seshat for Improved or Great Communication.
quotes: The mystagogue must have a (Presence + Lore of the House) total of at least 6.
This requires a Communication + Charm roll against an Ease Factor of 12

entries.title: Swallow Whole (new Mundane Quality)
entries.summary: The scorpion fish stat block introduces a reusable Swallow Whole Quality with rules for escaping, suffocation, stomach acid damage and bracing against immersion.
quotes: The scorpaena can swallow whole any creature of Size 0 or smaller.
The fish cannot swallow a second creature until the previous one has reached the stomach.

entries.title: The Baqt (Rego vis source)
entries.requires: Access to copies of the Baqt in Nobatia, Makuria or Dongola Cathedral
entries.summary: Explains the Nubian-Egyptian treaty and the vis it yields: signed copies and the two original documents are Rego vis sources whose output depends on peace and the tribute being paid.
quotes: Furthermore, the vis is only produced in years in which the Egyptians do not attack and the Nubian tribute is not in arrears.

entries.title: Slavery in a Saga (slave, owner and slaver characters)
entries.requires: Saga set in Egypt or Nubia (Slavelands)
entries.summary: Guidance for troupes on playing slaves, free Aithiopians, slave owners, slavers and campaigners against slavery, including which Virtues and Flaws suit each character type.
quotes: Characters who are slavers should take the Merchant Social Status Virtue if they are mostly involved in the transport of slaves, or the Mercenary Captain Social Status Virtue if they are captors.

entries.title: A Free Aithiopian Character
entries.requires: Aithiopian character in a saga set outside the Slavelands
entries.summary: Says which Social Status Flaw a free Aithiopian character should take and suggests related Story Flaws.
quotes: Free Aithiopians should take either the Outsider or Outcast Social Status Flaw in any saga set outside of the Slavelands.

entries.title: A Slave Owner Character
entries.requires: Saga set in Egypt or Nubia
entries.summary: In Egypt and Nubia owning slaves needs no Virtue, and a Christian owner in a Christian kingdom takes a small Local Reputation for the social disapproval.
quotes: A Christian slave owner in a Christian kingdom has a Local Reputation at a score of 1, representing the social disapproval that this practice engenders.

entries.title: Lost Temple of Ramses (Faerie regio)
entries.summary: Describes a hidden Faerie regio holding twin temples, its aura strength, and the baboon ritual that reveals the way in.
quotes: Explorers have been unsuccessful in locating the lost temples because they reside within a Faerie regio with an aura of 5.

entries.title: Tumulus Graves (Magic aura)
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura strength of intact Nobatian royal tumuli and notes the grave guardians that may protect them.
quotes: Each intact tumulus (for some have been robbed) has a Magic aura of 1, and may contain a grave guardian such as a mummified dog.

entries.title: Dju Wa'ab (Magic aura)
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura of the sacred mountain Dju Wa'ab, hints that the surrounding burial sites are stronger, and notes the faded Faerie auras of the old temples.
quotes: Dju Wa'ab, as an impressive natural feature, has a Magic aura of 3; the various burial sites might have a higher aura.

entries.title: Kurru (Magic aura)
entries.summary: The first Kushite pyramid field carries a Magic aura from two centuries of use as a royal cemetery.
quotes: There is a Magic aura of 2 at Kurru, deriving from the use of this site for two centuries.

entries.title: Nuri Necropolis (Magic aura)
entries.summary: The later Napatan pyramid field has a strong Magic aura earned by about five hundred years of use as a royal cemetery.
quotes: Nuri was in use for about five hundred years, before Arqamani moved the royal cemetery to Meroë, long enough for it to gain a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: The Church of the Granite Columns (Dominion auras)
entries.summary: Gives the Dominion aura strengths of Dongola's cathedral and the neighbouring Church of the Angels.
quotes: There is a Dominion aura of 7 within the cathedral.

entries.title: Ancient Auras
entries.requires: Saga set among ancient Egyptian or Nubian monuments
entries.summary: Explains how long-used ancient cemeteries and monuments gain Magic auras after their Faerie auras fade, and how natural features or decay modify the strength.
quotes: These tethers have generated a Magic aura of 1 for every century that they saw continuous use

entries.title: Kerma Cemetery (Magic auras)
entries.summary: Gives the graded Magic aura levels across the huge royal tumuli and the rest of the ancient Kerma cemetery.
quotes: A Magic aura of level 3 lingers around these four tumuli, but weakens to 2 over the rest of the royal cemetery and 1 over the rest of the graves.

entries.title: The Dihi (detachable-head race)
entries.requires: Dihi heritage (Blemmya and human offspring from northern Atbai)
entries.summary: Rules for playing a Dihi, whose head detaches under shock or strain: the stress-die trigger, botch effects, reattaching the head, inheritance, and the Flaw and Virtue that suit the condition.
quotes: Under situations of physical or emotional stress roll a stress die; if the result is 9 or more then her head detaches.
It takes a round to reattach the head to the body.

entries.title: El-Hobagi (Faerie aura)
entries.summary: The tumulus and temple of Atum at el-Hobagi, with a Faerie aura around the temple and notes on entering the unopened tumulus.
quotes: The Faerie aura of 3 at the temple suggests that the building is still used for worship of the Kushitic gods

entries.title: Kassalan Exorcists
entries.requires: Training by the Mortuary Society of Kassala
entries.summary: Describes the typical Virtues, Abilities and tactics of an exorcist of the Mortuary Society, who specialises in laying ghosts and the walking dead.
quotes: Exorcists tend to concentrate on low level, high Penetration effects, and often work in concert to destroy powerful ghosts.

entries.title: New Virtue: Kassalan Exorcism
entries.summary: A limited supernatural casting method for wards against ghosts and the walking dead and for stripping their Might, with its own fatigue cost, preparation time, Casting Total and Penetration rules.
quotes: To cast a spell you must expend a Fatigue level, whether the spell succeeds or fails.
Your Casting Total is equal to (Stamina + Organization Lore: Mortuary Society + Aura modifier + stress die) / 2.

entries.title: Kassalan Dust
entries.requires: Virtue: Kassalan Exorcism or Organization Lore: Mortuary Society
entries.summary: The gold-based dust required for Kassalan Exorcism, with its bonuses against Corpse Magic and the dead and its cost in gold.
quotes: A handful also adds +3 to uses of the Corpse Magic Supernatural Ability to command a corpse to return to its grave or prevent it from being affected by Corpse Magic.

entries.title: Begarawiyah Necropolis (Magic auras)
entries.summary: Gives Magic aura strengths for each cemetery of the royal necropolis outside Meroe, based on centuries of royal burial, and notes occupied pyramids with stronger auras.
quotes: There is a Magic aura of 4 here, representing the preternatural tether of over four hundred years of royal burials.
The preternatural tether of six and a half centuries of royal burials has resulted in a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: The Alchemists of Soba
entries.requires: Virtue: Soban Alchemy or Alchemist of Soba
entries.summary: Explains how to build a Soban Alchemist character, the Abilities and patronage they need, the obligation to stay near Soba, and how the craft is taught from books or by initiation.
quotes: They also require the Profession: Apothecary Ability to manage and run a well-stocked alchemist's laboratory.

entries.title: Soban Alchemy
entries.summary: Introduces Soban Alchemy as a supernatural science that makes temporary changes to matter, separate from Philosophiae reagents and not reproducible by Rego Craft magic.
quotes: Unlike alchemical reagents made with Philosophiae, Soban Alchemy is a supernatural science, and cannot be duplicated with Rego Craft magic.

entries.title: New Ability: Soban Alchemy (Sovereign Reagent)
entries.summary: Full procedure for making and applying Sovereign Reagent: dose cost and seasonal limits, which properties can change, Duration by Ability score, Casting Total against property Ease Factors, Penetration and Warping.
quotes: Each dose of Sovereign Reagent costs the equivalent of a Mythic Pound of ingredients, or else a pawn of Muto vis.
After applying the reagent, generate a Casting Total from Intelligence + Soban Alchemy + Aura modifier + stress die against an Ease Factor determined by the type of change desired:
The Penetration Total is equal to Casting Total – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus.

entries.title: Blemmyae Characters
entries.summary: Describes the physical traits of Blemmyae and the Magic Qualities and Inferiorities they inherit as Magic Humans, with differences between male and female Blemmyae and notes on armor and shields.
quotes: Male Blemmyae also have the Age Quickly Major Flaw as a Magic Inferiority, meaning that they have a lifespan typical of that of a human.
They cannot use large shields effectively.

entries.title: Structure of the Cult of Dedun
entries.summary: Describes how the Cult of Dedun is organised into districts under temple priests, that its Mysteries are aligned to the Magic realm, and what its members seek.
quotes: The Cult of Dedun is a Mystery Cult.
its Mysteries are aligned to the Magic realm rather than that of Faerie

entries.title: The Initiation Process
entries.summary: Recaps how a Mystagogue rolls an Initiation Total against the script's Ease Factor, how not knowing the power raises the Ease Factor, and how The Gift affects Ordeals and self-initiation.
quotes: generates an Initiation Total equal to his Presence + Organization Lore + Script Bonus
If the Mystagogue does not personally know the power then the Ease Factor is increased by 3 (if the power is a Minor Virtue) or 9 (if the power is a Major Virtue).

entries.title: Cult of Dedun: Adherent
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Adherent
entries.summary: Explains who the cult's Adherents are, what is required of them, and how the cult's Prohibition protects its secrecy.
quotes: relying on the cult's Prohibition (gained upon Initiation to the rank of adherent) to maintain secrecy

entries.title: Initiation Script: Adherent of Dedun
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Adherent
entries.summary: Initiation Script for the lowest rank, which grants no Virtue but binds the Initiate with the Prohibition Flaw; also covers the aging-Crisis-like penalty for breaking it.
quotes: Violating the cult's Prohibition causes Dedun's Shadow to pass over the oathbreaker.

entries.title: Cult of Dedun: Altar Priest
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Altar Priest
entries.summary: Describes the duties and Ability requirements of altar priests and how they trade their Prohibition for a Vow.
quotes: Altar priests are expected to have an Organization Lore: Cult of Dedun of 1 or more, and a Meroitic of at least 3 to perform the rites to Dedun.

entries.title: Initiation Script: Altar Priest of Dedun (Dedun's Blessing)
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Altar Priest
entries.summary: Initiation Script that grants Dedun's Blessing, letting the character align Magic auras toward the dead through yearly ceremonies and an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll.
quotes: The level of the aura is doubled when the activity matches the alignment
You may then make a roll of Intelligence + Magic Lore + stress die against an Ease Factor of (9+aura level).

entries.title: Cult of Dedun: Temple Priest and the Court of the Dead
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Temple Priest
entries.summary: Rank requirements and duties of temple priests, including how they build a court of prepared corpses and how the court's strength is totalled from the Reputations of its members.
quotes: To be considered for this rank, a character must have an Organization Lore: Cult of Dedun of at least 3, and knowledge of Meroitic at 4 or more.
Each member of the court contributes the highest Reputation that it had in life to the total strength of the court, with a minimum of 1.

entries.title: Initiation Script: Temple Priest of Dedun (Unnatural Vitality)
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Temple Priest
entries.summary: Initiation Script that grants Unnatural Vitality, turning Decrepitude into a bonus to Casting and Laboratory Totals and softening the effects of old age.
quotes: She gains a bonus to all Casting Totals and Laboratory Totals equal to (3 x Decrepitude Score).

entries.title: Cult of Dedun: The Undying Ones
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, rank of Undying One
entries.summary: Prerequisites for the final rank, how it turns a Gifted initiate into a Magic Human, and how the corpse-court substitutes for a Magic aura to stave off Acclimation.
quotes: Furthermore, the sum of the character's Warping Score and Decrepitude Score must equal or exceed 7.
The court substitutes for a Magic aura of a level equal to one tenth (or fraction) of the total strength.

entries.title: Initiation Script: Undying One (Transformed Human)
entries.requires: Cult of Dedun, Temple Priest with The Gift (self-initiation)
entries.summary: Initiation Script that makes the character a Magic Human with Might bought from the court's strength, removes ageing and Warping, and imposes a year-long ritual and the loss of The Gift.
quotes: You can raise this Might above the base using the total strength of the character's court, buying Might Score as if it were an Art.

entries.title: Losing The Gift
entries.requires: Character who has lost The Gift (for example by Undying One initiation)
entries.summary: Lists the consequences of losing The Gift for a magical character, covering Favored Abilities, inventing spells, Initiation Scripts, Hermetic Virtues and Parma Magica.
quotes: She loses all Hermetic Virtues and Flaws (these may only be possessed by Gifted characters).

entries.title: The Lost Regio of the Great Stelae
entries.summary: Describes a Faerie regio of the ancient afterlife reached through the Axum stelae, accessible only when the Divine aura recedes at the winter solstice, and the ghosts of kings who dwell there.
quotes: on the night of the winter solstice, the Divine recedes just enough for Faerie to emerge for one short window, allowing easier entry to the regio within.

entries.title: The Ethiopian Calendar and Dates
entries.summary: Table of Ethiopian months with their Julian start dates (and leap-year starts), plus a note that Year-duration spells are unaffected by the different calendar.
quotes: This does not impact spells with Year durations, as the duration is based on Solstices, rather than mundane calendars.

entries.title: Ethiopian Calendar (year numbering)
entries.summary: Explains the Ethiopian month lengths, intercalary days and how to convert Ethiopian year numbers to Julian ones.
quotes: so the number of the Ethiopian year is eight years less than the Julian year number from January 1 until August 30 or 31, and then seven years less for the remainder of the Julian year.

entries.title: Ethiopian Church Forests and Tabot (Divine auras)
entries.summary: Explains how the sacred forest around an Ethiopian church concentrates its Divine aura, how a lush forest strengthens it, and how the consecrated tabot maintains the aura.
quotes: In communities with these forests, the Divine aura is concentrated within the forest area, resulting in an aura one lower in the areas outside the forest, even if the church is in the middle of town.

related.text: Realms of Power: Divine Revised p.10

entries.title: Ark of the Covenant and Ring of Solomon (relic Faith Scores)
entries.summary: Gives the Faith Scores and Divine Might of the Ark of the Covenant and the Ring of Solomon for different believers, the ring's bonus to Solomonic and Ars Notoria casting, and its use as a tractatus.
quotes: The Ark of the Covenant has a Faith Score of 10, giving it 10 Faith points and a Divine Might of 100 for any Ethiopian, Falasha or Christian

related.text: Realms of Power: Divine Revised pp.44, 98

entries.title: Debterah (Ethiopian holy societas)
entries.requires: Holy Societas: Debterah (Ethiopian church lay cantors and amulet-makers)
entries.summary: Sidebar on Saint Yared and the debterah, an Ethiopian Christian holy societas, giving its favored Abilities and a stand-in Virtue and Ability package for using debterah without Realms of Power: the Divine. Also notes the Yared chant books as a summa on Organization Lore: Ethiopian Church.
quotes: Adjuration, Blessing, Craft Amulets, Invocation.
These books collectively act as a summa of Organization Lore: Ethiopian Church, Level 5, Quality 8.

related.text: Realms of Power: the Divine Revised p.34, 37, 48-50, 137

entries.title: Roha pilgrimage story framework
entries.summary: Describes how a season spent navigating and praying at the churches of Roha can count as a pilgrimage story, tying into the pilgrimage rules in The Church. Lists the Holy Land replicas found there.
quotes: an individual can complete a pilgrimage story as described in The Church, pages 16–19.

entries.title: Mythic Aithiopians as characters
entries.summary: Explains how to build a Mythic Aithiopian character: they carry an Outsider status in Nubia and gain tribe-specific intrinsic Virtues and Flaws on top of the normal allotment, or may be built as Magic Humans instead.
quotes: Aithiopes have intrinsic Virtues and Flaws, which are in addition to the normal allotment for characters.
They automatically receive the effects of the Outsider Social Status Flaw within Nubia
Magic Humans are by default immune to aging and deprivation

entries.title: Rhizophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the root-eating Rhizophagi, expert herbalists and poisoners, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw and a short explanation of the Herbalism Ability.
quotes: the Herbalism Virtue grants access to a special Ability called Herbalism

entries.title: Icthyophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the coastal fish-eating Icthyophagi, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw and the properties of their preserved fish bricks as travel food.
quotes: A month's worth of this food weighs just one point of Load.

entries.title: Hylophagus characters
entries.summary: Describes the tree-dwelling Hylophagi as intelligent monkeys built from baboon statistics plus extra Virtues and Flaws, and suggests using their village-trees as covenant sites and the Hylophagi as covenfolk.
quotes: Use the statistics for baboons in the Bestiary, but add the Perfect Balance Virtue and the Primitive Equipment Flaw
A village tree has the approximate interior dimensions of a Mystic Tower.

related.text: ArM5 p.139 Free the Striding Tree

entries.title: Cynegus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the hunters of the Cynegi, who use kombe-laced arrows; gives the Stamina roll against the poison, the Profession: Prepare Kombe Ability and its application roll, and the tribe's intrinsic Virtue and Flaw.
quotes: must make a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 12
characters should roll Dexterity + Profession: Prepare Kombè against an Ease Factor of (usually) 6

entries.title: Struthophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the ostrich-riding Struthophagi, valued as light cavalry, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw.
quotes: Puissant Ride; Small Frame

entries.title: Acridophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the locust-eating Acridophagi, whose intrinsic Flaw is a curse that makes Aging rolls start early when the louse infestation begins.
quotes: The Acridophagus curse causes them to start making Aging rolls at 15

entries.title: Cynamolgus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the dog-pack herders of the Cynamolgi, who may use Animal Handling in place of Leadership when commanding their dogs, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw.
quotes: a Cynamolgus can act as the leader of a trained group of dogs, using his Animal Handling in place of Leadership

entries.title: Megabarus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the Megabari herders, giving separate intrinsic Virtues and Flaws for men and for women.
quotes: Puissant Bows; Prohibition (harming women)

entries.title: Tribunal boundaries and joining a Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga option: expanding or redrawing Tribunal boundaries in the Nile region
entries.summary: Explains what a new covenant needs in order to join an existing Tribunal and how inter-Tribunal border disputes are settled at Grand Tribunal.
quotes: Inter-tribunal disputes, such as border definitions, must be settled at Grand Tribunal (ArM5, page 14).

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.49

entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: Founding a new Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga option: creating a Nile Tribunal
entries.summary: Sets out the minimum membership needed to found a new Tribunal and the steps and obstacles to getting it ratified at a Grand Tribunal.
quotes: A Tribunal must have at least twelve magi from at least four covenants, and at least one Quaesitor to preside at Tribunal meetings.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: Siwa Oasis Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: The Boons and Hooks that define Siwa Oasis as a covenant site, with notes on extra Hooks such as Castle, Natural Disaster and Site Hook: Regio that a troupe could add.
quotes: With seven Boons and seven Hooks, there is room for Siwa to be customized by magi living there by adding a balance of Boons and Hooks.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: New Hook: Multiple Sites
entries.requires: Covenant with important facilities at several separate sites
entries.summary: A new Resources Hook for covenants spread over several sites, covering the trade-offs of protecting each site with the Aegis of the Hearth and the threshold for the major version.
quotes: For the major form of this Hook, there are five or more sites requiring protection.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: New Hook: Fragile Vis Source
entries.requires: Covenant with a vis source of four or more pawns that can be damaged
entries.summary: A new Resources Hook describing vis sources that stop producing if a specific feature is damaged, resuming if the damage is repaired, with the threshold and counting rule for the major version.
quotes: For the major form of this Hook, there are three or more vis sites which are fragile.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: Ikhmindi Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: The Boons and Hooks that define Ikhmindi as a covenant site, including a well that benefits the Aging rolls of those who drink from it, plus suggestions for further Hooks and Boons a troupe could add.
quotes: There are six Boons and eight Hooks selected for Ikhmindi, allowing for some customization by magi establishing a covenant.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: Adulis Boons and Hooks
entries.summary: The Boons and Hooks that define the Adulis covenant site, including a Regio Hook, a healthy-feature bonus to Aging rolls, and suggestions for further Hooks such as Uncontrolled Portal and Monster.
quotes: There are four Boons and nine Hooks based on the site, allowing for some customization by magi establishing a covenant.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: New Hooks and Boons: Linked Vis Site and Unwitting Defenders
entries.requires: Covenant creation (optional new Hook and Boon)
entries.summary: Rules for two new covenant options: the Linked Vis Site Hook, where linked vis sources fail in stages if an associated condition is not met, and the Unwitting Defenders Boon, where an unaware outside force protects the covenant until the covenant reveals itself.
quotes: Their rates are halved in the first year, then quartered in the second, then stop altogether.
The vis sites thus linked must be purchased separately during covenant creation.
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

entries.title: Adulis lighthouse laboratories
entries.summary: Describes using the old Adulis lighthouse as four sanctums and laboratories, and the distraction penalty that applies to laboratory activity if magic is used to keep the lighthouse lit.
quotes: any laboratory activity suffers a –5 penalty, unless the magus is Blind
entries.section: Potential Covenant Sites of the Nile Region

groups.title: Mythic Locations
groups.intro: Rules tied to the places of Mythic Locations.

entries.title: What the Magi Know (location lore rolls)
entries.summary: Before visiting a location, a character may already know something about it, found by an Intelligence + Ability roll against an Ease Factor. Information is sorted into four categories of knowledge, each with its own Ease Factor, and what is known may be misleading or false.
quotes: Exactly what she might know is determined by an appropriate Intelligence + Ability roll measured against a set Ease Factor.
Information is divided into four categories: Known by All, Widely Known, Uncommon Knowledge, and Lost Secrets.

entries.title: Bath: Rumors (what is known by category)
entries.summary: Bath's application of the lore-roll system: the roll uses Area Lore (or Organization Lore: Church with penalties by distance), and sorted lists show what is known at each of the four knowledge levels.
quotes: Players can make an Intelligence + Area Lore: Stonehenge Tribunal to see what their characters know.

related.text: Mythic Locations: What the Magi Know

entries.title: Bath: Effects of the Baths
entries.summary: Bathing at Bath gives bonuses to Disease Recovery rolls depending on the care received, and the storyguide may instead pick other effects such as suppressing Flaws, bonuses to Aging, wound recovery or study totals.
quotes: A character attempting Disease Recovery rolls adds +5 if given a full course of care, +3 if she bathes regularly and cares for herself, and +1 if she simply bathes each day until the symptoms abate.

related.text: Art and Academe p.46 and p.58 Disease Recovery

entries.title: Bath: A Fourth Set of Baths (Gift-suppressing baths and vis)
entries.summary: An optional hidden set of baths that suppresses the social penalties of The Gift for a time, allows a spent Confidence point to be regained once per story, and can yield Vim vis from the skin of Gifted bathers tied to their Warping Score.
quotes: The waters here suppress the negative communication effects of The Gift, for a week with each bathing.
The oil can only be drawn from a magus once after each time his Warping Score increases, and forms an Arcane Connection to the magus.

entries.title: Bear Island: What the Magi Know (lore rolls)
entries.summary: Bear Island's specific lore rolls: Area Lore (Anatolia or Theban Tribunal) with a bonus for eastern magi, or Artes Liberales with a penalty, followed by what is known at each knowledge level.
quotes: The legend is more popular in the east than the west, and an eastern magus receives a +3 bonus.
This roll is penalized by –6, because the Legend of the Golden Fleece is not popular or readily accessible.

related.text: Mythic Locations: What the Magi Know

entries.title: Bear Island: Chytus Harbor (Gegenees external vis boulders)
entries.summary: A Faerie aura site where the Gegenees keep their external vis in boulders; the number of vis-holding boulders is scaled to the saga's power level and moving or threatening them provokes an assault.
quotes: How many of these hold vis depends on how many Gegenees you need for your saga: 50 for a low powered saga, 200 for a medium powered saga, and 1,000 or more for a high powered saga.

entries.title: Bear Island: Temenos of Dindyméné (dual Magic and Faerie aura)
entries.summary: A sacred grove holding overlapping Magic and Faerie auras, where the older Magic aura normally suppresses the Faerie one except on certain anniversaries and festival dates, and which is the doorway to a Magic regio and a Faerie regio.
quotes: The temenos has both a Magic aura of 3 and a Faerie aura of 3.
At certain times of the year, however, the Faerie aura increases to 4 and suppresses the Magic aura.

entries.title: Bear Island: The Jasonian Way (faerie regio path)
entries.summary: A faerie regio path to the summit of Mount Dindymon with fixed travel time, entrances in weaker or stronger Faerie auras at each end, and a vast faerie forest of Gegenees off the path.
quotes: It takes four hours to travel the trail, no matter what the characters do to expedite this process.

entries.title: Bear Island: Entering the regiones and Regio Sight ease factors
entries.summary: How to enter the Faerie regio by ritual and how to find either regio by spell or Regio Sight roll, with Ease Factors that change depending on which aura currently dominates.
quotes: Under the Temenos of Dindyméné's Magic aura, the Ease Factor to see the Magic regio is 11 and to see the Faerie regio is 23.
When the temenos has a Faerie aura of 4, the Ease Factor to see the Magic regio is 25 and to see the Faerie regio is 9.

entries.title: Bear Island: Faerie Regio of Dindyméné
entries.summary: The Faerie regio behind the temenos, home of the Idaian Daktyls, stacked with a Magic aura and Magic regio.
quotes: The Faerie regio has a Faerie aura of 6.

entries.title: Bear Island: Magic Regio of Dindyméné
entries.summary: An enlarged, uninhabited Magic regio whose peace gives visitors a temporary Calm personality trait unless they have Magic-realm supernatural abilities, and which grows Herbam and Terram vis each year.
quotes: With a Magic aura of 6, the Magic regio is an enlarged copy of the Temenos of Dindyméné.
Entering characters gain a new Personality Trait, Calm +2, unless they have supernatural abilities derived from the Magic realm, which includes the Gift.

entries.title: Bear Island: The Xoanon of Dindyméné (pre-Hermetic artifact)
entries.summary: A Magic-realm effigy with three command-word powers, usable once per day each, that can be studied in a lab using the listed equivalent Hermetic Lab Totals.
quotes: Each of the xoanon's powers can be activated once per day.

related.text: ArM5 p.126 Clouds of Rain and Thunder

entries.title: Bear Island: Hunting Gegenees (faerie regeneration)
entries.summary: A slain Gegenes leaves its body and returns to its external-vis rock to craft a new body from glamor, so the supply of Gegenees to hunt is effectively unlimited and the corpse holds no vis.

entries.title: Bear Island: Waking or sleeping the titaness (Dindyméné ritual)
entries.summary: The dance and chant around the xoanon that wakes or puts to sleep the titaness, with an Ease Factor, bonuses for observing or including Daktyls, botch consequences, and a note on penetrating her Magic Resistance.
quotes: The player whose character is leading the dance must make a Faerie Lore + Communication + stress die against an Ease Factor of 18.
Faerie Lore + Communication + stress die vs. 18
Use the same formula if characters try to put Dindyméné to sleep, but increase the Ease Factor to 21.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.102 Daimons

entries.title: Bear Island: Covenant Boons and Hooks for the temenos
entries.requires: Location: Bear Island temenos used as a covenant site
entries.summary: Pre-built Boons and Hooks to apply during covenant creation if the Magic temenos is the covenant site, to be adjusted as events change the island.
quotes: Boons: Major Site: Regio (Magic regio), Minor Site: Seclusion, Minor External Relations: Ungoverned, Free Fortification: Island

related.text: ArM5 Covenant creation Boons and Hooks

entries.title: Bear Island: Founding a covenant (aura choices and patron spirit)
entries.summary: Compares the three Magic aura sites on Bear Island as covenant locations and notes that covenants in the Theban Tribunal must bind a patron spirit, which could be a Daktyl or the titaness.
quotes: In the Theban Tribunal, each covenant needs to bind a patron spirit.

entries.title: Spirit types: airy spirits, genii loci and daimons
entries.summary: Short definitions distinguishing airy spirits, the more powerful genii loci that embody a place, and daimons that act in the world only through replaceable aspects.
quotes: More powerful are the genii loci or spirits of place

entries.title: Cursewood: What is Known of Regulus (lore roll)
entries.summary: An Intelligence + Organization Lore: Order of Hermes roll to learn about Regulus, modified by training at his covenant or outside the Rhine Tribunal, with lists of what is known at each knowledge level.
quotes: players roll Intelligence + Organization Lore: Order of Hermes
Magi trained outside the Rhine Tribunal suffer a -3 modifier to the roll.

related.text: Mythic Locations: What the Magi Know

entries.title: Cursewood: What is Known about Pomerania (lore roll)
entries.summary: An Intelligence + Area Lore: Pomerania roll at the first mention of the Cursewood, with the knowledge levels it unlocks.
quotes: At the first mention of the Cursewood, players may make a roll of Intelligence + Area Lore: Pomerania.

related.text: Mythic Locations: What the Magi Know

entries.title: Cursewood: Forest Lore and communing with the forest spirit
entries.requires: Ability: Forest Lore (Guardians of the Forest)
entries.summary: A table of what a character with Forest Lore learns or can do in a foreign forest at each Ability score from 3 upward, from learning the spirit's name to being automatically judged worthy.
quotes: can try to commune with the forest spirit, but as this is a foreign place the character must have an Ability level of at least 3 to have any effect.
Character may find vis, although it is vis sordida.

related.text: Guardians of the Forest p.37 Forest Lore

entries.title: Cursewood: Trekking (stages, rolls and modifiers)
entries.summary: Procedure for crossing the Cursewood in five stages, each costing a Long Term Fatigue level, with a leader and guide, a terrain-dependent progress roll made with the guide's stats, and group-size and encumbrance modifiers.
quotes: The leader and guide can manage a group of people no larger than their combined Leadership scores; exceeding this causes additional hazards as shown later.
Each stage takes a number of hours to complete equal to the number of hazards suffered, although always at least one.
+1 per group member who knows the Ability used apart from the guide

entries.title: Cursewood: Trek Progress table
entries.summary: Converts the guide's progress roll into a number of hazards suffered in the stage, with extra hazards for oversized groups and a bonus or free stage for very high rolls.
quotes: Add one extra hazard for each person exceeding the maximum group size, defined as the combined Leadership scores of the leader and guide.

entries.title: Cursewood: Retreat and Defeat
entries.summary: A group that retreats suffers little harassment and needs no rolls, taking only an hour per stage, but the terrain resets so later visits are no easier.
quotes: they suffer minimal harassment on the way out, which takes only an hour per stage

entries.title: Cursewood: Rest, Sleep, and Supplies
entries.summary: Fatigue recovery in the woods: Long Term levels need a night's rest, Short Term recovery is slowed, hazards at night prevent recovery, supplies are spoiled and eating local plants or water wounds.
quotes: recovery times are doubled for Short Term Fatigue
ingesting any plants or water from the Cursewood immediately causes a Light Wound

entries.title: Cursewood: Hazards and Penetration
entries.summary: How hazards are chosen and when the spirit's effects must Penetrate, using Wyzwanie's Penetration with the regio bonus against characters weakened by the Infernal aura.
quotes: A hazard caused indirectly by Wyzwanie’s powers, like moving or reshaping terrain features, does not need to penetrate.
so gets a +7 bonus to Penetration

entries.title: Cursewood: Forest hazards
entries.summary: Sensory descriptions and example hazard events for forest stages, including corrupted trees, thorn walls and pitfalls with set damage.
quotes: A fall of 10 feet results in a +2 damage for mud, +5 for dirt, or +10 for rocks.

entries.title: Cursewood: Hill hazards
entries.summary: Example hazard events for hill stages, including loose-rock slides with Dexterity rolls and Ease Factors, hostile weather and exploding ground.
quotes: The Ease Factor is 6 to stay in place or 15 to move up the slope.

related.text: ArM5 p.125 Charge of the Angry Winds
ArM5 p.127 Talons of the Wind

entries.title: Cursewood: Swamp hazards
entries.summary: Example hazard events for swamp stages, including quicksand hands that lead to deprivation of air and churning waters needing a swim or boating roll, with botch consequences for progress.
quotes: Victims roll Strength + Swimming (or Profession: Boating) against an Ease Factor of 12 to reach the safety of the river banks.

related.text: ArM5 p.156 Hands of the Grasping Earth

entries.title: Cursewood: Malevolent Infernal aura effects
entries.summary: Lists the game effects of the aura of 5 in the Cursewood, a Malevolent Infernal aura: penalties to wound Recovery, added Damage, extra botch dice on physical activities and reopening of demon-caused wounds.
quotes: Wounds suffer a penalty to Recovery rolls equal to the aura rating of 5 while inside.
All physical activities suffer 5 additional botch dice from the aura; this includes all rolls for trek progress.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.12-14 Malevolent auras

entries.title: Cursewood: Using shortcuts and magic against the hazards
entries.summary: Guidance on how the spirit treats magical shortcuts and spellcasting: the regio can only be entered when led by the spirit, clever low-magnitude magic earns respect but invites a different hazard, and elemental specialists fare better though the hostile aura still risks fatigue and botches.
quotes: However the regio can only be entered by those led by Wyzwanie, and he only allows this once he is satisfied.

entries.title: Cursewood: The Regio (entry only when led by Wyzwanie)
entries.summary: The level 7 Magic regio containing Regulus' encampment, which may be entered only if the spirit allows it by letting the worthy cross the wall.
quotes: Regulus' encampment is now hidden in a Magic regio of level 7.

entries.title: Cursewood: Poisoned Sap (vis sordida extraction formula)
entries.summary: Once per year a magus may spend a season extracting Perdo vis sordida from the old oak, with the yield set by a formula using the Infernal aura and a risk of Twilight on a double botch.
quotes: collect pawns of Perdo vis sordida equal to (Aura + Intelligence + Infernal Lore + stress die)/5 rounding up.

entries.title: Cursewood: De-Corrupting the Vis
entries.summary: Tainted vis stays corrupted, but once the Magic aura dominates again, and after a year free of Infernal influence, newly produced vis is clean.
quotes: After a full year with no Infernal influence, all vis sources are free from corruption.

entries.title: Changing an aura (reducing Infernal, raising Magic)
entries.summary: How a corrupting Infernal aura fades once its focus is removed and the Magic aura dominates, and how a Magic aura can be raised with a yearly stress roll and bonuses from magical activities.
quotes: the Infernal aura drops by 1 after a number of years equal to its strength
A stress roll made once per year against an Ease Factor of 15 is needed for a permanent increase of 1.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.10-11

entries.title: Using vis sordida (tainted vis)
entries.summary: Risks and benefits of using Infernally tainted vis by non-Infernal users: a creeping Wrathful trait, bonuses to casting totals and study Source Quality, extra botch dice, and corrupted levels when preparing items for enchantment.
quotes: Modify casting total by +5 per pawn.
Add three extra botch dice per pawn used
+1 bonus to Source Quality per pawn for studying Hermetic Arts.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.18-19

entries.title: Dealing with Wyzwanie (research the artifact)
entries.summary: How the forest daimon bargains once the magi reach him, including a season of research against an Ease Factor to learn how to cleanse the Infernal artifact and the benefits of lasting friendship.
quotes: may roll Intelligence + Infernal or Dominion Lore versus an Ease Factor of 12 for a season of study with an appropriate selection of books.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests Nature Lore

entries.title: Cult of Wyzwanie (Walking the Path mystery)

+4 preservation of dead things from decay

crossing in any other manner requires a Regio Sight roll of 37

Realms of Power: the Divine p.63 Ascension

entries.title: The Fountain of Youth

entries.summary: A one-time-per-life fountain that removes Decrepitude or Warping, lowers Apparent Age, grants the Unaging Virtue, and also serves as an Insight source for the Limits of Aging or Warping.

It is only possible to benefit from the Fountain's power once in a lifetime.

entries.summary: Rules for statting human souls found in Purgatory and the Earthly Paradise, including their Might Score, capped Abilities, lack of Decrepitude and Warping, and what happens if a soul is retrieved.

entries.title: Pack hunt: the kill (trained group and trip attacks)
entries.summary: How an attacking pack fights: a trained group led by the pack leader, swapping group members with a Leadership roll, and trip maneuvers that leave a target with a reduced Defense.
quotes: making a roll of Communication + Leadership + stress die against an Ease Factor of 9
If the Attack Total exceeds the Defense Total by three or more, then the target is tripped

entries.title: The Wolf's Court aura and the She-Wolf's manifestation
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura of the Wolf's Court and describes how the She-Wolf forms a body, assesses petitioners without negotiation and speaks with her Voice of the Wolf power.
quotes: The Wolf's Court itself is situated in a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: Aspects of a Daimon (the She-Wolf)
entries.requires: Being type: Aspect of a Daimon
entries.summary: Explains how a spirit that creates a material body behaves: it can dismiss and recreate its body, the Daimon can send a new Aspect after a day, Acclimation applies, and spending Might on Virtues and Flaws erodes the Aspect. Also advises how to use such a spirit as a provider of vengeance rather than an antagonist.
quotes: If the Aspect is destroyed, the spirit can send another to the Wolf's Court after a day has passed.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.102 Daimon
Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Acclimation
Realms of Power: Magic p.46 Master of Animal Creatures

entries.title: How the She-Wolf grants revenge
entries.requires: Being type: Aspect of a Daimon
entries.summary: Describes how a spirit judges a petitioner's claim and then bestows Virtues or Flaws through its powers, either permanently (costing Might score as well as pool) or temporarily (Might not recovered while the effect lasts).
quotes: If permanent, the power is a ritual-like power and costs points from the creature's Might score as well as Might pool.
If temporary, the power lasts until the She-Wolf dismisses it, but the Might points spent on this power are not recovered while it is ongoing.

entries.title: Ritual of passing on the power
entries.summary: The optional ritual by which the She-Wolf endows a petitioner, which also gives the spirit an Arcane Connection and sympathetic connections to the recipient.
quotes: This ritual is not strictly necessary, but it provides an appropriate amount of mystery and formality to the seeking of vengeance.

entries.title: Spiritual Pact (Major Supernatural Virtue)
entries.summary: Extended rules for a character bound by pact to a Magic spirit: spending a Confidence Point to draw a temporary Might pool, how Penetration and duration work, the lack of a Might score, and how the spirit's own pool is reduced.
quotes: Make a Presence + Magic Lore + stress die roll: this is the amount of Magic Might Pool that the character acquires from his spiritual master.
A character can only have a single pact.

entries.title: The Wolf Brothers (Luperci cult overview)
entries.summary: Introduces the Luperci as a non-Hermetic Mystery Cult whose members use the Wolf's Court for Initiations, with the She-Wolf as magical patron; the storyguide chooses how widespread it is.
quotes: This priesthood still exists as a Mystery Cult

entries.title: The Luperci Mystery Cult: grades and Initiations
entries.summary: Describes the three grades of the Luperci cult, the Organization Lore: Luperci needed for each, the Virtues and Flaws gained at each Initiation and their Initiation Script bonuses and Ease Factors, and the lykaia rite for magistri.
quotes: The most junior grade is called the lupellis, which requires an Organization Lore: Luperci of at least 1.
(Initiation Script +9 for the Major Flaw; Ease Factor 15)
a character must have an Organization Lore: Luperci of 5 before being considered for this rank

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition Chapter Two
Realms of Power: Magic p.45 Lesser Power

entries.title: The Luperci as a Hermetic Mystery Cult (variant)
entries.requires: Optional variant: Hermetic version of the Luperci
entries.summary: Optional variant making the Luperci a Hermetic cult open only to magi, adjusting the crimes it avenges and the meaning of its Dark Secret, and noting that Gifted characters need not take an Ordeal at every Initiation.
quotes: Unlike unGifted characters, Gifted individuals do not have to take an Ordeal at every Initiation

entries.title: The Lupercalia curse-breaking rite
entries.summary: Yearly festival during which the senior Luperci present may attempt to dispel a curse on the community with a Communication roll against the curse's level, with bonuses for individuals brought to justice.
quotes: To evoke this power requires a Communication + Organization Lore: Luperci + stress die against an Ease Factor equal to the level of the spell that generated the curse (or 5 x the Supernatural Ability used to lay it).
it receives a bonus of +3 for every individual who has been brought to justice in the last year

groups.title: Dies Irae
groups.intro: Apocalypses: the end of time, Fimbulwinter, the Great Pestilence and Ragnarok.

entries.title: Daimons and Aspects
entries.summary: Explains how Magic Realm Daimons act in the world through Aspects: spirits with their own Might that serve as Arcane Connections to the Daimon, can be recreated when destroyed, and cannot be removed for good by Perdo Vim through an Aspect.
quotes: Creating an Aspect does not cost the Daimon any Might points, and it can have any number of Aspects active at any one time.
An Aspect has its own Might Score, although its Might pool does not replenish

related.text: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic p.102 Daimons

entries.title: Cosmology of the Spheres
entries.summary: Describes the nested celestial spheres, which of them (the elemental ones) Hermetic magic can affect, and why the lunar sphere and the ethereal spheres beyond it, made of unchanging aether, lie outside Hermetic Magic Theory until a breakthrough.
quotes: it cannot be affected by Hermetic magic

entries.title: Creo Aethera Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for creating aether at each density from intangible up to metal, with an extra magnitude for unusual or worked shapes.
quotes: Creating that aether in some unusual or worked shape is one magnitude higher than the listed values.

entries.title: Intellego Aethera Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for sensing aether, whether free or within other material, perceiving its unnatural properties, and speaking with aetheric spirits, creatures and plants; they are unaffected by aether density.
quotes: Intellego Aethera spells are not affected by the density of the aether.

entries.title: Muto Aethera Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for giving aether new properties and sensory species, changing its speed, and transmuting it into elemental, living or intangible Forms, with extra magnitudes for denser aether.
quotes: Add successive magnitudes for aether with densities of fire, air, water, earth, stone, and metal.

entries.title: Perdo Aethera Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for destroying a property of aether, a quantity of free aether, or aether contained in other material, with extra magnitudes for denser aether.
quotes: Perdo Aethera spells may be used to destroy an amount of aether.

entries.title: Rego Aethera Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for warding against aether, changing its density and moving it, with magnitude adjustments based on the highest density involved.
quotes: Magnitude adjustments are required based on the highest density.

entries.title: Criamon Player Characters in the End of Time
entries.requires: House Criamon player characters in the End of Time chapter
entries.summary: Guidance for involving Criamon player magi in the doomsday plot: how much they learn as their understanding grows, what tasks the House asks of them (vis tribute, research resources, helping Andreva, preparing the move to Megiddo), and how secret to keep it.
quotes: Those recently out of apprenticeship are considered young and unreliable

entries.title: Divine and Infernal Player Characters in the End of Time
entries.requires: Characters with Divine or Infernal patrons
entries.summary: Notes that characters with Divine or Infernal patrons may receive visions or premonitions about each event, which should point toward House Criamon, even though the potential end of time is not God's will.
quotes: Any Divine or Infernal visions or premonitions concerning story events should point the character squarely at House Criamon.

entries.title: Everything is a Lie: What Criamon Know of the Plan
entries.requires: House Criamon, Enigmatic Wisdom or House Criamon Lore
entries.summary: A table of how much a Criamon knows of the plot to end time according to their Enigmatic Wisdom or House Criamon Lore score, plus the note that once the breakthrough is made Criamon magi can be initiated into the new mysteries at Enigmatic Wisdom 7.
quotes: magi of House Criamon are offered initiation into the secret new mysteries of the House when they reach Enigmatic Wisdom level 7
The world will escape all time with the coming conjunction on December 23rd in the year 1277.

entries.title: Advancing the Antagonists (Aetheric Magic after the breakthrough)
entries.requires: Storyguide running the End of Time chapter
entries.summary: After the breakthrough the antagonist Andreva gains the Aetheric Magic Virtue and the Form of Aether, and the Virtue is then initiated out to Criamon magi and willing allies who gain the Form at a score of zero.
quotes: This grants the new Form of Aether but at a score of zero.

entries.title: Properties of the Axis Mundi
entries.requires: Being at an Axis Mundi (End of Time chapter)
entries.summary: Rules for an Axis Mundi, a place where the ethereal spheres touch the world: bonuses to totals relating to the cosmological spheres, mutual Arcane Connections between all known Axes Mundi, and absence from the Magic, Divine and Infernal realms.
quotes: Those within the Axis Mundi gain a bonus of +5 to any totals relating to the cosmological spheres.

entries.title: The Alien Aura (Lunar Aura Effects)
entries.requires: Lunar aura around fallen lunar material
entries.summary: A fallen star creates a Lunar aura that penalises casting totals, cannot be identified by Intellego Vim as any of the four known auras, stays when the object moves, and fades over a season once the Dominion reasserts itself.
quotes: This Lunar Aura is of strength 3 and imposes a –15 penalty on casting totals generated within it.

entries.title: The Fallen Star: Searing Light of Heaven
entries.requires: Encounter with the fallen star (End of Time chapter)
entries.summary: Statistics the blinding light of the fallen star as a Hermetic effect with no Penetration, with a Stamina stress roll to avoid blindness that magi can bolster with Ignem or Aether Form bonuses, and an explanation of the Spectacle Target.
quotes: Those affected must make a Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 to avoid blindness.
(Effect: Base 5, +2 Sun, +4 Spectacle; Modifications: +1 for 2/day, +3 triggered at sunrise/set)

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (Spectacle Target)

entries.title: Interrupting the Criamon Ritual
entries.requires: Storyguide running the End of Time chapter
entries.summary: Describes what happens if the characters violently interrupt House Criamon's great ritual: an immediate casting roll as if the ritual had finished, with a possible massive botch whose effects the storyguide decides.
quotes: although this is with 30 botch dice due to the magnitude of the ritual and the pawns of vis being used

entries.title: The End of All Moments
entries.summary: When the ritual completes, the spheres stop and all active Hermetic effects are canceled, as when crossing into the Magic Realm; spells relying on celestial-linked Durations fail again when recast, and the storyguide decides what time of day the region is stuck in.
quotes: all active effects are suddenly canceled

entries.title: Designing the Ritual: Hold the Sky in Thrall
entries.summary: Gives the two Aether effects needed for the ending ritual: a sight effect to perceive aether and a unique ritual to stop its motion, with level builds and the Required Lab Total for different numbers of seasons.
quotes: (Base 5, +3 Sight, +5 density, +20 size)
Required Lab Total: 4 seasons (182), 8 seasons (164), 12 seasons (158), 16 seasons (153), 20 seasons (152)

entries.title: The Falling of the World into Ruin (Moon Fragment Strikes)
entries.summary: A seasonal procedure for deciding when and how near moon fragments strike the player Tribunal, plus an Astronomy stress roll that lets a character foresee where the next strikes will land, with a penalty for each further season predicted.
quotes: Characters may make an Intelligence + Artes Liberales (Astronomy) Stress Roll.
