The target Ease Factor is 12 in order to determine which area will be affected in the next season.

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Sickness
entries.summary: Smoke and ash cause non-natural sickness, raising the frequency of choleric diseases and imposing a modifier on aging rolls, even within covenants, which may in turn affect covenfolk loyalty.
quotes: These conditions that promote sickness also impose a –2 aging roll modifier.

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Lunacy
entries.summary: Manifest aether drives people mad according to their dominant humor, with the afflicted gathering into roaming discordant pilgrimages.
quotes: those with a dominant sanguine humor become hysterical

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Famine
entries.summary: Food becomes scarce, imposing a cumulative annual living standards modifier that covenants can offset with magical resources for their covenfolk and protected areas.
quotes: Each year after the first, a cumulative –1 living standards modifier is imposed as food becomes more scarce and less nutritious.

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Loss of Rule
entries.summary: Each season a mundane leader makes a Leadership stress roll to hold authority, with failures increasing a Poor Leader reputation and botches signalling an imminent uprising.
quotes: must make a Communication or Presence + Leadership stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Apocalypse Condition: Aetheric Storms
entries.summary: Storms of aether sweep west across Europe, unbalancing humors and, at higher densities, causing damage per Diameter of exposure, with shelter giving protection.
quotes: Those caught in such storms suffer +8 damage each diameter that they are exposed.
Aetheric earth moves at 100 paces per round

entries.title: Creatures of Lunar Fire
entries.summary: Lunar-sphere creatures are built as ordinary Magical or mundane animals with the added Lunar Animal Quality.
quotes: All creatures from the lunar sphere and beyond possess the Lunar Animal Quality, reflecting their strange physiognomy.

related.text: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic (Magical Animals)
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (mundane animals)

entries.title: Lunar Poisoned Waters
entries.requires: Water contaminated by the lunar sphere
entries.summary: Rules for contaminated and aetheric lunar water, treated as a poison and as vitriol respectively, and how Perdo Aquam or Experimental Philosophy can purify it.
quotes: Treat such water as a poison causing a Light Wound with an Ease Factor of 9 to resist if ingested.
(stress die + 9 in this case)

related.text: ArM5 Art & Academe p.67 Experimental Philosophy

entries.title: New Animal Quality: Lunar
entries.summary: Defines the Lunar Animal Quality: invisible bodies that dissolve into aether, and attacks that sap the victim's highest Personality Trait which the creature can use like Ferocity.
quotes: For each point of wound penalty inflicted, the victim loses one point off their highest Personality Trait.

entries.title: Forests of the Dead (Lunar Plants)
entries.summary: How Lunar plants and their spores grow, hide and attack a host, with the Perception roll to notice a spore and the spore's attack, defense and Stealth bonuses.
quotes: This gives the seed +6 to attack, +9 to defense, and +9 to Stealth rolls.
characters make a Perception + (Awareness or Hunt) roll against the seed's Dexterity + Stealth (+9, as above)

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.33 faint traces

entries.title: The Lunar Infection (disease)
entries.summary: Disease statistics and symptoms for infection by a Lunar spore, which paralyses the body and gradually erodes the victim's most distinctive Personality Trait.
quotes: Severity 18 Stable 6, Improve 18, Interval: Week

related.text: ArM5 Art & Academe pp.45-51 disease rules

entries.title: Magic After the Apocalypse
entries.summary: Introduces the new Lunar Realm and explains that, with the spheres stopped, spells and device effects with Sun, Moon or Year Duration fail unless altered by Flexible Formulaic Magic or similar.
quotes: Spells and device effects relying on Sun, Moon, or Year Duration become obsolete and fail.

entries.title: The Lunar Aura
entries.summary: Lunar auras form wherever lunar material lies and scale with the amount of material; clearing material by the season weakens an aura but relocated material creates or strengthens another.
quotes: Each season's work spent clearing an area of Lunar material reduces the aura strength by one.

related.text: ArM5 Covenants p.49 Rego Craft Magic

entries.title: Impact on Hermetic Magic
entries.summary: Summarises three ways Hermetic magic is hampered after the apocalypse: the hostile Lunar realm, failing celestial Durations, and the loss of the Aegis of the Hearth and Parma Magica.
quotes: the Aegis of the Hearth ritual and even the Parma Magica, which are tied to the Year and Sun Durations, do not function

entries.title: Lunar Realm Interaction
entries.summary: Explains that the Lunar realm imposes large penalties on Earthly powers and that lunar creatures' effects count as Lunar Powers for realm interaction, referring to the replacement Realm Interaction Table.
quotes: any effects they use are considered a Lunar Power for the purposes of realm interaction

entries.title: Durations After the Apocalypse
entries.summary: Notes that Hermetic Durations tied to the heavens no longer work and points to a table of which Durations still function and which are unusable, with replacements researchable.
quotes: The nearby table shows which Durations still function correctly and those that are beyond use.

entries.title: Parma Magica and the Aegis of the Hearth After the Apocalypse
entries.summary: With the Sun and Year Durations disrupted, the Parma Magica and Aegis of the Hearth both fail until the Order researches new Durations and new versions of those rituals.
quotes: The Sun and Year Durations are both disrupted once the lunar sphere falls.

entries.title: New Lunar Durations
entries.summary: Replacement Durations that do not depend on the moving heavens (Burning of a Taper, At the Waking or the Sleeping, 300 Miles, The Weight of Years), each needing a Minor Breakthrough to formalize; improvising a non-standard Duration without the breakthrough raises its effective magnitude.
quotes: each requiring a Minor Breakthrough and around 30 Breakthrough Points (or 150 levels of experimental effects)
but the Duration is considered one magnitude greater than it would have been had it been formalized through research.

entries.title: Summary of Durations after the Apocalypse
entries.summary: A table showing which standard Durations still work (Momentary, Ring, Concentration) and which fail (Diameter, Sun, Moon, Year) after the heavens stop, with the alternative Duration for each; other traditions' Durations are judged against it.
quotes: Durations granted by mystery cults or other traditions should be judged against this list.

entries.title: New Realm Interaction Table (Lunar)
entries.requires: Lunar realm present in the saga
entries.summary: A replacement Realm Interaction table that adds a Lunar aura and Lunar power to the existing Magic, Divine, Faerie and Infernal columns and rows, giving the aura-based penalties and bonuses for each pairing.
quotes: + (1/2 aura)
- (3 x aura)

entries.title: Exotic Magic and Supernatural Beasts after the Apocalypse
entries.summary: Non-Hermetic traditions suffer the same Duration limits as Hermetic magi, but the powers of supernatural beasts are unaffected even when they reference a disabled Duration.
quotes: For the most part, the powers of supernatural beasts are unaffected by the Apocalypse.

entries.title: Infernal and Divine Powers after the Apocalypse
entries.summary: Infernal and Divine Powers keep working normally; only aura-interaction penalties apply to them.
quotes: Infernal and Divine Powers are unaffected by the Apocalypse, with the exception of any aura-interaction penalties.

entries.title: Initiation Script: Aetheric Magic
entries.summary: The initiation script for learning Aetheric Magic from House Criamon: a journey to Megiddo, paid tuition, a Criamon stigma that gives the Disfigured Flaw, and a vow to spread the knowledge.
quotes: Target Level: 21
Script Bonus: +13

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (initiation scripts)

entries.title: Regiones and the Supernatural Realms as Refuge
entries.summary: Magi can shelter from the apocalypse in deep regiones or by withdrawing into the Magic or Faerie Realms, where Hermetic magic works again, while the Divine and Infernal Realms offer no return.
quotes: Magi who withdraw to the Magic Realm find that their command over Hermetic magic returns to them

entries.title: Touching the Sky: Breakthrough Points for Aetheric Research
entries.summary: Summarises how breakthrough points are earned (experimenting on effects or studying a source of insight, one point per magnitude) and the point costs for breakthroughs such as Aetheric Magic, new Durations and new versions of the Parma Magica or Aegis of the Hearth.
quotes: each magnitude of effect contributes one breakthrough point toward the specific breakthrough
Each of the new Durations represents a Minor Breakthrough requiring 30 breakthrough points, while a New Parma Magica or Aegis of the Hearth would take 60 points.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.26

entries.title: Hermetic Breakthrough: Aetheric Magic
entries.summary: The 100-point Hermetic Breakthrough that creates the Form of Aether: research must come from projects tied to each Technique, and completion grants the Aetheric Magic Major Hermetic Virtue with Aether bought from the converted experience points.
quotes: a minimum of 20 points must be gained from projects associated with each of the Hermetic Techniques
the new Art of Aether at a starting score of 13 with a further nine experience points left over.

entries.title: Aetheric Magic Virtue and the Form of Aether
entries.summary: The Aetheric Magic Major Hermetic Virtue grants the Form of Aether, which combines with every Technique like any other Form, with the usual rules for rituals.
quotes: The Major Hermetic Virtue of Aetheric Magic grants knowledge of the new Hermetic Form of Aether.

entries.title: Aetheric Spells and Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Spells that create aether must still penetrate Magic Resistance, but magi lacking the Form of Aether get no Form bonus to Magic Resistance or soak against aether; aether suits offense poorly and few attack spells exist.
quotes: magi without knowledge of the Form of Aether do not receive any Form bonus either as part of their Magic Resistance or as a soak bonus to reduce any damage received.

entries.title: Sample Aetheric Magic Projects
entries.requires: Research towards the Aetheric Magic breakthrough
entries.summary: A set of example research effects, grouped by Technique, that count toward the Aetheric Magic breakthrough, with the number of further breakthrough points each Technique still needs once the examples are completed.
quotes: The examples below provide a total of 84 breakthrough points.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.26 experimentation

entries.title: Endurance of the Witch Moon (fallback Witch Moon rule)
entries.requires: Aetheric research project; Hedge Magic: Revised Edition optional
entries.summary: A research spell that forces a target to endure the Witch Moon, with a fallback procedure for troupes without the hedge magic rules: a fever, a month without the Gift, and a Stamina-based roll each month to end it, with failures adding Warping.
quotes: To End Witch Moon: Stamina – Warping Score + stress die vs Ease Factor 6

related.text: Hedge Magic: Revised Edition p.42 Witch Moon

entries.title: Arcane Knowledge: Aether Books and Lunar Lore
entries.requires: Access to the Criamon aetheric library
entries.summary: The aetheric library's tractatus and summae can each be studied as a source of insight toward the Form of Aether breakthrough, and the new Lunar Lore Ability has no books and no knowledge of the Lunar realm until after the first fall.
quotes: Each of these twelve volumes may be studied as a source of insight (as per the rules in Ancient Magic)

entries.title: The Form of Aether (Ae)
entries.summary: Describes the new Form of Aether: the base Individual by density of aether, the east-to-west motion and speed of aether at each density, the associated Magic Realm Province, and the Form bonus for soaking aether damage and resisting its influence on the humors.
quotes: Form Bonus: Soak against damage inflicted by aether, rolls to resist the influence of aether on the humors.
one pace per round for a density of metal, ten paces per round for stone, 100 paces for earth, 1,000 for water, 10,000 for fire, 100,000 for air, and 1,000,000 for intangible aether

related.text: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic p.24 Provinces

entries.title: Winter's Bite (Fimbulwinter exposure)
entries.summary: Sidebar describing how the Fimbulwinter grows harsher after a year or more of Aspects roaming, making Scotland and Scandinavia uninhabitable with Major Exposure hazard checks and driving migrations and travel difficulties.
quotes: Deprivation checks each hour, Ease Factor 9 or +3 frostbite damage

entries.title: Magically Created Food and Deprivation (Covenant Survival)
entries.summary: Covenants hiding from Fimbulwinter face attacks if the site is not concealed, and magically created food made without vis builds up a Deprivation debt of Long-Term Fatigue with escalating Stamina Ease Factors and a Living Conditions penalty.
quotes: Each successive month of magical food increases the Ease Factor by 9 with the loss of three Long-Term Fatigue levels.
anyone living in such an environment suffers a –2 Living Conditions modifier

entries.title: Penetrating Cold (Penetration of Created Weather)
entries.summary: Clarifies which weather and cold effects must Penetrate: magically created media or controlled substances must, while mundane items moved by magic and then released need not.
quotes: Magically created media or magically controlled substances must Penetrate, but mundane items that have been moved by magic and then released need not.

entries.title: Seasons of Conflict: Pacing the Fimbulwinter Saga
entries.summary: Guidance on pacing the saga: a rough number of stories per antagonist for each stage, scripted optional hooks that proceed without the players, and letting the Muspelli succeed in their goals when the players pursue other plots.
quotes: consider roughly two or three stories per Muspelli for each of the first two stages

entries.title: How did the Irminsul get There? (Irminsul Rules)
entries.summary: Explains where Irminsul survive, that they can be moved and work in any aura, that they are Arcane Connections to the Aspects of Fimbulwinter but not to each other, and how the Muspelli and magi can locate them.
quotes: Irminsul serve as Arcane Connections to the Aspects of Fimbulwinter, but not to each other.

entries.title: The Price of Ignorance (First Stage)
entries.summary: Consequences when the covenant ignores a Muspelli activity in the first stage: they gain an Arcane Connection and vis sample, materials for a talisman, and experience in Muspelli Lore.
quotes: The Muspelli gains 5xp in Muspelli Lore, increasing this score for later use.

entries.title: The End State (First Stage)
entries.summary: How the first stage should leave the covenant's knowledge of the Muspelli, and the experience the antagonists gain during seasons when they are not directly involved in stories.
quotes: For every two seasons where the Muspelli are not directly involved in stories, the storyguide should provide them with 15 experience points to increase their abilities.

entries.title: What is Insight? (Muspelli sources of Insight)
entries.requires: Original Research rules, or the storyguide's substitute
entries.summary: Explains that Insight comes from objects, texts or bodies that help a researcher towards a breakthrough, offers an experience-based substitute if those rules are not used, and notes that dead Muspelli stop being Arcane Connections to their patrons.
quotes: Once dead, Muspelli are no longer Arcane Connections to their Jotun patrons.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages (Original Research)

entries.title: When Do Other Muspelli Find Irminsul?
entries.summary: A shortcut for resolving the offstage searches of the other Muspelli from the result of the player characters' encounter with the one near their covenant, and for deciding when the third stage can begin.
quotes: then each other Muspelli has a 50% chance of securing his Irminsul.

entries.title: The Price of Ignorance (Second Stage)
entries.summary: If the covenant leaves the Muspelli alone, they find at least two Irminsul sites in the Tribunal and build further resources, a process expected to take around two years.
quotes: This stage should probably take at least two years, with one year dedicated to finding Irminsul, and a second spent creating resources.

entries.title: The End State (Second Stage)
entries.summary: What the covenant should know by the end of the second stage, the antagonists' experience gain during seasons off-screen, and how the Muspelli return to learn the summoning ritual and prepare to unleash the Aspects at a winter Solstice.
quotes: For every two seasons where the Muspelli are not directly involved in stories, the storyguide should provide them with 15 experience points to increase their abilities.

entries.title: Corrupting Auras (Trolldomur)
entries.summary: Muspelli can destroy Faerie auras and convert Magic auras to Trolldomur-aligned ones by performing utiseta against an Ease Factor tied to the aura's strength; Divine auras are immune and Infernal ones nearly so.
quotes: the Muspelli must enact utiseta with an Ease Factor equal to or greater than 5 times the Faerie Aura, or 10 times the Magic Aura

entries.title: Death Which Does Not Die (Muspelli Walking Dead)
entries.summary: How the Muspelli use animated corpses as tireless sentries and levies, noting that their usual Might means an Aegis of the Hearth keeps them out although the Parma gives no protection against their physical attacks, and that Walking Dead without Might exist only as part of an ongoing utiseta.
quotes: Commonly, they possess a Might of 9, and so most covenants' Aegis of the Hearth keeps them outside.

related.text: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic p.98 Walking Dead

entries.title: Summoning Aspects of Fimbulwinter (Utiseta)
entries.summary: The Muspelli release Aspects of the primal cold by performing a special utiseta at an Irminsul, using Intelligence and Muspelli Lore like the Jotun patron summoning, with extra modifiers from the Irminsul and the patron's elements. Gives the Ease Factor, typical Power Modifier and what happens when an Aspect is reduced to 0 Might.
quotes: with an Ease Factor of 50
The Irminsul used in the utiseta provides an additional Power Modifier of 1, cumulative with all the standard ones.
Reducing an Aspect to 0 Might doesn't destroy it, but forces it to return to the Magic Realm, where it could be summoned again.

related.text: Rival Magic p.9 and p.85 Muspelli Magic Defenses

entries.title: Researching Muspelli Magic as a Hermetic Breakthrough
entries.summary: Describes how magi can investigate Fimbulwinter and the Muspelli tradition, and notes that integrating utiseta-style casting into Hermetic Theory counts as a Hermetic Breakthrough giving an alternative for ceremonial casting.
quotes: This last option represents a Hermetic Breakthrough, representing the integration of the utiseta-style casting method as an alternative for ceremonial casting.

entries.title: Hunting the Muspelli: Arcane Connections to the Jotnar
entries.summary: Explains that the threat ends only when every Muspelli who knows the summoning ritual is dead, that the ritual can be passed on in a season of instruction, and how an Arcane Connection to a Jotun patron can be used against all its Muspelli.
quotes: a process which takes a season of instruction
Once dead, Muspelli are no longer Arcane Connections to their Jotun patron.

entries.title: Destroying Irminsul and Using Them as Arcane Connections
entries.summary: Destroying an Irminsul removes the Arcane Connection the Muspelli need for summoning Aspects, but the surviving Irminsul can also be used by magi as a lasting Arcane Connection to the currently summoned Aspect.
quotes: the Irminsul is considered an indefinite Arcane Connection

entries.title: Daimon of Fimbulwinter and Perdo Vim
entries.summary: Rules guidance on striking at the Daimon of Fimbulwinter in the Magic Realm: it is effectively immortal there and immune to Perdo Vim, while summoned Aspects can be destroyed but not eradicated.
quotes: It cannot be damaged by Perdo Vim effects the way other creatures with Might are vulnerable.

entries.title: Gandar and Utiseta (Storing and Casting Utiseta)
entries.summary: Explains how a Muspelli stores an utiseta effect in a gandur for quick use, the limits on storage time and on fixing the target at casting, and when the Casting Total and Penetration are rolled and what failure or botch does.
quotes: a gandur can only store an effect for one year
A failure on this roll means that nothing happens, and the energy gathered is safely dissipated

related.text: Rival Magic p.90 Penetration of utiseta
Rival Magic p.91 storing utiseta in a gandur and Warping

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines: Rego Herbam (Plant Disease Wards)
entries.summary: New Rego Herbam guidelines for wards that protect plants against mundane or realm-linked magical plant diseases, using a Touch, Ring, Circle format.
quotes: Ward a plant against mundane plant diseases.

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines: Creo Herbam (Healing Plants)
entries.summary: New Creo Herbam guidelines for healing plant wounds and curing plant diseases by severity, with a note that plant disease severity mirrors the disease in the eater and that non-Momentary healing is suspended like Creo Corpus healing.
quotes: Cure a Critical plant disease
Heal all damage to a plant, including wounds, disease, and poison.

entries.title: Tribunal Debate and Hellix's Trial
entries.summary: Covers the emergency Tribunal and offers a quick substitute for the Societates debate rules: opposed Communication + Code of Hermes stress rolls where each solicitor must win three points.
quotes: have the debating solicitors make opposed Communication + Code of Hermes stress rolls
Each solicitor has to make three points in the formal argument, and winning the roll equates to winning a point.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.90 debate rules

entries.title: New Spell Guidelines: Creo Animal (Animal Diseases)
entries.summary: New Creo Animal guidelines for curing animal diseases by severity, with a general base to stop any disease, and the same suspended-healing caveat as Creo Corpus healing.
quotes: Stop the progress of any disease. Cure any disease countering its effects.

entries.title: Geography of the Magic Realm (Boundaries, Vestiges, Twilight Void)
entries.summary: Short sidebar describing how the Magic Realm is organised into boundaries aligned to Forms, reached by vestiges or regiones, connected through the Twilight Void and its ten provinces to the Arcana Centrum.
quotes: The ten provinces converge at the Arcana Centrum, the center of the Magic Realm and the hub of all arcane power.

entries.title: The Great Pestilence: Overview and Order of Forms
entries.summary: Overview of the Great Pestilence creature's attack pattern: the order in which Forms are infected, what happens to vis, creatures and auras during each month, and how a ruined Form stops working for Hermetic spellcasting without vis.
quotes: The order of Forms attacked is Herbam, Corpus, Mentem, Vim, Aquam, Auram, Animal, Imaginem, Terram, and finally Ignem.
It takes four months to destroy a Form.

entries.title: Accidentally Creating the Great Pestilence in the Lab
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a player magus trigger the Great Pestilence by a botch or a 9 on the Extraordinary Results Chart while experimenting with Rego Herbam lab work, with a Disaster roll deciding whether a vestige forms.
quotes: the player must roll either a botch or a 9 on the Extraordinary Results Chart
if the roll is anything else (3 or higher) the vestige and the Great Pestilence are created

entries.title: Great Pestilence Penetration vs Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Explains how the Great Pestilence overcomes the Magic Resistance of Magic beings: its powers cost no Might, and its Penetration total is built from its Might and Penetration with bonuses for attacking from the Magic Realm and its current Form province.
quotes: its total Penetration is its Might (50) + its Penetration (10) = 60
for a Penetration total of 80

entries.title: Warning Signs: Premonitions and Visions
entries.summary: Characters with Premonitions or Visions get vague warnings of the coming Great Pestilence, with the accuracy of a Premonitions roll set by thresholds on the result.
quotes: A 6 or higher indicates something terrible is coming
a 15 or higher that a wizard created the malady that will destroy the world

entries.title: Rotting Vis: The Moon of Herbam Rot
entries.summary: First month of infection: all vis of the targeted Form rots, can be noticed by Awareness rolls, still works but makes casting that Form riskier, and can be saved only by moving it fully outside every Magic aura; infected auras stop producing that vis.
quotes: The average autocrat's Ease Factor is 9, while a lazy autocrat's Ease Factor is 12.
Herbam spell-casting requires a stress die in situations that normally use a simple die
It must be outside all Magic auras to retain its potency.

entries.title: Sickness of Magic Creatures: The Moon of Herbam Sickness
entries.summary: Second month of infection: Magic beings of the targeted Form inside Magic auras or regiones must pass weekly Disease Avoidance rolls or die, can be saved by leaving the aura (risking Acclimation), and their deaths weaken the aura and spoil their vis; familiars are affected too.
quotes: must succeed on a Disease Avoidance roll
add one-fourth of their Might to the area's Magic aura, measured in magnitudes

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Acclimation

entries.title: The Great (Form) Pestilence (Disease)
entries.summary: Disease statistics and symptoms for the Great Pestilence as it afflicts creatures, objects, minerals and plants of the attacked Form.
quotes: Critical Phlegmatic Disease, Severity 21 Stable: 12, Improve: 18, Interval: Day

entries.title: Miasmas: The Herbam Miasma Moon
entries.summary: Third month of infection: every Magic aura and regio spawns a drifting invisible miasma that blights things of the attacked Form, lasts a year, has no Might and Penetration Total 0, and penalises Aging rolls for each circulating cycle.
quotes: A miasma has a life span of 1 year.
each miasma penalizes Aging rolls by –2
impose a –2 penalty for every active cycle of Formtype miasmas circulating through Mythic Europe at that time

entries.title: Miasma Sizes (Targeting Spells at Miasmas)
entries.summary: Rules for sizing a miasma as about an acre per Auram Individual target, with each magnitude of added size covering ten times more area, and how larger covenant-sized miasmas need spells raised.
quotes: one target: Individual is a miasma the size of an acre of land
need to be increased by two magnitudes to affect the miasma

entries.title: Miasmas and Regiones
entries.summary: Magic regiones generate miasmas that are not blown away and are replaced by newer ones, while Divine, Faerie and Infernal regiones keep miasmas out and act as havens.
quotes: In regiones, and only in regiones, a new miasma will replace an older one.

entries.title: Detecting Miasmas and Aegis Protection
entries.summary: Shows how physicians deduce miasmas from bad air with Intelligence + Medicine, how Second Sight spots one, and that an Aegis of the Hearth keeps foreign miasmas out once the initial one is dealt with.
quotes: Spot a Miasma: Perception + Second Sight + stress die vs. 9
Success is indicated by succeeding on an Intelligence + Medicine roll against an Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: Handling Multiple Miasmas (Wind and Arrival Tables)
entries.summary: Procedure and wind-direction table for deciding whether, from where and how soon later miasmas reach a locale, using a stress die reduced by the number of Forms infected.
quotes: Roll a stress die (no botch) and subtract the number of Forms infected to determine the number of days before the next miasma visits an area.

entries.title: Form Ceases to Work: The Herbam Death Moon
entries.summary: Fourth month: formulaic and spontaneous spells of the destroyed Form only work if vis is spent, and lab work with that Form also costs extra vis.
quotes: one pawn per magnitude of the spell
it costs 1 pawn of vis for every two magnitudes (10 levels) of final effect

entries.title: Slowing the Rate of Infection (Optional Rule)
entries.summary: Optional rule to slow the pace of the Great Pestilence from four months to four seasons per Form for less powerful sagas, stretching the timeline to about ten years.
quotes: Rather than four months to destroy a Form, the Great Pestilence needs four seasons, Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

entries.title: Twilight Tears
entries.summary: After Hellix's accident, every Hermetic Temporary Twilight opens a temporary rent into the Form province the Great Pestilence is currently attacking, which can be seen with a Second Sight or Magical Sensitivity roll and used to enter the Magic Realm.
quotes: Viewing a Twilight Tear: Perception + Second Sight or Magical Sensitivity + stress die vs. 12

entries.title: Marking Time: New Moons and Seasons
entries.summary: Simplified calendar for placing new moons in the seasons over the four years of the Great Pestilence.
quotes: There are 12 new moons per year for the first two years of the Great Pestilence, 13 new moons in the third year, and 12 new moons in the final year.

entries.title: Effect of Destroyed Forms on Supernatural Abilities and Other Traditions
entries.summary: Describes how the rotting Magic Realm raises the difficulty of Magic-realm Supernatural Abilities for each destroyed Form and how to adapt other Magic-based traditions by mapping their divisions to Forms.
quotes: For every destroyed Form, increase the Ease Factor difficulty of every magical Supernatural Ability by 1.

entries.title: Corpus Infection (Corpus Pestilence and Miasma)
entries.summary: Second Form attacked: Corpus vis rots, Corpus beings sicken, and the Corpus miasma infects every human it touches with the lethal Great Corpus Pestilence, while magi and others with Magic Resistance are immune. Covers covenant and city responses, healing aid and the end of unaided Corpus casting.
quotes: Luckily magi, and all others with Magic Resistance, are immune to the
An Intelligence + Medicine roll against an Ease Factor of 6 indicates that relocating and outrunning the miasma are the better options.
This spell grants a sick person a +15 bonus to Recovery rolls.

entries.title: Mentem Infection (Mentem Blight)
entries.summary: Third Form attacked: Mentem miasmas strip people without Magic Resistance of their intellect, replacing Intelligence with Cunning, and the Aging roll penalty from earlier miasmas accumulates.
quotes: Aging rolls are penalized by a cumulative –4
Substitute Cunning for Intelligence to those affected.

entries.title: Vim Infection (Vim Blight)
entries.summary: Fourth Form attacked: Vim vis rots and can no longer be extracted from Magic auras, and Vim miasmas cancel spells and enchanted effects up to a stated level unless protected by the Parma Magica.
quotes: From this point onwards magi cannot extract vis from Magic auras
It cancels any spell or spell-like effect of level 30 or less.

entries.title: Divine, Infernal, and Faerie Vis (Tainted Vis Substitutes)
entries.summary: Optional rule letting magi replace dwindling Magic vis with Divine, Infernal or Faerie vis, which causes temporary Personality Traits with regular use, extra botch dice per pawn, and realm-flavoured botches.
quotes: Tainted vis adds extra botch dice, 1 per pawn of tainted vis
Abstaining from using tainted vis for six months removes the temporary Personality Trait.

entries.title: Aquam Infection (Aquam Blight and Rain Clouds)
entries.summary: Fifth Form attacked: Aquam miasmas poison and destroy water, small springs are lost for good while large rivers refill, and a covenant can get drinking water by pulling rain clouds to the ground.
quotes: Rain clouds lie 2,000 to 3,000 paces above, well within Range: Sight

entries.title: Auram Infection (Foul Air)
entries.summary: Sixth Form attacked: Auram miasmas foul the air so that breathers are weakened rather than killed, with a physical-activity penalty, Fatigue loss from exertion and a larger Aging roll penalty from the active miasmas.
quotes: Impose a –6 penalty to Aging rolls.
suffers a –3 penalty on all rolls involving physical activity

entries.title: Animal Infection (Animal Blight)
entries.summary: Seventh Form attacked: Animal miasmas inflict an Incapacitating Wound on every animal they touch, ending the milk and meat supply the survivors rely on, and Animal casting then needs vis.
quotes: This spell-like effect inflicts an Incapacitating Wound on an animal.

entries.title: Imaginem Infection (Imaginem Blight)
entries.summary: Eighth Form attacked: Imaginem miasmas stop objects producing visual images so anyone inside seems invisible and sight inside the cloud is lost, though magi still show an image. Describes the effect on sight and navigation.
quotes: things within a miasma are invisible until the miasma moves on

entries.title: Terram Infection (Terram Blight)
entries.summary: Ninth Form attacked: Terram miasmas strip the topsoil and drop structures into a pit, with simple-roll Ease Factors for collapse by structure size, descent rate of the miasma and a large cumulative Aging roll penalty.
quotes: Wooden buildings and small trees collapse on a simple roll against an Ease Factor of 3.
Aging rolls made this Winter are penalized by a cumulative –10 for 5 active types of miasmas

entries.title: Ignem Infection (Ignem Blight)
entries.summary: Final Form attacked: Ignem miasmas coat everything in frost, dealing damage each round to unprotected people and animals and killing small plants.
quotes: Unprotected men and women take +5 damage per round that they are inside an Ignem miasma.

entries.title: After the Great Pestilence (Postmortem)
entries.summary: Describes the end state after all ten Forms are consumed, including the lingering miasmas and the Living Condition modifier applied to the following Aging rolls.
quotes: The Living Condition penalty is modified by –6 for the next set of Aging rolls in the coming Winter.

entries.title: Bookkeeping the Great Pestilence
entries.summary: Advice on tracking only the nearby auras: record vis produced and resident magic beings, stop vis production once its Form is destroyed, and reduce an aura when a powerful resident creature dies.
quotes: the aura diminishes by 1 for every 4 magnitudes of the being's Might

entries.title: Protective Walls Against Miasmas
entries.summary: Compares the height of a miasma to real walls and towers to show why a barrier must be very tall and must include a portal to expel miasmas generated inside.
quotes: A miasma is approximately 60 paces high

entries.title: Seeing, Moving and Destroying Miasmas (Spell Design)
entries.summary: Design guidance for spells that view, move or destroy miasmas: an Intellego Vim base, a Form requisite that adds no magnitude, Rego Auram to move them and Perdo Auram with Vim and Form requisites to destroy them, treating a miasma as a severe weather phenomenon.
quotes: The Intellego Vim base level is 3.
A necessary condition of viewing a miasma, and affecting it with magic in general, is to include a Form-specific requisite.

entries.title: Changing the Order of Plagues (Optional Rule)
entries.summary: Optional variant letting the storyguide reorder the Forms attacked to spare civilization, while keeping Herbam first so the characters can link events to Hellix.
quotes: It is important that the first infection be Herbam, to give the characters a clue to Hellix's involvement.

entries.title: Deducing the Order of Forms Attacked
entries.summary: The Pestilence attacks Forms in the order of Hellix's Art strengths, which a researcher can infer from her lab notes with an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll, easier if she helps.
quotes: The observer must succeed with an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against an Ease Factor of 12.
adjust the Ease Factor of the Intelligence + Magic Theory roll to 6

entries.title: Healing Blighted Auras (Creo Vim Guideline)
entries.summary: Healing a blighted aura is a Creo Vim ritual with a requisite for the infected Form, using a base derived from the Creo Corpus disease-healing guideline; it repairs blighted vis but does not restore vis already destroyed.
quotes: Healing the aura is a Creo Vim spell, and needs to include a requisite for the infected Form being healed.

entries.title: Curing Diseased Magic Beings
entries.summary: Magic beings sick with the Great Pestilence can be cured with Creo magic of their body type or, through a spell keyed to their Form association, with a stated base level that must be cast as a ritual for permanent healing.
quotes: the base level of the spell is 25

entries.title: Researching a Way to Affect the Magic Realm (Breakthrough and Insight)
entries.summary: Research procedure for a Minor Breakthrough allowing spells that reach the Magic Realm: gain Insight Points from diseased vis and slain Magic creatures, invent Intellego Vim effects to earn Breakthrough Points, and accumulate enough to integrate the new magic, which then acts as an Arcane Connection.
quotes: To integrate spells that affect the Magic Realm the researcher needs 30 Breakthrough points
Each rotted pawn of vis provides 1 insight point, as does each magnitude of Might of a dead Magic creature.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.26-30 original research

entries.title: Cutting an Aura's Link to the Magic Realm
entries.summary: Once the Arcane Connection between an aura and the Magic Realm is found it can be destroyed like any Arcane Connection, protecting that site from the Pestilence; severing it removes the preternatural part of the aura, or halves it if the tether split is unknown.
quotes: simply reduce the strength of the aura to half its original strength when the connection is severed

entries.title: Inventing the Great Barrier (Ward Against the Great Pestilence)
entries.summary: Explains designing a general ward against the Great Pestilence once Magic Realm magic is integrated, with a Penetration Total that must exceed the creature's effective Magic Resistance.
quotes: The Great Pestilence has a Might of 50 and the Form province adds +10 to its Magic Resistance for a total of 60.

entries.title: Reaching the Arcana Centrum: Lore Rolls and Casting Bonuses
entries.summary: Gives the Magic Lore rolls for characters and creatures to have heard of the Arcana Centrum, the Reputation roll to recognise its author, and the casting-total bonuses of the Arcana Centrum and the matching Form province.
quotes: Intelligence + Magic Lore + simple die against an Ease Factor of 18
the Arcana Centrum adds +10 to spell casting and magic Supernatural Ability totals
A spell with the same Form cast within the province of that Form receives another +10 bonus.

entries.title: Entering the Magic Realm: Vestiges, Arcane Connections and Twilight Tears
entries.summary: Describes the ways into the Magic Realm: vestiges leading to boundaries, using an Arcane Connection during the short window when the Pestilence targets a Form, and stepping through a Twilight Tear opened by a magus entering Temporary Twilight.
quotes: At that exact moment, and for the next two minutes (20 combat rounds) the magi can target the Great Pestilence with spells.
Anyone can enter the Magic Realm if they do so at the same time as a magus enters Temporary Twilight.

entries.title: Boundary, Vestige and Twilight Void Travel
entries.requires: Ability: Magic Might, Second Sight or Magic Sensitivity
entries.summary: Travel roll to pass a vestige or boundary, a familiarity table, a Speed Level chart converting the result into elapsed mundane time, the Twilight Void Travel roll, and the rule that Magic Realm adventuring yields vis instead of experience.
quotes: Boundary and Vestige Travel: Stress die + Perception + appropriate Ability + Form bonus vs. ((10 – level of boundary or vestige) x 3) – Familiarity modifier
Twilight Void Travel: stress die + Stamina + Concentration + Form bonus
travelers do not gain experience points while adventuring inside the Realm

entries.title: New Spell Guideline: Perdo Vim (Destroying Raw Vis) and Leaving the Arcana Centrum
entries.summary: New general Perdo Vim guideline for destroying raw vis equal to the spell level, plus the rule that leaving the Arcana Centrum requires another Twilight Void Travel roll against the same Ease Factor.
quotes: Destroy an amount of raw vis equal to the level of the spell.

entries.title: After the Great Pestilence: Forms, Auras and Vis Recover
entries.summary: When the Pestilence ends the Forms work normally again without vis, miasmas fade within a year, and auras and regiones gradually resume vis production except those that dropped to zero.
quotes: As soon as the Great Pestilence dies, the ten Hermetic Forms start functioning again normally.

entries.title: Lunar Eclipses
entries.summary: Reference list of the dates of total lunar eclipses visible in Mythic Europe across the saga period, with a reminder that the storyguide may add or move eclipses.
quotes: Total lunar eclipses occur in October 1222, February 1226, September 1233, January 1237

entries.title: Playing Loki
entries.summary: Advice for a storyguide running a being far cleverer than the storyguide: invent obstacles retroactively to fill loopholes in his plans, but let a genuinely clever player plan succeed.
quotes: the storyguide is justified in inventing new obstacles for the players on the spur of the moment and playing them as if they had always been there

entries.title: Aspects of Loki
entries.summary: Limits on how Loki, a Daimon of kosmokrator rank, creates and uses Aspects: how many copies may exist, the loss of constant communication, regaining Might from vis, and the proximity restriction between Aspects.
quotes: Loki can only have a number of copies of the same Aspect active at any one time equal to the Intelligence Characteristic of that Aspect (with a minimum of one)
an Aspect of Loki cannot come within one mile of a place that another Aspect of Loki has been within the last 24 hours
5 points per pawn if the Form matches their Might, 2 points per pawn otherwise

entries.title: Gifts of the Gods
entries.summary: How an Aspect of Loki can loan one of its powers to another being as a mystical item: the Might cost, the item acting as an Arcane Connection, and what happens if the Aspect is destroyed or the original owner recovers the item.
quotes: The item is an Arcane Connection to the Aspect that created it (not to Loki himself), with a +3 Penetration modifier.

entries.title: Prophecies of the End Times
entries.summary: Rules for using prophetic texts as sources of lore: a character who can read the language but lacks the Ability may roll to find a specific fact, and each extra book on the subject helps at the cost of more research time.
quotes: It takes about an hour to find the information.
For every different book he has on the same subject, he adds +1 to the roll but requires an additional hour of research time.

entries.title: Letting the World Burn
entries.summary: Optional variant in which the player characters ally with Loki instead of opposing him, with storyguide characters taking the opposing role, plus advice on keeping characters from standing aside as bystanders.
quotes: Instead of opposing Loki, they could become his allies

entries.title: Five Acts to Destroy the World
entries.summary: Explains how Loki's success is judged: he must fulfil enough symbolic signs of the prophecy, not every one, so disrupting one plan does not end the threat and many minor successes can still bring about Ragnarok.
quotes: Loki might still be able to get Ragnarok started with a large number of minor successes rather than a few major successes.
Loki has to fulfill a certain number of signs

entries.title: The Magogoli
entries.summary: Shows how to build Magogoli troopers, generals and spirit summoners by adjusting existing character templates with Giant Blood, Magic Human and Gigantic features, and notes how a Nightwalking summoner without a Might score interacts with wards.
quotes: A common trooper is a grog character, although he also has the Giant Blood Virtue on top of his normal allotment.
it has no Magic Might and so cannot be affected by spells targeting a creature's Might

related.text: Realms of Power: the Infernal p.119
The Cradle and the Crescent pp.179-184

entries.title: The Eastern Bastion
entries.summary: Notes on how magic fares against a massed army (foot soldiers exceed the base Individual size, weakening Group-target spells) and a summary of Mongol-style Magogoli battle tactics.
quotes: The footsoldiers are outside the range of a base Individual of Corpus, which also reduces the effectiveness of Target: Group spells fivefold.

entries.title: The Monsters in the Ironwood
entries.summary: Describes the Ironwood regio: its single-level Magic aura aligned to a giant-derived tradition so only users of that magic gain the aura bonus, its hostile terrain, and the warped Hundings and Muspelli who live there.
quotes: The Ironwood has a single level with a Magic aura of 9.
This aura is aligned to trolldomur (Rival Magic page 92), which means that only those using giant-derived magic can benefit from the aura modifier.

entries.title: The Snatcher of the Moon
entries.summary: Worked example of a Muspelli utiseta ritual, setting out the Ease Factor, Range, Duration and Target components and the Power Modifiers a practitioner needs, and noting that separate Muspelli cannot combine powers.
quotes: Sjonhverfing Ease Factor 48
(Base 12, +9 Sight, +15 Decade, +12 Boundary)
would need Power Modifiers of x5 or x6

entries.title: The Army of the Faerie Gods
entries.summary: Gives a quick way to statistic the einherjar warriors from an existing template and changes how Muspelli Warping works once they are awakened, so that a failed Heipt Roll brings a group of them down on the Muspelli.
quotes: use the Berserker or Grizzled Veteran Template (ArM5 page 21) but also give him a Faerie Might of 5 (Corpus)

entries.title: Loki Succeeds
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Describes the course of the Second Titanomachy if Loki succeeds: all bindings fail for the duration, and ordinary people survive only by sheltering in Divine or Magic auras or within the Dominion, while those outside risk Warping.
quotes: The sympathetic magic of this event is so great that all bindings fail, all knots untie, and all locks open.
All Divine and Magic auras prove refuges against the war of the powers

entries.title: Wild Magic
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Lists the lasting rule changes from the flood of wild magic: Magic Lore becomes a General Ability, Magic auras strengthen, regio travel gets easier, many creatures and objects are warped, vis and The Gift become more common, and unGifted initiates and Folk Magic are affected.
quotes: Magic Lore becomes a General Ability rather than an Arcane Ability
All Magic auras of level 9 or less increase by one point.
reduce all Ease Factors for Regio Sight rolls for Magic regiones (ArM5 page 189)

entries.title: The Golden Chain
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: After the Titanomachy, Magic-aligned practitioners must connect to a being higher in the hierarchy of magic to fuel their powers. Describes the hierarchy, who keeps working, how a Gifted magus forms a pact with a patron (treated as an Initiation), and the cap the patron's Might places on Casting and Lab Totals.
quotes: The character's Casting Totals and Lab Totals cannot be higher than the Might of the creature with which one has made a pact
then the Target Ease Factor for the Initiation should be equal to two-thirds of the patron's Might
Only characters connected to this 'Golden Chain' can sequester the power necessary to fuel their spells.

related.text: Realms of Power: the Infernal p.124
Realms of Power: the Divine p.66

entries.title: New Virtue: Folk Magic
entries.summary: A new Minor Supernatural Virtue giving very minor spell-like magic in one narrow area, keyed to a Realm Lore. It explains the allowed categories of effect, the casting cost and preparation, and the halved Casting Total formula.
quotes: Your Casting Total is equal to (Stamina + (Realm) Lore + Aura modifier + stress die) / 2.
To cast a spell you must expend a fatigue level, whether the spell succeeds or fails.

entries.title: All Bonds Break
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Rule changes after the Titans are freed: summonings, wards and banishments no longer work on Magic creatures higher on the Golden Chain than their originator, Perdo and Rego cannot defeat their Might, and familiar bonds with Magic-Might creatures are broken.
quotes: all summonings, wards, and banishments no longer work against Magic creatures that are higher up the Golden Chain than the originator of the effect

entries.title: Impacts on Non-Hermetic Magicians
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Summarises how each non-Hermetic tradition fares once magic is regulated by the Golden Chain: which are already connected, which must find patrons, and which lose the ability to bind Magic and Faerie spirits.
quotes: Learned Magicians who Entreat the Magic Powers are already connected to the Golden Chain
Other wizards have to find a patron in the same way as Hermetic magi.

related.text: The Cradle and the Crescent Chapter 3

entries.title: Deicide
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Describes how Faerie power collapses: the greatest faeries are gone, surviving ones have much reduced Faerie Might, and faerie wizardry, charm-based magic and Folk Mysteries stop working.
quotes: the most powerful faeries still abroad in the world have a Faerie Might around 20

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.96-99

entries.title: No Faerie Auras
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Gives the conversion of existing Faerie auras into weaker Magic auras by level, the collapse of faerie regiones, and the guardians placed on the strongest former Faerie auras.
quotes: All Faerie auras of level 1 or 2 vanish entirely.
Those of level 3 to 5 become Magic auras of level 1.

entries.title: Vitality Is No Longer Enough
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Explains how surviving faeries sustain themselves after the Titanomachy through a formal, knowing yearly exchange with humans, and how those who fail lose Might and Virtues over time.
quotes: Faeries incapable of forging or sustaining a formal bond with humans cannot maintain their glamour and lose one point of Might every year.

entries.title: Realm Interaction Table
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: A revised table of how auras of one Realm modify the powers of another, reflecting the weakened Faerie Realm and strengthened Magic Realm.
quotes: The Realm Interaction Table has changed with the weakening of the Faerie Realm's influence on the world and the burgeoning power of the Magic Realm.

groups.title: Hooks
groups.intro: Rules from the stories of Hooks.

entries.title: Faerie Cognizance and Pretenses
entries.summary: Explains that faeries are Incognizant, Narrowly Cognizant or Cognizant depending on how freely they can step outside their story role, and that they have Pretenses in place of Abilities. Pretenses are used exactly like Abilities in play.
quotes: Faeries have Pretenses instead of Abilities.
In play, use Pretenses exactly as Abilities

entries.title: Raising a Faerie's Might (Increased Might)
entries.summary: Quick way to make faeries tougher for powerful magi by giving them the Increased Might Virtue, in its Major or Minor form.
quotes: The Major Faerie Virtue Increased Might increases a faerie's Might Score by 15.

entries.title: Faerie Aura Grown from Faerie Sovereignty of a Fief
entries.requires: Faerie ruler holding a mundane fief
entries.summary: When a faerie queen inherits a mundane fief, a Faerie aura appears across it and strengthens each spring equinox up to a cap, often overlapping existing Dominion or other auras. Includes notes on the fief's heralds and their limits against the Aegis of the Hearth.
quotes: every spring equinox the Faerie aura increases by 1, until it reaches a value of 4

entries.title: Faerie Court Regio
entries.summary: Describes a faerie court regio with a strong Faerie aura, how characters cross into it from the mundane forest, and its endless-looking but finite geography. Useful as a worked example of a faerie regio.
quotes: which is a regio with a Faerie aura of 4

entries.title: Finding a Moving Regio Entrance by Horoscope
entries.requires: A regio whose entrance shifts with sun and moon
entries.summary: A regio whose entrance is the darkest place in a forest moves with the seasons and the heavenly bodies. A character can work out where it will be by casting a horoscope, then needs to be able to see the way in; carrying light defeats the purpose, and an Arcane Connection spell can bypass the entrance.
quotes: Intelligence + Artes Liberales (astronomy) roll against an Ease Factor of 9

related.text: ArM5 p.158 Piercing the Faerie Veil

entries.title: Moving Through Sticky Webs
entries.summary: Webs fill a regio so that any movement, even flying, needs a successful roll. Stuck characters cannot attack or defend, and a botch in melee can leave a free character stuck.
quotes: moving around (including flying) requires a successful Strength + Stress Die roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: The Time Trap (Frozen Time in a Regio)
entries.requires: Regio in which time has been stopped
entries.summary: In a regio where time is frozen, long-Duration spells and effects do not expire, while Momentary spells work as usual. Destroying enough of the web that holds time releases it, aging everything inside and ending short-Duration effects.
quotes: any spells (and other effects) cast with a long Duration in the regio do not expire
everything in the regio ages by one year; make Aging rolls if required

entries.title: Researching Other Magi and the Order
entries.summary: How magi look up information about another magus: an Intelligence plus relevant Ability roll against a storyguide-set Ease Factor, modified by the reputation of the subject and the quality of the library or contacts consulted.
quotes: The researcher rolls Intelligence + Ability against an Ease Factor set by the storyguide

entries.title: Decoding the Clay Tablets and Searching for En-Dor
entries.requires: Possession of the Canaanite clay tablets (Ancient Magic)
entries.summary: Deciphering the tablets is a seasonal activity with a stress roll, after which they function as a Summa in Area Lore: Canaan whose Quality falls with each missing tablet. Searching for En-Dor in the field is a further seasonal roll, harder when done as off-site research.
quotes: Decoding is a seasonal activity requiring a stress roll of Intelligence + Hebrew against an Ease Factor of 18.
A complete sequence of six tablets is Level 10 Quality 15, with each missing tablet subtracting three from Quality.
A season's worth of search requires an Intelligence + Area Lore: Canaan roll against an Ease Factor of 18 for success.

entries.title: Copying Unintelligible Tablets
entries.requires: Possession of the Canaanite clay tablets (Ancient Magic)
entries.summary: Copying a text you cannot read risks errors, so copying either goes at half rate or costs Quality in the final translated text. Quick rubbings are fast but also cost Quality.
quotes: Careful copying is done at half the standard rate, while copying at normal speed means –3 Quality for the final, translated text.

entries.title: Canaanite Necromancy
entries.summary: Short account of what the ancient Canaanite necromancers could do beyond Hermetic limits, such as affecting the dead at any range and creating Arcane Connections to them easily, and why the Order fears their rediscovery.

entries.title: Converting a Dead Character to a Spectre
entries.summary: Defines a spectre as a ghost bound to its vocation and gives simple rules for turning a dead character into one: assign a Might by importance, keep Virtues, Flaws and Characteristics where they still apply, and keep only the Abilities of the vocation.
quotes: Might is assigned depending on importance and power, typically between 1 and 20.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic ch.5, pp.115-116

entries.title: Lore of the Dead (Supernatural Ability and Necromantic Rites)
entries.summary: Explains how a character with the Lore of the Dead Virtue casts necromantic rites, ceremonially in an hour or casually in a round, with the casting totals and Penetration formula, followed by four sample rites (Eyes of the Dead, Touch of Ghostly Calling, Dirge, Anchored in the Veil) with Ease Factors and vis costs.
quotes: Stamina + Lore of the Dead + Shape & Material bonus + stress die
Casual rites take only one round, but the casting total is halved unless a Fatigue level is spent.
Casting Total – Ease Factor + Penetration ability

entries.title: House Bjornaer: Harmonists, Wilderists, Clans and Septs
entries.summary: Background summary of House Bjornaer's two philosophical factions, its six clans and the role of septs, including clan Ilfetu's link to the Heartbeast initiation.

entries.title: Awakening a Genius Loci (Rossen-Antunnuac)
entries.requires: A dormant Genius Loci (Realms of Power: Magic)
entries.summary: A comatose Genius Loci bound to a site awakens through constant magical activity over it, starts weak, and grows over months to a high Magic Might. As it strengthens, the local Magic aura rises until it suppresses the Dominion aura outside the church.
quotes: it achieves Magic Might 40

entries.title: Initiation of the Simple Heartbeast (Bjornaer Mystery)
entries.requires: Initiation: Bjornaer mystagogue of Clan Ilfetu (Organization Lore: Bjornaer)
entries.summary: A Clan Ilfetu initiation script that awakens a heartbeast in a character who lacks the Gift, giving the Initiate the Flaw Magical Air. It gives the Ease Factor, script bonus, regio bonus and the witness-temperament participation modifier.
quotes: Ease Factor: 15 (Minor Virtue known to the Mystagogue)
The Initiate must not possess The Gift.

entries.title: Supply Shortage in Laboratories
entries.summary: Rules for a lab supply shortage that halves lab capacity: with core rules the number of active labs is cut, and with the Covenants lab rules the total Upkeep is halved by taking Flaws or removing Virtues. Labs shut down completely if the shortage lasts four seasons.
quotes: the shortage means that the number of active labs must be reduced to half (round down)

entries.title: Gathering Information in Town
entries.summary: Guidance for the roll to pick up facts and rumors in town: which Abilities and Characteristics fit each location, a baseline Ease Factor and modifiers for location, Ability used and tactful bribes.
quotes: An Ease Factor of 9 is sufficient, while modifiers between –3 and +3 apply

entries.title: Court Mechanics (Town Court and Guild Hearings)
entries.summary: Procedure for resolving a mundane trial or guild hearing: each side makes a Communication plus legal Ability roll with situation modifiers for the Gift, witnesses, reputation and actual innocence, and the court finds for the higher total. Sentence follows from the town charter or written law.
quotes: A roll of Communication + Civil and Canon Law or Artes Liberales (logic) versus an Ease Factor of 9 results in a credible statement.
The court finds in favor of the side which rolls higher.

entries.title: Demonic Possession of an Animal by Investing Might
entries.requires: Demon with the Possession power (Realms of Power: The Infernal)
entries.summary: A demon can possess an animal by investing Might in an independent, weaker copy of itself that shares its powers and statistics but has no body. The copy senses and controls the host, can use limited powers, and is exorcised by an Oblivion-type spell without harming the host or the original demon.
quotes: This means that an independent Infernal Might 1 copy of the demon resides within the cockerel.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.32

entries.title: Harvesting an Infernal Vis Source
entries.summary: Describes harvesting hellfire as a tainted Ignem vis source with a seasonal yield that the storyguide may adjust, with the reminder that Hell offers vis as a temptation.
quotes: Five pawns of Ignem vis can be harvested per season, and this vis is tainted with the infernal.

entries.title: Entering a Haunted Infernal Regio and Its Heat and Smoke
entries.requires: Infernal regio (Realms of Power: The Infernal)
entries.summary: An Infernal regio that opens at set times and can be crossed by those who can see into it. Characters who stay inside must make a Deprivation check each Diameter for heat and smoke, with a bonus for covering the face.
quotes: A character who wraps his face in a cloth receives a +3 bonus to the Deprivation roll.

entries.title: Hellfire Damage and Escaping a Burning Regio
entries.summary: Rules for passing through supernatural hellfire: damage per exposure, much larger damage for total immersion, a Soak bonus for magi from their Ignem Form, and ways to avoid immersion by flying, teleporting or wards. The fire is a natural feature of the regio so cannot be dispelled or blocked by Magic Resistance.
quotes: These terrifically hot black flames inflict +15 damage.
Any character running through the flames takes +60 damage (due to total immersion; ArM5, page 181).

entries.title: Quick Trial Resolution
entries.summary: A short rule for deciding a mundane trial in a single roll of Communication plus a legal Ability, with the Gift penalty already built into the Ease Factor, and the consequences of success or failure.
quotes: Communication + Civil and Canon Law roll versus an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Mechanica of Heron
entries.summary: Introduces the Mechanica of Heron as both a Major Supernatural Virtue and its Supernatural Ability, letting a character build magical wonders and sentient animae. Mechanicians can also make permanent enchantments without vis and build devices whose effects can later be changed within the same Technique and Form pairing.
quotes: Mechanica of Heron refers to both a Major Supernatural Virtue and its attendant Supernatural Ability.

entries.title: Animae as Enchanted Devices
entries.summary: Explains how to treat animae in play: they are enchanted devices, so they hold no vis and are immune to Might-stripping but not to Disenchant, their Might acts as Magic Resistance, and their powers follow magic-item rules for uses per day and Penetration. Hostile auras lower their Magic Resistance and Penetration but do not stop them affecting themselves or ordinary people.
quotes: The primary function of their Might Score is to provide them with Magic Resistance.
The powers of animae work like those of Hermetic magic items in terms of uses per day and Penetration.

entries.title: Damage Levels and Repair of Animae
entries.summary: Animae track damage as object-style Damage Levels instead of Wound Penalties. Damage past Soak forces a Stamina roll to avoid losing a level, they do not heal naturally, and craftsmen with the right Ability can repair levels each season.
quotes: Whenever an anima suffers damage exceeding its Soak, it must make a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor equal to the amount by which the damage exceeded the Soak.
Maahes and Ailuros each have 5 Damage Levels.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.128

entries.title: Identifying a Magus by Sigil
entries.summary: Once a caster's sigil has been detected in spell traces, an investigator familiar with that Tribunal's magi can recognise whose it is with an Intelligence plus Organization Lore roll, which is harder for an unfamiliar investigator.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Organization Lore: Order of Hermes roll against an Ease Factor of 9 (or 15 if the investigator is unfamiliar with Rhine magi)

entries.title: Detecting Spell Traces
entries.summary: When a spell's Duration ends it leaves traces whose strength fades over time at rates depending on the original Duration. Investigators can detect them with Intellego Vim effects whose level scales with the trace strength, and extra magnitudes reveal the Form, Technique and even the caster's sigil.
quotes: When a spell's Duration expires it leaves behind spell traces equal to half the magnitude of the original spell.
Traces down to magnitude zero can be detected by a base InVi 10 effect.

entries.title: Tribunal Politics and Trial Procedure Decisions
entries.summary: A checklist of decisions a troupe should make about how its Tribunal handles a prosecution: when and how a case is brought, what evidence is allowed, how truthfulness is judged, and whether magi vote by favor, by character of the accused or by the facts.

entries.title: Guardians of the Forests (Rhine Peripheral Code Ruling)
entries.summary: Describes a Rhine Tribunal ruling letting a recognized guardian of a forest do otherwise forbidden things in its defense, how guardian status becomes official only if the Tribunal accepts the claim, and why it does not apply outside the Rhine.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p.18

entries.title: Nature Lore Supernatural Abilities
entries.requires: Supernatural Ability: Nature Lore / Forest Lore
entries.summary: Nature Lore Supernatural Abilities let a character interact specially with a natural feature such as a forest or river. A river version lets its holder find regiones and vis, speak with supernatural inhabitants and commune with the river spirit without Hermetic magic.
quotes: This allows him to find regiones and vis within the Danube, speak with supernatural river inhabitants, and commune with the river spirit, all without the use of Hermetic magic.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.103

entries.title: Trained Group and Mounted Bonuses for a Knightly Band
entries.summary: Shows how a band of companions fights as a trained group, the vanguard gaining a combat bonus from the others, and that mounted combatants add a bonus to Attack and Defense.
quotes: each receive a +3 bonus to their Attack and Defense Totals

entries.title: Protections Against Magic for Mundane Characters
entries.summary: Ways a mundane character can be shielded from magic: a relic giving Magic Resistance, a Guardian Angel, or effective folk charms. Five sample charms each give a roll, Ease Factor or bonus against a specific kind of ongoing magical effect.
quotes: Sir Erwan may have a Guardian Angel (which gives him a magic resistance of 15
gives Sir Erwan a +3 Soak bonus against magic sources of damage

entries.title: Greater Malediction of Hereditary Madness (Personality Flaws on Aging)
entries.summary: A hereditary curse that adds a Minor Personality Flaw each time the cursed character's Decrepitude increases, chosen on a table by a die plus Decrepitude. A repeated Flaw becomes Major, with no further effect once already Major.
quotes: The curse means that every time Sir Erwan's Decrepitude Score increases he gains a Minor Personality Flaw, in addition to any other aging effects
To determine the Personality Flaw roll a simple die + Decrepitude Score and compare to the list that follows.

gated.title: Transforming Mythic Europe
gated.intro: The Fourth Estate and the Island of the Magicians.

entries.title: Construction: Earth Jacketed In Stone
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Introduces the method of building an artificial island by casting Creo Terram rituals that make a thick stone wall jacketing an infill of earth.

entries.title: Outer Wall Shapes
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Describes the default design of the island's sea wall, how changing its height changes its diameter, and how a few extra spell levels greatly increase its area.
quotes: an extra 5 spell levels increases the area incredibly

entries.title: Open Ended Cylinder
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Gives the spell levels needed to create an open-ended cylindrical wall of a given diameter, and recommends treating a conical frustum as a cylinder for calculation.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates a wall 30 paces high, 2 paces thick, and just over 3 miles in diameter.

entries.title: Tall Empty Cylinder
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Gives the spell levels for a much taller cylindrical wall suited to deeper water, with correspondingly smaller diameters.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates a wall 240 paces high, two paces thick, and just over a third of a mile in diameter.

entries.title: Simple Spells to Create Permanent Walls
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: A set of ritual spells that create permanent stone walls of increasing volume, showing how size magnitudes scale and noting that rituals below a certain volume gain no advantage.
quotes: which is a total of 100 cubic paces of stone
Due to the quirk of Hermetic magic that makes all Rituals fourth magnitude spells or greater

entries.title: Open Ended Rectangular Prism
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Gives the spell levels for walls forming a rectangular island, noting that it suffers more erosion than a cylinder and that a pyramidal frustum is a better shape.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates sufficient stone to make walls 30 paces high, 2 paces wide, and a top square with 4,166 paces (2.4 miles) per side.

entries.title: Solid Stone Cylinder
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Gives the spell levels for a single monolithic stone cylinder that can be quarried into to create rooms.
quotes: A level 30 spell creates a stone cylinder 30 paces high and 206 paces in diameter.

entries.title: Ablative Slope
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Explains how a slope of mud or sand at the base of the wall protects it from wave erosion and how its spell level compares with the wall's.
quotes: the spell to create an ablative slope is three magnitudes lower than the spell that creates the wall

entries.title: Ornamentation
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Wall features can be added by raising the spell level of the initial spell, or retrofitted afterwards with Rego Terram or mundane craftsmen.

entries.title: Maximum Magnitudes Due to Complexity
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Suggests the troupe cap the magnitudes added by complex features, after which the magus can shape his creation freely.
quotes: after adding three magnitudes for complexity, the magus can manipulate his creation into any shape he wishes, without adding extra magnitudes

entries.title: Fortified Wall
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Lists fortress features for the sea wall and whether each adds a magnitude to the spell or merely uses stone: crenellations, fire step, height, machicolations and hoardings.
quotes: Adding crenellations adds a magnitude.

entries.title: Sea Gates and Docks
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: A sea gate and internal harbor wall add a single magnitude to the wall spell, with extra material needed for the harbor.
quotes: it adds 1 magnitude because it has some metal parts, but requires no added material

entries.title: Statuary
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Statues or reliefs on the wall cost nothing if they express the caster's sigil, otherwise they add a magnitude.
quotes: If they are an artistic motif, they add a magnitude.

entries.title: Base Metal Walls
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Walls of copper, bronze, brass or iron alloys cost extra magnitudes to create compared with stone, and the section gives example wall sizes by spell level.
quotes: The base spell level is two magnitudes higher, while the base Individual of is 1/27th the volume.

entries.title: Noble Metal Walls
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Walls of silver or gold are possible with very high-level spells but are much more difficult than base metals and attract invaders.
quotes: Walls made of valuable metals are three magnitudes more difficult to create than walls of base metals of equivalent size.

entries.title: Unnatural Stones
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Adding a Muto requisite lets the wall have unnatural properties, with further requisites needed for effects such as burning or self-healing.
quotes: By adding a Muto requisite to the ritual used to create the wall, magi can create stone with unnatural properties.

entries.title: Biological Substances
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Walls of wood or bone are equally difficult to produce by volume, but vulnerable to predators and faerie influence, and human bone is as hard as base metal.
quotes: When calculating volumes, stone, animal bone, and wood are equally difficult to produce.

entries.title: Dirt, With a Layer of Topsoil
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Gives the soil volumes needed to fill islands of various sizes and the Creo Terram ritual levels that provide that volume.
quotes: A level 35 spell provides up to 10 billion cubic paces of soil.

entries.title: A Basic Quote (Island Cost)
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Worked example of the spells, vis and time needed to create a circular island of a given size with a standard wall and soil fill.
quotes: that requires just two spells, a level 35 and a level 40, and 15 pawns of vis

entries.title: Clay Fill
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Clay fill is as easy to create as soil and is waterproof, so the soil calculations can be used for a topsoil-over-clay fill.
quotes: Clay is as easy to create as soil.

entries.title: Stone Fill
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Stone fill is harder to create than soil, and choosing a variety of stones adds a magnitude for complexity.
quotes: Stone is three magnitudes more difficult to create than soil of the same volume.

entries.title: Rooms and Utility Spaces
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Excavated or created underground rooms need extra magnitudes for elaborate design, using Conjuring the Mystic Tower as a reference.
quotes: adds 3 magnitudes for elaborate design

entries.title: Road Works
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Explains why paved roads are the only worthwhile road to create magically and gives a ritual that makes road networks of a stated maximum length, with extra magnitudes for complex designs.
quotes: the maximum length for this spell, which is 3.78 miles

entries.title: Creating Houses and Other Buildings
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Ways of making housing on the island, including shell keeps and rituals that raise many identical cottages, with each added magnitude multiplying the number produced by ten.
quotes: Every magnitude added to the spell multiplies the number of cottages produced by ten.

entries.title: Water Works
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Covers cisterns, canals and aqueducts on the island, with rituals that create stone-lined canals for local use and for seagoing vessels, scaled by spell level.
quotes: A single horse can draw 30 tons of cargo on a barge

entries.title: Creating Fields and Forests
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Herbam rituals that create forests, acorns or grassland, where each added magnitude multiplies the quantity created by ten.
quotes: Each added magnitude multiples this number of trees by 10.

entries.title: How Many Peasants Are Needed?
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Gives manor size, income and peasant families per manor to estimate how many manors an island of a given size can support.
quotes: A typical manor, for a landed knight, is 600 acres.
This provides 20 Mythic Pounds of income, before expenses, each year.

entries.title: Story Seeds for the Residue of Great Magic (Moving an Aura)
entries.requires: Saga arc: Island of the Magicians
entries.summary: Moving a site of great works usually leaves its aura behind, because the spirit of place is tied to the location; overcoming this needs a Rego Vim effect or requisite, usually a ritual opposed by the Spirit of Place.
quotes: the aura is usually left behind

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.106 Genius Loci

entries.title: Sea Depths of the North Sea
entries.requires: Saga: raising a magical island from the sea
entries.summary: Average depths of the parts of the North Sea, plus the extra height allowed for storm waves and freak waves, used to work out how high a raised wall must be.
quotes: The Dogger Bank is the shallowest part of the North Sea, between 17 and 33 paces deep.

entries.title: A Note on The Powers of Demons
entries.summary: Describes three common demonic powers: Coagulation (building a solid body), Envisioning (invading dreams) and Obsession (imposing a temporary Personality trait that may become permanent).
quotes: Manifesting takes (Might) rounds, but dissolving again requires only one round of concentration.
This gives the person a temporary Personality trait equal to the number of points spent

entries.title: Demon Weaknesses
entries.summary: Each demon has a Weakness that characters can learn with a lore roll; a weakness that is a material forces the demon to flee and stops it regaining Might, while a protected group cannot be harmed by it.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Infernal Lore roll against an Ease factor of 9 + (Might / 5)

entries.title: Tainted Vis (Simplified)
entries.summary: A simple fallback for troupes not using the full Infernal rules: tainted vis gives a larger casting bonus, adds botch dice for users not aligned with the Infernal, and slowly implants a sinful Personality trait in whoever carries it.
quotes: Adds 5 instead of 2 to casting totals.
Adds three botch dice per pawn, for non-Infernally aligned users.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.18-19

entries.title: Wall Ring Size in the Atlantic
entries.requires: Saga: raising a magical island from the sea
entries.summary: Because the ocean is very deep, the diameter of the stone ring a spell can raise depends sharply on its level; the section lists the ring size produced by each higher spell level in the Atlantic.
quotes: A level 45 spell creates a ring 22 miles in diameter.
A level 40 spell creates a ring just over two miles in diameter.

entries.title: Wall Ring Size in the Baltic Sea
entries.requires: Saga: raising a magical island from the sea
entries.summary: Gives the ring size produced by the wall spell at two levels in the shallow Baltic, and notes that the larger one is too big for the sea.
quotes: The Baltic Sea averages 60 paces in depth, which means:
it creates a ring 150 miles across

entries.title: Wall Ring Size in the Black Sea
entries.requires: Saga: raising a magical island from the sea
entries.summary: Gives the ring size produced by the wall spell at three levels in the deep Black Sea.
quotes: A spell of level 40 gives a ring 11200 paces (6.36 miles) wide.
This sea averages 1420 paces deep

entries.title: Wall Ring Size in the Mediterranean
entries.requires: Saga: raising a magical island from the sea
entries.summary: The Mediterranean is deeper than the North Sea, so the same wall spell yields a much smaller ring; the section gives the depth and the resulting diameter.
quotes: On average, the Mediterranean is 1630 paces deep

entries.title: A Floating Island
entries.requires: Saga: raising a magical island from the sea
entries.summary: A mobile island is made by shaping the wall as a circular cap of pumice; the section lists the size of cap produced at each spell level and the ways it can be steered.
quotes: A level 35 spell creates a circular cap around 2500 paces (1.4 miles) across.
